The lead sponsor is now listed as Seattle Project Corporation, but the record was last verified in May 2025.Gritstone filed for Chapter 11 in October 2024 and sold its assets (vaccine brief). The brief’s “no clear sponsor” does not reflect this listing, but the listing is itself about 17 months old.INTerpath program (intismeran)None of its nine trials is in GI cancer (vector memory 22080f32, checked 2026-08-29).For her, melanoma only (see Fit). The INTerpath-001 registry number is not recorded in Maple.Expanded access—Made per patient, and only inside protocols (vaccine brief).
Contraindications, interactions and open questions

Which cancer? For her melanoma, the open question is its stage; the brief recommends
pulling the dermatopathology report. Even at stage IIB or higher, adjuvant melanoma trials
generally exclude a patient with another active cancer (brief).
Her neoantigen count can be measured from data already on disk
(#257). That would turn “would she qualify?”
from a guess into a fact.

What would reopen it

A neoantigen trial opens for GI or colorectal cancer, in INTerpath or elsewhere.
Her melanoma turns out to be stage IIB or higher, or recurs.
A low-burden colorectal recurrence, the only setting in which GRANITE showed a signal.
A measured neoantigen count well above 5 (#257).

Next step
Record the melanoma’s AJCC stage once its report is parsed
(#213). Otherwise, re-read the registry entries
above at each review.

Bacterial oncolytics





















StatusparkedAdded2026-10-01Last reviewed2026-10-01
Tracked, not actionable. Both programs come from the Miyako lab at JAIST in Japan, and
neither has reached a human. The full assessments are in the notes of their
mods_intervention rows:

AUN: 93038d1e-4fcb-4dca-9683-b193effaddac
Ewingella americana: 7343900e-6f1c-415d-a898-50c6abacead0

What it is and how it works



































AUN consortiumEwingella americanaWhatTwo bacteria at a fixed 3:97 ratio, not engineered: Proteus mirabilis (“A-gyo”) and Rhodopseudomonas palustris (“UN-gyo”)One bacterium from a Japanese tree frog’s gut, not engineeredRoute in miceIVIV, single doseMechanismSelective clotting in the tumor’s vessels, then vascular collapse and necrosis, plus direct oncolysis. Independent of the immune system: complete remissions in both immunocompetent and immunocompromised mice.Colonizes the hypoxic tumor core, about 3,000-fold in 24 hours, and kills directly. Also activates neutrophil, T-cell and B-cell immunity, with memory on rechallenge.PaperIwata et al., Nature Biomedical Engineering 2026;10(2):293–308, PMID 40764397Iwata et al., Gut Microbes 2025;17(1):2599562, PMID 41376334DevelopmentDaiichi Sankyo scientists are co-authors; patent WO2023223869A1; first-in-human aimed at about 6 years (the team’s own estimate)No IND, sponsor, company or patent; 8–12+ years, if ever
Why she is interested
A short video about the frog-gut result was forwarded in late August 2026. The sender is not
recorded (MapleLog 2026-08-29). Whether Maureen herself is interested is not recorded.
Fit to her disease





















Her fact (source)RelevanceMSS, TMB 2–3: an immunologically cold tumor (§2.4)Neither mechanism depends on mutation burden or T-cell infiltration. That is the reason to track them (intervention notes).Nodal-predominant recurrence, now NED (§2.3, §2.5)Both need a substantial tumor, with a hypoxic core or established vessels. Inference: they do not suit low-volume or NED disease (intervention notes).Recent chemotherapy and surgery (§2.2)E. americana is a documented opportunistic human pathogen, and it preferentially infects exactly that group (intervention notes).
Evidence
Level: preclinical, in mice, for both. AUN was also tested on human-tumor xenografts.
The relevant human precedents come from vector memory 906b98fe:

The IV route has failed before. Salmonella VNP20009
(NCT00004216, COMPLETED; ClinicalTrials.gov,
2026-10-01) reached the tumor in 2 of 24 patients and gave no benefit. Cytokine toxicity
prevented a higher dose.
Injection into the tumor has worked. Clostridium novyi-NT shrank the injected lesion
in 9 of 22 evaluable patients (Janku et al., Clin Cancer Res 2021).

Who would give it, and access path
None. Without an IND there is no trial and no compassionate-use route.
Contraindications, interactions and open questions

Pathogen risk. E. americana is a documented human pathogen. P. mirabilis is a
common one too, and AUN’s safety case rests on the 3:97 ratio holding in a human host.
Where it would fail. In humans, the step most likely to fail is colonizing the tumor
after IV dosing, not killing tumor cells.

What would move it
These triggers are from the intervention notes:

a startup is formed or financed around either program;
Daiichi Sankyo takes an option on AUN or licenses it;
an IND is filed, or a phase 1 is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov or jRCT;
large-animal data on colonization or safety appear;
E. americana’s colonization is replicated independently, in any species.

Next step
None while parked. Check the triggers at each review.

Schema notes for #565
Written 2026-10-01 from the eight entries above. (2026-10-05: the ledger’s schema was since
decided as D-Q4-05, and its v0 has merged, seeded from the eight entries above; these notes were
an input to it.) The aim is to derive the schema from what
the entries needed, not to fit them to a design. The draft compared against has six tables:
mods_option, mods_option_event, mods_claim, mods_party, mods_meeting and
mods_trial. It also has fixed vocabularies for an option’s status, horizon, kind, safety
against her regimen and access path, and for a claim’s verification state.
How the entries fill the draft’s option fields






















































































Entrystatushorizonkindevidence_levelsafety_vs_regimenaccess_pathDendritic cell therapyresearchingprevent_while_ned (inferred)cell_therapy, but a product familyinvestigational, phase 1/2unknownabroad + self_pay; trial (none found)BOT/BALdiscussed with clinicianprepare_for_recurrencecombination, reached through trialsphase 1b/2no value fits: it would replace maintenance (14-day washout)trial ×8 + expanded_access abroad (France)Disulfiram ± copperdiscussed with clinicianprevent_while_neddrug, or a combination with copperapproved (other indication); preclinical (CRC)cautionoff_label_rx; otc (copper)Live-tissue drug testingresearchingprepare_for_recurrenceno value fits (a functional test)concordance studies: test validity, not efficacyunknown (washout unverified)self_pay, physician-orderedMore sensitive ctDNA assaydiscussed with clinicianserves all threemonitoring_testnot compilednone_knownself_pay, physician-orderedMebendazoleresearchingnot recordeddrugnot compiledunknownnot recordedNeoantigen vaccinesparkedprepare_for_recurrence, and partly for her melanomavaccine, a class of four programsphase 3 positive (melanoma); phase 2 negative (CRC)n/atrial (all closed)Bacterial oncolyticsparkedno value fits (watch only)no value fits (live bacteria); two productspreclinicaln/anone
Where the entries confirm the draft

A table of its own, not a status on ModsIntervention. Five of the eight are not one
intervention row: a product family, a two-product pair, a four-program class and two
tests. Only two of the eight entries have mods_intervention rows at all: three rows, for
BOT/BAL, AUN and E. americana. One of those rows is already wrong: AUN’s category is
immunotherapy, though its own notes say the mechanism is “explicitly NOT
immune-mediated”. So keep mods_option, with an optional link to mods_intervention, and
do not inherit its category.
mods_claim with all four verification states. All four were needed on the first
pass:

verified: 13 registry records and the disulfiram registry search, read on
2026-10-01;
unverified: Travera’s specifications, PARIS’s tissue rules, the “Signatera On
Genome” figures;
contradicted: the disulfiram review’s “undetectable since September 2025”;
stale: her ctDNA status, last reported 2026-03-03; GRANITE’s registry record, last
verified 2025-05; IMMUNE-FRAME, from February 2025.


expires_at. Needed for:

trial statuses: BATTMAN went from start to terminated in three and a half months;
vendor prices;
her clinical state.


mods_trial. BOT/BAL alone touched eight registry records, vaccines three, and
live-tissue testing and bacterial oncolytics one each.
mods_party. Needed for clinicians (her oncologist, the prescribing physician, the integrative physician), the two
unnamed DC providers, vendors (Cure First, Travera, Natera, Personalis) and sponsors
(Agenus, CCTG, MSK).
mods_meeting. The DC provider consultations are the first real case, and the
question checklist is what such a meeting row should carry.
mods_option_event. Two entries need events with an actor:

Vaccines are parked, not declined, only because no decision by her or a
clinician is recorded. A status change needs a decided_by.
Disulfiram has a “prescribed” event, with the prescriber as its actor, and no “started” event.


origin, next_step, readout. Every entry used origin and next step.

Origins were three clinicians, two news items, a forwarded video, Richard’s
question, the Metro map and one unknown (DC).
Readout carried the most important finding for two entries, DC and disulfiram: no
benefit readout is possible while she is NED and ctDNA-negative. The ctDNA-assay entry
exists because of that floor.



Where they contradict or extend it


kind.

trial is a route, not a kind. BOT/BAL is a combination reached through eight
trials and a French program; drop trial from the kind list.
Missing values: nothing fits a functional drug-sensitivity test, or live bacteria.
Add functional_test and live_biotherapeutic, or allow other.
Classes: three entries are classes of products, not products. Needs
scope ∈ {product, class} and member rows recording product, developer and trial.
Optional components: disulfiram with optional copper wants a component list, not a
choice between drug and combination.



horizon. Five of the eight fit one value.

Bacterial oncolytics fits none: it is watch-only and years away.
The ctDNA assay serves all three, because its result is what triggers the others.
Make horizon nullable, or add watch.



safety_vs_regimen conflates two questions. One is whether an option would be added
to maintenance; disulfiram would, and its level is caution. The other is whether it would
replace maintenance; BOT/BAL would, because of the washout. Split it:

relation_to_regimen ∈ {add_on, replaces, between_lines, none};
per-drug interaction rows: option × regimen drug × effect × level × source.

Keep the enum only as a rollup. A test can interact with the regimen too: PARIS’s washout,
unverified.


access_path must be multi-valued, with a status per route. BOT/BAL had nine known
routes, each blocked by a different criterion, plus one not yet researched. Route and
payer are separate dimensions: France’s AAC is expanded access, abroad, and reimbursed.
Suggested shape: mods_option_access, with route, trial or party, country, status,
blocking criteria and checked_at. A trial row also needs a role per option: access
route for BOT/BAL, evidence or precedent for VNP20009 and bacterial oncolytics.


evidence_level per option is too coarse. Evidence varies by indication and
setting:

Vaccines: phase 3 positive in resected melanoma, phase 2 negative in MSS CRC.
Disulfiram: approved for alcohol-use disorder, preclinical in CRC.
Tests: these need validity measures such as PPV and NPV, not efficacy levels.

Store evidence as claims carrying level, indication, setting and citation. An
option-level value is at most a rollup.


Fit facts should link to shared patient-fact claims, not be copied into each entry.

“ctDNA negative since 2025-12-05, last on file 2026-03-03” appears in five entries,
“MSS, TMB 2–3” in four, and the nodal-predominant recurrence in three. Each should be
one claim with one expiry and many links.
Each link needs a polarity: supports, argues against, or blocks. No liver metastases
supports BOT/BAL yet blocks three of its trials.
Each link needs an is_inference flag.



Fields the draft lacks.

target_primary. mRNA-4157 concerns her melanoma, not her CRC.
Triggers, for four entries. Some are patient events (ctDNA conversion, the next
biopsy, a melanoma stage). Some are external (an IND, a GI trial opening). Some windows
are relative to an event, which expires_at cannot express: MSK requires consent
within 6 weeks of the ctDNA result date.
Questions to a party, with answers. DC has eight for every provider, the disulfiram
review has thirteen for the prescribing physician, BOT/BAL has the trigger to agree with her oncologist, and
live-tissue testing has six for vendors.
Links between options:

live-tissue testing and DC can share one biopsy;
the ctDNA assay feeds the BOT/BAL trigger;
AUN is the leading indicator for E. americana.


Separate benefit and harm readouts. For disulfiram, harm is measurable and benefit
is not.
Source depth. Most citations here are second-hand: a paper cited by a repo doc cited
by this file. A claim needs both its source and the route by which it arrived.
source_kind also needs a value for the caregiver-authored journal, which is narrative,
not a report row.



One case is a dispute, not a contradiction. Who orders her Signatera: the integrative clinic, per
the reports, or someone outside it, per the integrative physician’s note? Neither source refutes the
other. Consider a disputed state.


Rule 5 does not fit tests. A test that is done produces a result, not a
ModsTreatmentEpisode. A test option needs a terminal state of its own that links to the
result, such as a mods_functional_test row or a document.


What the entries did not need

Statuses. pursuing and declined were not used.
Kinds. procedure, supplement and lifestyle were not used.
Access paths. soc was not used, and otc only for copper.
Single fields. A single evidence_level and a single access_path were each
replaced by lists in practice.
Cost. It was the thinnest field: a real number for one entry (live-tissue testing),
“inexpensive” for one, and unknown for the rest. That argues for cost as a claim (amount,
conditions, recurrence, source, date) rather than a column.

Shapes in the record that these entries do not test
Her clinical journal archive holds option-shaped material not catalogued here:

The trial-strategy consultant’s January 2026 case notes list seven CAR-T and cell-therapy trials with
registry numbers and coordinator contacts, and an abscopal SBRT-plus-checkpoint idea. They
also hold a three-phase supplement protocol whose doses are set by day of the chemotherapy
cycle.
The September 2025 entry names an RGCC vaccine and RGCC SOTs, suggested for prevention
after chemotherapy.

The schema should be able to hold:

trial lists with contacts, using mods_trial and mods_party;
supplement protocols whose dosing is timed against a treatment cycle;
items she has already had, such as an RGCC SOT in July 2025. Those belong in
ModsTreatmentEpisode, not in the catalog.

For the “Considering” view
The entries suggest these default columns:

candidate;
status;
horizon;
next step and the party it waits on;
last reviewed;
a count of its claims past expires_at.

cohorts/cbioportal_spike_2026-10.title: cBioPortal for MODS, October 2026
cohorts/cbioportal_spike_2026-10.content:
cBioPortal for MODS, October 2026
Issue: #658 · Builds on: #590 (cohort funnel), #327 (external cohort track)
Script: backend/scripts/cohorts/cbioportal_inventory.py
Data: the public API, portal v7.1.2, database 3.0.0, gene table hgnc_v7_2025.10.7. The script fetched
everything between 08:10 and 08:18 PDT on 2026-10-02 (613 requests). An exploratory pass from 07:49 gave the
same counts. Web sources were read the same day.

What this is for. The cohort funnel (#590) used one slice of cBioPortal to answer one question: how many
public patients have tumours like hers. This is the whole-site look. It covers what the portal holds, the
tools and services around it, what the terms allow, and which pieces serve MODS. It builds nothing except
the read-only script behind the numbers.

Summary


What cBioPortal is, for us. The largest free, uniform window onto clinical cancer genomics. It offers:

548 public studies behind one REST API with no login;
a weekly dump of the whole database;
open services around it: Genome Nexus for variant annotation, OncoTree for cancer types, Cancer Hotspots.

It is a source of evidence about patients and models like her. It is not a drug-response source: its one
drug-response dataset is a 2019 copy of GDSC. It is not a knowledge-graph source. Beyond overall survival, only
MSK-CHORD’s treatment timelines carry outcomes.


For her disease it holds 62 studies with colorectal samples, nearly twice the funnel’s 34. They include
MSK-IMPACT 50K, MSK-MET, NCI’s patient-derived models, and several organoid and cell-line collections (§1.2).


What the API already showed about her (§5):

Variants. Her APC frameshift is a recurrent hotspot, in 1.9–2.9% of colorectal patients in four cohorts. Her
TGFBR2, MGA and NTRK2 variants appear at their residues in none of about 9,000 patients. Getting that right
needed genomic coordinates, because protein strings mislead across sources.
Liver groups. Joining MSK-MET to MSK-CHORD gives an independent check on the Neighbors liver groups:
90% agreement, with “no liver” confirmed for 38 of 40. It also shows that disease like hers, nodal without
liver, is three public patients.
Models. Six BRAF V600E, MSS colorectal patient-derived models are orderable from NCI, with exome and
RNA-seq on the portal.



Recommendations, in order (§6):

a shared client with read-only MCP tools;
the MSK-MET cross-check for #614 (2026-10-05: #614 was decided as D-Q4-13, and the approved plan leaves the MSK-MET line out);
per-variant cohort context in the Genomic Browser and the Options Ledger;
Genome Nexus: Pfam domains on the lollipop now, the variant resolver later;
a proxy-model shortlist on #327.

GENIE is Richard’s call.


Not now:

a self-hosted portal holding her data;
cohort-derived KG edges;
TCGA as her expression reference. It failed in June, for reasons that still apply.



Found in passing:

OncoKB’s terms. They forbid AI/ML training. How MODS uses OncoKB is a licence decision recorded on the project’s tracker (#660).

OncoKB approved the project’s account on 2026-05-18
(#680).


A false answer without a token. OncoKB’s no-token API says there are no approved treatments for BRAF
V600E colon cancer. MODS’s connectors use the tokened API, and any new path must too.



1. What the public portal holds
Every count in this section comes from the script, run on 2026-10-02.
1.1 The whole portal





































WhatCountPublic studies548Samples, summed over studies414,487Studies on hg19 / hg38476 / 72Cancer types (OncoTree nodes)897Molecular profiles2,559Gene panels69Distinct clinical attributes4,811
The sample total double-counts. The MSK studies re-use the same MSK-IMPACT patients, and the TCGA builds
overlap each other.
What the studies carry:

















































DataStudiesMutations542Copy number351RNA (sequencing or microarray)156Protein (RPPA or mass spectrometry)83Structural variants223Overall survival316Progression-free survival77An MSI call (MSI_TYPE or MSI_STATUS)92Metastatic site101Treatment records97

Treatment data is concentrated in one study. The 97 studies hold 43,263 treatment rows, and MSK-CHORD
alone holds 24,028 of them (56%). Most of the rest, 11,157 rows, are spread over 64 TCGA builds.
Drug response is in one dataset. Of 201 “generic assay” profiles across 29 assay types, three are drug
response, and all three are the same CCLE 2019 screen (IC50, AUC and a z-score). §1.3 says what it is.
importDate is a reload date. All 548 studies show an import date in 2026 (441 of them in January), so
it says when the portal last loaded a study, not how old its data is. Reproducibility has to rest on the
portal version, the fetch time and the source publication.

1.2 Colorectal cancer across the whole portal
The funnel searched the bowel subtree of OncoTree plus the mixed studies that carry treatment data, 34 studies
in all. Counting colorectal samples in every study finds 62 studies and 44,986 colorectal samples. A
sample counts when its OncoTree code is one of the seven the funnel uses (COAD, READ, COADREAD, MACR, SRCCR,
CMC, CAIS). Three studies have no OncoTree field; for those, the cancer-type text or the study’s own cancer type
decides. No other colorectal
code is in use: the remaining bowel codes are appendiceal, anal, small-bowel, neuroendocrine or adenoma.
Some of the hits are not tumour data:

Blood. The three clonal-haematopoiesis studies hold 6,451 of the colorectal samples, almost all in
msk_ch_2023 and msk_ch_2020. Their mutations were called in blood, and the cancer type is the patient’s.
Never count them as tumour samples. Without them the total is 38,535.
Polyps. crc_hta11_htan_2021 holds 61 precancerous polyps.

The largest pan-cancer and model studies. All but HCMI are outside the funnel’s 34:

































































StudyColorectal samplesWhat it addsmsk_impact_50k_20265,277MSK-IMPACT 50K (Cancer Cell 2026): allele-specific copy number, cancer cell fractions, mutational signatures, HLA types. No treatment data.msk_met_20213,548MSK-MET (Cell 2022): per-organ distant-metastasis flags, including distant lymph nodes. §5.2 uses it.pancan_mimsi_msk_20242,447MSI calls with orthogonal MMR immunohistochemistrypan_origimed_20201,290Chinese pan-cancer panel cohortpancan_pdmr_20251,218 (175 models)NCI Patient-Derived Models Repository: PDX, PDX-derived organoids and cultures, with exome and RNA-seqmsk_impact_20171,007The original MSK-IMPACT cohortpancan_hcmi_2025318 (169 models)Human Cancer Models Initiative organoids, with RNA-seq and methylation. Also in the funnel.msk_ctdna_vte_2024173ctDNA panel sequencing (MSK-ACCESS)ccle_broad_2025, ccle_broad_2019, cellline_ccle_broad, ccle_genentech_2014, cellline_nci6096, 84, 56, 55, 7Cell lines; only CCLE 2019 carries drug responsepan_pdo_wcm_202669 (29 models)Weill Cornell patient-derived organoidspancan_pcawg_202052Whole genomes (PCAWG)
The full per-study table is in the script output.
1.3 What the one drug-response dataset is
CCLE 2019’s three drug-response profiles cover 266 compounds, not the two dozen of the original CCLE drug
panel. Every compound links to cancerrxgene.org, and the curve fits cite Vis et al. 2016, the GDSC fitting
method. So it is a pre-2019 snapshot of the Sanger GDSC screens, mapped onto CCLE lines. It includes
dabrafenib, PLX-4720, trametinib, cetuximab, 5-FU and SN-38. 55 of the portal’s 84 colorectal lines have IC50
rows, and so do 9 of its 10 BRAF V600E colorectal lines (all but COLO201).
For the Q4 proxy work (D16: PRISM first, GDSC2 as replication) it is a convenience copy, not a source. The
primary releases are newer, and its licence is ambiguous (§4).
2. Tools on the site
Everything except the chat works without logging in. Sources are the cbioportal-frontend code and
docs.cbioportal.org, read 2026-10-02.


















































ToolThe question it answersUse for MODSQuery page with OQLWhich samples carry these alterations? For example BRAF: MUT = V600E or APC: MUT = TRUNC.Defining a cohort in one line, as a shareable URLResults ViewOncoPrint, frequency by cancer type, mutual exclusivity, any-against-any plots, the lollipop, co-expression, altered-against-unaltered comparison with survival, pathways, downloadHand exploration of her genes across cohortsStudy ViewA cohort dashboard with click-to-filter charts: clinical attributes, mutated genes, survival, treatment charts, clinical-event counts. A patient “Similarity Map” (embeddings) is behind a feature flag since July 2026.Exploring MSK-CHORD by hand before writing a funnel stagePatient ViewOne patient: timeline, genomic evolution, mutational signatures and, since June 2026, an mRNA tab that plots the patient’s expression against the study cohortWhat a self-hosted instance would show for her (§6)Group ComparisonHow groups A and B differ: survival, clinical attributes, alterations, mRNA, protein, methylation and generic assays, drug response includedQuick checks of a hypothesisVirtual studies and sessionsCustom cohorts with permanent links. Login only stores them.Citable query links for Ledger factsMutationMapper, OncoPrinterLollipops and OncoPrints from pasted data. MutationMapper sends the pasted variants to Genome Nexus for annotation, so they leave the browser.Not for her datacBioPortalChat (chat.cbioportal.org, August 2026)Natural-language questions, answered by Claude Sonnet over the database, after a Google sign-in. It stores whole conversations indefinitely, staff may read them, and it asks users not to paste health information.Public-cohort questions only, never anything about her
The site is a good place for Richard to look around. The Study View of
MSK-CHORD shows the treatment and timeline data
the funnel used. MSK-MET shows the per-organ
metastasis flags.
3. Getting data out















































PathWhat it isBest forWatch forREST API (/api)152 operations, OpenAPI 3.1. No login, and the “internal” endpoints that serve treatments, clinical events and survival answer without auth too.Targeted queries: the funnel, this spike, an MCP toolIt calls itself “[Alpha]” and “beta”, and it broke real clients in 2026 (entrezGeneId became required on the mutations GET). Today projection=ID on /studies returns []. There is no published rate limit, and maintainers declined application-level limits on 2026-09-21, so pacing is on us.Weekly database dump (index)Parquet, one file per table, about 87 GB in all. The latest is dated 2026-09-27. The useful tables are small: mutations 176 MB, timeline events 11 MB, patient and sample clinical data 8 and 12.5 MB.Bulk population work in one pull, e.g. variant recurrence across all 548 studies with no pagingOnly recent dumps are kept, so archive what we use, with its date. A Hugging Face mirror is tagged AGPL, which conflicts with the data licences.Per-study tarballs and the datahub (datahub.assets.cbioportal.org/{studyId}.tar.gz; GitHub cBioPortal/datahub)Each study in cBioPortal’s staging formatFile-level copies of one studyOverwritten in place, with no version in the name. 38 studies, including crc_msk_2026, have neither, so the dump or the API is the only route to them.Client librariesNo official Python client. R cBioPortalData is maintained; CRAN cbioportalR likely breaks on whole-study pulls (its fix is unmerged). The documented Python bravado example points a Swagger-2.0 client at the OpenAPI 3.1 spec.—The funnel’s plain-HTTP client is the right call for us.Self-hosting (docker-compose)The web app (Java, 2–4 GB heap), ClickHouse, a session service and MongoDB. Studies load through validateData.py and metaImport.py.A private instance holding her data (§6)On Windows it must run from WSL2. A one-patient study looks loadable from the docs but is untested. The timeline format draws numeric labs such as CA 19-9 as line charts.MCP serversAn official hosted server (mcp.cbioportal.org, August 2026) that runs SQL over a ClickHouse clone; a “navigator” that turns questions into portal URLs; and BioMCP (MIT, about 645 stars), which includes cBioPortal variant frequenciesAd-hoc public-cohort questions in Claude sessionsThe official server needs Google sign-in and logs your account email and every query. “Still under construction”; the team’s own benchmark scores it 72% overall and 46% on navigation questions.
Three things follow for MODS:

Pin and record. Every pull should store the portal version, the fetch window and the source study, as the
funnel does. Nothing in the data says when it changed.
The dump beats paging for anything broad. One 176 MB mutation file answers “how often is this variant seen,
anywhere” for the whole portal, and it reaches crc_msk_2026, which has no tarball.
Nothing of hers goes to the hosted AI services. Their terms log identity and content.

3.1 Maple’s own client and tools (built 2026-10-02, #667)
Recommendation 1 (§6) is built.

One client. backend/connectors/cbioportal_client.py
is shared by the funnel, the inventory and the tools. It has a process-wide 0.6 s limiter, retries that honour
Retry-After, typed errors and an atomic disk cache. Its cache key is #590’s, so old caches replay unchanged.
Three read-only MCP tools in mods_server.py, built on
connectors/cbioportal_queries.py:

mods_cbioportal_studies: find studies, with data types and stated licence;
mods_cbioportal_variant_frequency: per-study patient counts for a variant or residue. It matches the exact
string and the GRCh37 coordinate, reports panel coverage, and refuses blood studies;
mods_cbioportal_cohort_counts: attribute values and treatment-agent patients under an OncoTree filter.
Every answer carries the portal version and the fetch window. Tool answers are cached for 7 days, in a cache
separate from the scripts’.


Proof the switch changed nothing. With the hash seed pinned, both scripts replay their caches offline to
byte-identical JSON under the old and new clients. Their JSON is now written with sorted keys, so a replay is
byte-identical whatever the seed.

4. Services around the portal, and the terms
4.1 Genome Nexus: variant annotation
MSK’s annotation service, and the one cBioPortal itself uses. One call returns, per variant:

VEP consequences and a canonical transcript;
SIFT, PolyPhen and AlphaMissense;
Cancer Hotspots and Mutation Assessor;
ClinVar, SignalDB (MSK germline frequencies) and myvariant.info;
OncoKB, only when a token is passed.

The software is MIT; the data carry their sources’ licences.


























InstanceBuildServerHotspotsClinVarwww.genomenexus.org (and v1, which the portal uses)GRCh372.2.3, VEP 116v32026-02-08grch38.genomenexus.orgGRCh381.4.1, lagging on purposev22025-01-06
Live probes with the textbook BRAF V600E:

GRCh37 works. The canonical transcript is ENST00000288602.6, c.1799T>A, p.V600E. The response carries the
V600 hotspot (897 tumours), Mutation Assessor “high”, and AlphaMissense 0.99.
GRCh38 misnames it by default. It picks ENST00000288602.11 and returns p.V640E, with no hotspots. The
MSK isoform override restores V600E, but hotspots stay empty. Her Caris VCFs are GRCh38, so her calls should be
annotated on GRCh37: lifted over, or queried by transcript HGVS-c.
It accepts more than coordinates. BRAF:p.V600E (with a colon) and ENST00000288602:c.1799T>A both
resolve. BRAF p.V600E (with a space) fails silently.
Failures return HTTP 200. A record can come back successfully_annotated: false with no error text.
OncoKB is dropped without notice when no token is passed. The rsID endpoint annotates every ALT allele at the
site. A client has to check each record.
Some of the payload is not licence-clean. SignalDB carries OncoKB-style terms, academic only with no
“patient services”, and myvariant.info passes COSMIC through. Request fields deliberately.

Two uses for MODS fall out of this:

The lollipop can get Pfam domains with two unauthenticated calls. These are
GET /ensembl/canonical-transcript/hgnc/{gene} and POST /pfam/domain, the calls cBioPortal’s own mutation
mapper makes. This is #173 item 7, with no need to adopt the AGPL component.
It can canonicalize her variants for cohort joins (§5.1). It can also settle the Phase 8.5 resolver’s
misses: an HGVS-p-only missense resolves through GENE:p.X. A novel indel annotates from its coordinates,
but it still has no ClinGen CAID.

4.2 OncoTree: the cancer-type vocabulary


Versions and licence. CC BY 4.0. The latest stable release is oncotree_2025_10_03, with 897 nodes; the
portal’s 897 cancer types are this tree. Each node carries NCIt and UMLS cross-references.


The crosswalk to MONDO lives on Mondo’s side, as xrefs:





















OncoTreeMondoCOADREADMONDO:0005008, colorectal adenocarcinomaCOADMONDO:0002271, colon adenocarcinomaREADMONDO:0002169, rectum adenocarcinoma


None of them is MODS’s colorectal anchor. The KG anchors colorectal cancer at MONDO:0005575, which carries
no OncoTree xref. Which Mondo node a cohort lands on is a vocabulary decision, so it is flagged here, not made
(CLAUDE.md hard rule).


OncoTree’s own mapping file has no MONDO column and lags the latest release by 52 codes.


4.3 Cancer Hotspots
v3 adds 164 hotspots (Bandlamudi et al., Cancer Cell 2026), mined from the MSK-IMPACT 50K cohort above. Data
are ODbL and the software AGPL; there is a public API. Hotspots are single residues and in-frame indels, so a
frameshift like her APC variant is out of scope by design; §5.1 is the question for those.
4.4 OncoKB, inside and outside the portal

On the public portal, OncoKB cards come through the portal’s own token. Its proxy demands a header in
which the caller attests that it is not fetching OncoKB data programmatically, so code must never use it.
The no-token public API gives a false answer for her. For BRAF V600E in colon adenocarcinoma it returns
“There are no FDA-approved or NCCN-compendium listed treatments specifically for patients with BRAF V600E
mutant colon adenocarcinoma.” It says the same for melanoma, so this comes from the stripped data, not from
curation. Anything that calls that API directly would pass the sentence on. (The Genome Nexus pipeline just
omits OncoKB without a token.)

MODS’s connectors call the tokened API and refuse to run without a token
(oncokb_annotate_connector.py: DEFAULT_API_BASE, download()). Any new path must keep that property.


The terms forbid training on it. The licensing FAQ says OncoKB “cannot be used to train AI/ML models
whether for academic or commercial purposes”; benchmarking needs explicit permission. “Use for patient
services” needs a licence agreement.

maureen_focus_v1 includes OncoKB; how MODS uses it is a licence decision recorded on the project’s tracker (#660).
OncoKB approved the project’s account in May 2026 (#680).
The stakes are small. OncoKB is 483 of about 8.0 million relations in that composition. 22 of them
concern her variants, and CIViC duplicates 9 of BRAF V600E’s 16. (2026-10-05: #744’s re-annotation has since grown the OncoKB source to 7,217 relations.)



4.5 Terms at a glance

Adapted material may not be shared. Citation: the FAQ asks for Cerami et al. 2012, Gao et al. 2013 and de Bruijn et al. 2023, plus the data source.
5. Three things the API can already do for her
These are demonstrations, not analyses. Each one is a pattern that a MODS integration would make routine.
5.1 Her somatic variants in public colorectal cohorts
Five of her somatic variants, counted per patient in four large colorectal cohorts:















































Variantcrc_msk_2026 (6,789)TCGA PanCancer (594)DFCI (619)SYSUCC, China (1,015)APC T1556Nfs*3 (c.4666dupA)195 (2.9%)11 (1.9%)18 (2.9%)23 (2.3%)BRAF V600E537 (7.9%)48 (8.1%)111 (17.9%)23 (2.3%)TGFBR2 at D5221 (D522N)000MGA at I9450000NTRK2 at V7170000

Her APC frameshift is a recurrent hotspot, the most common change at its residue in every cohort. Her
BRAF V600E is common, though cohorts differ several-fold. DFCI’s cohort is BRAF- and MSI-rich: by the funnel’s
rule only 37 of its 111 V600E patients are MSS.
Her TGFBR2, MGA and NTRK2 variants appear at their residues in none of about 9,000 patients. The genes
themselves are often mutated (403, 415 and 148 patients in crc_msk_2026). The panels cover them, except
MGA on IMPACT341 (202 samples). For the NTRK2 V717M VUS, no recurrence is weak evidence against a hotspot
role, not a verdict.
Protein strings are not a safe join key. The first pass counted her APC variant as absent, because
cBioPortal gives T1556Nfs*3 (a duplication in a run of As) a proteinPosStart of 1554, not 1556. And TGFBR2
is numbered on different isoforms in different studies: residue 522 reads D in the MSK data and R in TCGA’s.
The script matches on the exact protein-change string and checks it against the GRCh37 genomic coordinate.
For APC and BRAF the two agree exactly in all four cohorts. Any variant-level join in MODS should go through
genomic coordinates and one canonical annotation (§4, Genome Nexus).

5.2 Joining studies on MSK-IMPACT IDs: liver and distant nodes
MSK studies share patient IDs, so one study can annotate another. MSK-MET (about 25,000 patients) records, per
organ, whether a distant metastasis was diagnosed, taken from pathology reports and billing codes
(Nguyen et al. 2022). That includes distant lymph nodes.
The funnel had no such field: MSK-CHORD’s lymph-node flag mixes regional and distant nodes, so the funnel could
not pick out nodal disease like hers. Group sizes only, because #614 pre-registers the Neighbors question:















































BRAF V600E + MSS, MSK-METMSK-METAlso in MSK-CHORD…with encorafenib or anti-EGFR there…with encorafeniball1411265732metastatic1371235531no liver metastasis recorded4946129distant nodes, no liver8831nodes, neck or mediastinum only3300

Disease like hers is about three public patients. That counts the patients whose specific distant sites
are nodes, neck or mediastinum. It is enough for an anecdote and too few for a Neighbors group.
“Unspecified” is common. 17 of the 49 patients with no liver flag carry only the unspecified-site flag,
so absence of a named site is weak evidence.
The join gives #614 a check that could have failed. MSK-CHORD reads liver involvement from radiology
reports by NLP; MSK-MET records it separately. On the 3,079 colorectal patients in both, the two agree for
2,770 (90.0%). When they disagree it is mostly MSK-CHORD saying liver where MSK-MET does not (217 against
80), probably because MSK-CHORD’s follow-up runs later. Among BRAF V600E + MSS patients, MSK-MET confirms
MSK-CHORD’s “no liver” for 38 of 40. So the funnel’s liver groups hold up against an independent reading.

5.3 Models with her driver profile

The portal has no drug response for the PDX or organoid models. Their value is that they can be found,
ordered, and matched to her expression profile, which is the Q1 2027 PDX and organoid lane in #327. The MSS
cell lines match an internal memory note: HT-29, COLO 205/201 (one donor), SW1417, MDST8 and OUMS-23. RKO and LS411N
are MSI-high.
6. Where it fits in MODS
The yardstick is the Q4 plan: Spine B ships the Options Ledger and Neighbors, and Spine A earns a model signal on
proxies. Two standing guardrails apply. Other patients never become KG nodes, and cohorts are validation and
decision support, never a repurposing signal.

One is attested against, and the other gives a false answer for her (§4.4).
The ranking follows two lessons from this repo. A tested shared client comes before features, because the funnel
and this spike both had to rebuild the same plumbing. And population data serves decisions and checks, not the
model, until the model beats its baselines (Q4 roadmap §3.2).
Why build tools rather than adopt the official MCP server or BioMCP:

The official server needs a Google sign-in and logs every query against the account.
Both serve Claude sessions only. Maple’s own backend and agents can’t call them.
Neither shares the funnel’s cache, pacing or fetch-window records.

BioMCP is still a reasonable stopgap for ad-hoc public questions in a session.
7. Follow-ups
Filed on 2026-10-02 with Richard’s go-ahead: three as new issues and three as comments on the existing issues
they belong to.

F3 as built (2026-10-04)
The Genomic Browser’s Table tab now has a CRC cohorts column: patients carrying the variant, out of patients
sequenced over the gene, across every public colorectal study on the portal.

How it is built. scripts/cohorts/build_variant_context.py
writes backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/variant_context.json (gitignored). GET /api/mods/vcf/cohort-frequency
serves it. The rules are in mods_variant_context_service.py,
and the pooled count is pooled_variant_frequency in connectors/cbioportal_queries.py. A full build takes
about four minutes at the 0.6 s pace.
Which calls. Somatic calls from the two colorectal specimens: tiered Pathogenic to VUS, VAF ≥ 0.05, and
absent from the separate melanoma specimen. A call that two independent cancers share is inherited, so it is
left out. Without that second specimen the build refuses.
The join. Her GRCh38 calls are lifted to GRCh37 locally (pyliftover, UCSC chain), so no coordinate of
hers is sent anywhere. The portal is asked for gene-level calls only. The exact-match string is the one the
portal records at her coordinate (T1556Nfs*3, where Caris writes T1556fs).
Which studies. 28 studies are typed colorectal, typed bowel, or sit under colorectal. A bowel-typed study
without OncoTree codes is skipped, and so are the msk_ch_* studies. MSK-IMPACT, TCGA and CPTAC IDs count once
across studies; any other ID is local to its study.
Check against §5.1. Restricted to the four cohorts, the build reproduces §5.1 exactly: APC 195 / 11 / 18 / 23
and BRAF 537 / 48 / 111 / 23. String and coordinate agree in all four (test_live_survey_counts_reproduce, opt-in).
A disagreement the column shows rather than hides. Over all 28 studies, crc_msk_2017 and coadread_mskcc
anchor the same A-run insertion one base later (5:112175952:-:A). There the string finds 30 patients and the
coordinate finds 5. The cell carries a ⚠, and the tooltip gives the per-study counts.
Not done: the Options Ledger. A Ledger fact cannot cite this until the Ledger schema lands (#565, #613).

Parallelization analysis (for F1–F6)

Surfaces touched:

backend API: yes (F3);
frontend: yes (F3, F4);
worker handler: no;
migration: probably not. F3’s table can be a cached file first, and becomes one if it moves into Postgres;
MCP tool: yes (F1);
DB-stored config: no;
docs: yes;
tests: yes (F1 fixtures, F3).


Parallel split. F1 goes first, because F3 and F5 call its client. F2, F4 and F6 are independent of it and
of each other, and can run now. F3’s frontend waits on its API contract.
Collision hotspots.

backend/mcp_servers/mods_server.py (F1) is shared with every MCP change.
frontend/src/components/GenomicBrowser.jsx (F3, F4) is also touched by the open PR #643. Serialize F3 and
F4 behind it.
No migrations.py, component_registry.py, main.py, Terminal.jsx or ComponentLoader.jsx changes are
expected.


Verify-how:

F1: fixture tests, plus one live call per tool against /api/info recorded in the output.
F2: the funnel prints the agreement table on every run.
F3: the APC and BRAF counts reproduce §5.1, and string and coordinate matches agree.
F4: BRAF shows RBD, C1 and kinase domains at 156–227, 235–280 and 458–712.
F5: the resolver’s miss count drops on her 14 eligible variants.



8. Limits

Counts are as of 2026-10-02, from portal v7.1.2. Studies are reloaded in place, and the API is beta.
MSK-MET’s site flags come from billing codes and pathology reports (Nguyen et al. 2022), which the authors
say miss some events. “Unspecified” is common.
The MSS rule is the funnel’s. Group sizes inherit its definitions, including its judgement calls.
Untested: loading a one-patient study into a self-hosted instance; embedding react-mutation-mapper in
Maple; whether the API is throttled at the infrastructure level.
Unverified: the MSS status of CL34 and SNUC5; the current DepMap and HCMI terms; whether GENIE BPC CRC is
browsable on the GENIE portal as well as on Synapse (de Bruijn et al. 2023 describes BPC data in cBioPortal).
The transcript problem is general. Any protein-level comparison across sources can mislead. §5.1 found two
cases in five variants.

Reproduce
The numbers above measure the portal on 2026-10-02, and it reloads weekly. To replay this measurement, point
the script at its snapshot in the main checkout:
python backend/scripts/cohorts/cbioportal_inventory.py --offline --cache-dir C:/Maple/backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/snapshots/2026-10-02_658/http_cache
python backend/scripts/cohorts/cbioportal_inventory.py --json backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/inventory.json


The snapshot holds the run’s 613 cached responses and its output, inventory_2026-10-02.json. It is
host-only and gitignored, because MSK-CHORD and MSK-MET are CC BY-NC-ND. An offline replay on 2026-10-04
sent no request and reproduced that output exactly.
A fresh measurement (the second command) sends about 650 requests, one at a time with a 0.6 s pause,
and caches them under backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/http_cache/ in the checkout it runs in. Copy that
cache into a new dated snapshot before the session ends.
Each step prints its own fetch window in PDT.

Web sources were read on 2026-10-02 by two research passes. Every claim above carries its source, either inline
or in the issue.

cohorts/cohort_funnel_2026-10.title: Public colorectal cohort funnel, October 2026
cohorts/cohort_funnel_2026-10.content:
Public colorectal cohort funnel, October 2026
Issue: #590 · Track: #327
Script: backend/scripts/cohorts/cbioportal_funnel.py
Data: the public cBioPortal API (portal v7.1.2, database 3.0.0), queried 2026-10-01. Every response was
fetched between 11:18 and 12:04 PDT. MSK-CHORD’s cBioPortal import is dated 2026-07-30.

What this is for. Before building a “people like her” (Neighbors) view, count how many public
patients have tumours that look like Maureen’s on somatic features, and check whether their
treatment timelines are usable. A cohort like this is decision support and validation. It is never
a repurposing signal: everyone counted here received standard drugs, and real-world exposure says
nothing about drugs nobody gave them.

Summary


Her full somatic profile is not in public data. In MSK-CHORD the strict funnel runs: 5,543
colorectal cancer (CRC) patients, then 4,114 metastatic, 280 BRAF V600E, 181 MSS, 53 APC truncating
and 2 ATM truncating. Neither of the last 2 is recorded as free of liver metastases, so 0 remain.


APC and ATM truncation are the wrong filters for a treatment question. They remove 99% of the
cohort without changing which drugs apply. The usable cohort is BRAF V600E + MSS + metastatic: 181
patients in MSK-CHORD. Of these, 46 never had liver involvement recorded, 133 did, and 2 are unknown.


98 of the 181 received encorafenib and/or an anti-EGFR antibody, and all 98 exposures have a start
and a stop date. 39 also have a later regimen recorded.


Encorafenib specifically. Among BRAF V600E + MSS patients at any stage:

71 have an encorafenib episode;
58 of those had a concurrent anti-EGFR antibody, 26 of them with a MEK inhibitor as well;
median time on encorafenib was 155 days (IQR 80.5–290.5).

66 of the 71 had systemic therapy recorded before encorafenib, so this is mostly later-line use.


Liver status at the start of encorafenib: 26 without, 45 with. These are the group sizes for the
proposed pre-registered question below. I deliberately did not compute their outcomes.


MSK-CHORD is the only public source with usable treatment timelines for this question. Across all
34 public CRC studies there are 342 distinct BRAF V600E + MSS patients where MSS can be resolved, and
128 of them are outside MSK-CHORD. None of those 128 has a usable encorafenib or anti-EGFR duration.
The other studies with timelines add 1 usable anti-EGFR course (TCGA, MSI unknown) and 1 encorafenib
course with no stop date (HCMI, MSI unknown).


GENIE BPC CRC would add curated regimen lines and imaging-based progression. It needs a Synapse
registration, which is Richard’s call. It probably adds few encorafenib exposures (see below).


Definitions
The funnel runs in the order #590 sets, and every stage is a named rule in the script.







































































#StageRuleMSK-CHORD fields1CRC patients≥1 sample with OncoTree code COAD, READ, COADREAD, MACR, SRCCR, CMC or CAIS: the codes MSK-CHORD groups under “Colorectal Cancer”ONCOTREE_CODE2metastaticregistry stage 4, a sequenced metastasis, or a distant organ named as a tumour site by NLP over radiology reports: liver, lung, bone, CNS/brain, pleura or adrenal (next section explains why)STAGE_HIGHEST_RECORDED, SAMPLE_TYPE, LIVER, LUNG, BONE, CNS_BRAIN, PLEURA, ADRENAL_GLANDS3BRAF V600Ea mutation call with protein change V600E on any CRC sampleMSK-IMPACT mutations4MSS≥1 CRC sample reads Stable, and none reads InstableMSI_TYPE5APC truncatinga protein-truncating call, such as a nonsense or frameshift mutation (the script’s TRUNCATING set)mutations6ATM truncatingsame classesmutations7no liver metastasesLIVER = No, and no sequenced liver metastasisLIVER, METASTATIC_SITE8exposurean encorafenib, cetuximab or panitumumab row in the treatment timelineTreatment events, AGENT9time on therapythe index episode has a recorded start and stopTreatment events10what came nexta later systemic regimen is recordedTreatment events
All four MSK-IMPACT panels in the CRC set (341, 410, 468, 505 genes) cover BRAF, APC, ATM, KRAS and
NRAS. So a missing call means wild type, not “not tested”. 5,521 of the 5,543 CRC samples were
sequenced against a matched normal, including all 214 BRAF V600E + MSS samples. None of the 214 carries
a KRAS or NRAS hotspot at the extended-RAS codons.
Why “metastatic” includes the NLP site flags
MSK-CHORD has no single “metastatic” field. I tested three readings against an external yardstick: the
2,665 CRC patients who received a drug used in CRC only for metastatic disease. Those drugs are
bevacizumab, irinotecan, regorafenib, trifluridine/tipiracil, cetuximab, panitumumab, encorafenib and
ramucirumab.

























DefinitionPatientsOf the 2,665, capturedstructured only: registry stage 4 or a sequenced metastasis3,0042,142 (80%)structured, or the liver NLP flag3,6442,476 (93%)structured, or any distant-organ NLP flag (used)4,1142,610 (98%)
The structured fields alone miss a fifth of demonstrably metastatic patients. By construction, the
patients they miss are registry stage I–III with only the primary tumour sequenced. Their drugs say
they had metastatic disease later. Of the 1,429 patients that no definition flags, 55 (3.8%) received
one of these drugs, so the chosen rule rarely misses. The script prints this table on every run.
Timeline rules
MSK-CHORD treatment rows are per-agent courses, with start and stop days counted from the sequencing date
(day 0). The timeline has no absolute dates.

Episode. Rows of one class merge into an episode when the next row starts within 30 days of the
current stop.
Index. The patient’s first encorafenib episode. A patient who never had encorafenib is indexed on
their first anti-EGFR episode.
Time on therapy. Index stop minus index start. It is usable only if every merged row has a stop.
Regimen. Agents starting between 14 days before the index start and 14 days before the index stop.
Supportive agents (leucovorin, bone agents, megestrol) are excluded.
What came next. The earliest regimen that starts after the index’s last 14 days and is either a new
agent or a regimen agent restarted more than 30 days after the stop.
Possibly ongoing. The patient is alive, has no later regimen, and the index stopped within 30 days
of last contact. This classification relies on OS_MONTHS sharing the timeline’s day 0. MSK documents

AACR GENIE BPC colorectal: what it would add
GENIE BPC is not on the public portal. It needs a Synapse account and acceptance of GENIE’s terms of
access, so whether to get it is Richard’s call. Here is what it would add, from #327 and the population
planning doc.

Curated outcomes.

It holds 1,485 CRC patients in v2.0-public, from several cancer centres including MSK.
Curators abstracted it under the PRISSMM model: regimen-level drug data with dates, imaging- and
oncologist-assessed progression, and so a real progression-free survival per regimen. That is the
endpoint MSK-CHORD lacks.
MSI/MMR and PD-L1 are recorded.


Some patients outside MSK. MSK-CHORD is one centre’s referral population.
Probably few encorafenib exposures. To my recollection the CRC cohort was sequenced well before the
April 2020 approval of encorafenib + cetuximab. That is unverified, so check the BPC data guide before
counting on it. If true, BPC strengthens the anti-EGFR and chemotherapy questions more than the
encorafenib one.
Overlap. MSK contributes to BPC, so some BPC patients are MSK-CHORD patients. Whether the identifiers
allow a join is unknown until the data is in hand.

Licence notes

MSK-CHORD is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, as stated in its cBioPortal study description. Commercial requests go
to MSK. In practice:

Attribution. Cite Jee et al., Nature 2024, and cBioPortal.
Non-commercial. Maple’s use is personal and non-commercial. Anything else needs MSK’s permission.
No derivatives. Adapted material may not be shared. Raw responses stay under
backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/ (gitignored), patient-level derived tables are never committed, and
this repo carries only the script and aggregate counts.
Publishing counts. Whether aggregate counts on a public page count as “adapted material” is a
contractual question, not a technical one. My reading is that counts are facts reported with
attribution, as papers report them. #327 left the call to Richard, and on 2026-10-06 he cleared the
aggregate counts on this page for publication.


The other 33 studies state no licence in their descriptions. TCGA and CPTAC are NIH open-access data.
Check each source publication’s terms before any reuse beyond counts.
GENIE BPC: Synapse registration and GENIE’s terms of access. That is a data-use agreement in all but
name.
TabPFN. #327 notes that MSK-CHORD’s non-commercial clause stacks with the TabPFN weights’ licence.
That matters only if these rows train a model, and nothing here does.

Proposed pre-registered question for a two-week Neighbors v0 spike
(2026-10-05: approved as decision D-Q4-13 on #614 and run once from the frozen code. Its results by liver group are not published.)
Question. Among MSK-CHORD patients with BRAF V600E, MSS colorectal cancer who started an
encorafenib-based regimen:

How long did they stay on encorafenib?
What systemic therapy came next?

Answer both separately for those without and those with liver involvement on radiology at the start.
Why this one. Her disease is nodal without liver metastases, and she is on BRAF/EGFR maintenance. So
the practical questions are how long such therapy holds and what usually follows it. Liver involvement is
the subgroup her own record makes salient (mission spec §2.5).
Fixed in advance:

Cohort. BRAF V600E + MSS CRC patients in MSK-CHORD with at least one encorafenib row, under this
script’s definitions. That is 71 at the 2026-10-01 query, and 69 of them also carry the metastatic flag.
Index. The start of the first encorafenib episode, with rows merged across gaps of 30 days or less.
Groups: liver at index, as defined above.

“With liver” means a radiology report naming liver by index + 30 days: 45 patients.
“Without liver” means none, though at least one radiology report was read by then: 26 patients.
The “ever” flag is not used. It would move 6 of the 26 into the liver group, because their liver
disease appeared only after encorafenib started.


Primary endpoint. Time on encorafenib (index stop minus index start). An episode is censored when
the patient was alive, had no later regimen, and stopped within 30 days of last contact (8 of the 71).
Secondary endpoints:

time to next regimen;
class of the next regimen;
the share with a positive NLP progression call after day 28 of the episode.


Analysis. A Kaplan–Meier median with a 95% CI per group, and the difference in medians with a
bootstrap CI. It is descriptive: with 26 and 45 patients no test is powered, and none will be reported
as one.
Reported by group, not adjusted for:

line of therapy (66 of 71 had systemic therapy before encorafenib);
regimen composition (with anti-EGFR, with a MEK inhibitor, with chemotherapy);
prior treatment outside MSK (19 of 71).


Freeze. The question, the definitions in this script and the analysis code are committed before
anyone computes durations by liver group. This script stops at group sizes and pooled durations for that
reason.

What the answer can and cannot say.

It describes how encorafenib-based therapy went for comparable patients in routine care at one centre,
mostly in later lines.
It does not predict her course.

Her regimen began with chemotherapy for a recurrence and continued as maintenance, and she has no
evidence of disease on it.
The cohort records disease status only through NLP calls, and has 24 encorafenib starts with
concurrent chemotherapy and 2 that look like a first systemic therapy.


It is not causal. Liver involvement travels with tumour burden, line of therapy and performance status.

Limits

One centre, a referral population, and mostly later-line encorafenib. There are no absolute dates,
so era can’t be adjusted for.
Rows record courses, not doses. 12 of the 100 index episodes are shorter than 14 days, which may
mean single administrations or recording artefacts.
Encorafenib exposure is a floor. Masked investigational rows (27 of 214 patients) may hide trial
BRAF or EGFR regimens.
Treatment before MSK is a flag, not a regimen list.
Site and progression flags are NLP model outputs. The liver flag misses at least 3.4% of sequenced
liver metastases.
Time on treatment is a proxy for benefit, not progression-free survival.

Reproduce
These numbers measure a portal that reloads weekly, so a fresh run measures a different one. To replay this
measurement, point the script at its snapshot in the main checkout:
python backend/scripts/cohorts/cbioportal_funnel.py --offline --cache-dir C:/Maple/backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/snapshots/2026-10-02_590/http_cache
python backend/scripts/cohorts/cbioportal_funnel.py --json backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/funnel.json


The snapshot is a 2026-10-02 re-run. The 2026-10-01 cache was lost when the worktree holding it was
pruned. The 2026-10-02 live re-run reproduces this document: 344 of the 346 numbers in its results
sections, and the other two are month conversions of day counts it carries. The snapshot holds its 702
cached responses and its output, funnel_2026-10-02.json. It is host-only and gitignored, because
MSK-CHORD is CC BY-NC-ND. An offline replay on 2026-10-04 sent no request and matched that output
exactly, apart from its own timestamp.
A fresh measurement (the second command) sends about 700 requests, one at a time with a pause
between them, and caches them under backend/data/cohorts/cbioportal/http_cache/ in the checkout it
runs in. Copy that cache into a new dated snapshot before the session ends. --refresh re-downloads.
Query window. Every printed study block carries its own fetch window in PDT.
The client is the shared one in backend/connectors/cbioportal_client.py (#667). Its cache key and
entry layout are this script’s originals, so caches made before the switch replay unchanged. Since #667
the --json output is written with sorted keys, so an offline replay is byte-identical across runs.

Kaiser medications and conditions at one row per record
Issue: #624, Lane I, PR I-3. Decision: D-Q4-16
(#631) item 3, with items 2, 5 and 7. Builds on: I-2
(#674: migration 111 and mods_ehr_upsert). Code read:
main at 855b437. Design only: no code, migration or database access went into this document.
Where a number would change a recommendation, the read-only query is in Appendix A for the steward
to run.
(Status, 2026-10-05: built and merged (PR #814) after Richard took every default in §7 (D-Q4-18). Where the build differs from this text, the implementation notes at the end say so. Counts in §1 are as of 2026-10-02.)
Maple keeps 141 Kaiser medication rows for 509 orders, and 42 condition rows for 392 conditions,
because both tables are unique on a name. I-2 gave each stored row the Kaiser id of the record it was
first imported from, and holds back every update to them. I-3 stores every record as its own row and
turns updates on. “Current medication” and “active condition” then stop being a column that readers
trust, and become a derived answer with written rules.

What it changes for her record. All 509 orders and 392 conditions are in Maple, and each stays
in step with Kaiser: a stopped drug reads stopped, and an encounter diagnosis is no longer filed as
a problem-list entry. “What is she on now” gets one answer with its reasons, which the Options
Ledger’s safety check and the week-1 safety lane need.
What it changes for the model. Smoke run #1’s export excludes the medication edges (playbook
D2), and Run #2 Arm A reuses that export, so none of the medication change reaches training.
Condition edges are not excluded. biolink:has_phenotypic_feature edges built from
mods_condition go into any export that includes maple_patient. Arm A is untouched. A later
export, such as Arm B’s, would see I-3’s changes if the patient KG is re-materialized first (§5.4,
J24).

0. Summary

Identity is already in place. Migration 111’s unique index on the Kaiser id is the identity. I-3
makes the two name indexes partial, covering only rows that have no Kaiser id. Kaiser records then
never collapse on a name; the March HTML rows still dedupe exactly as today (§2.1).
The 137 + 42 stored rows with an id are already per-record rows, only stale. They stay, and each
is updated in place from its own record, with every old value in mods_ehr_record_change. The
first sync inserts the 370 orders and 350 conditions it collapses today. This replaces the hand-off
outline’s “mark the old rows superseded” (§2.3).
Fidelity: I-3 also keeps intent, category, sig, dose, route, frequency and prescriber for orders,
and category, verification status and recorded date for conditions (§2.2).
Derived views: one Python module classifies each record into a state, with an explicit rules
table (§4). Consumers combine states by their own error costs. A safety screen over-includes; the
KG under-asserts.
24 judgment calls are flagged, each with a proposed default (§7). Most are vocabulary
mappings, which CLAUDE.md reserves for Richard.
Proof: a read-only compare script builds the old and new KG edges from one database snapshot and
explains every difference by a rule row (§5.5). A positive control has to pass: each drug of her
maintenance regimen must read current or on hold.
Staging: backup, then merge, then compare on the same data, then a sync at a login, then compare
again. The KG is re-materialized last, on a schedule that respects the Run #2 exports (§6).
Migration 113, free on every branch as of 2026-10-02. Re-check it at implementation time (§2.5).
(Built as 116: see the implementation notes at the end.)

1. Where things stand (2026-10-02)

2. The schema change
2.1 Identity, and what happens to the name indexes
Identity is the Kaiser id, already enforced by migration 111. uq_mods_medication_source_record and
uq_mods_condition_source_record are unique on (patient, source, resource type, id) where the id is
set. I-3 adds no identity. It changes the two indexes that collapse records today:




















Index todayColumnsAfter I-3idx_mods_medication_dedupUNIQUE (patient_id, name)replaced by uq_mods_medication_name_without_id: the same columns, WHERE source_record_id IS NULLidx_mods_condition_dedupUNIQUE (patient_id, name, category)replaced by uq_mods_condition_name_without_id: the same columns, WHERE source_record_id IS NULL
Why partial, not dropped. Rows without an id still need a key:

the March HTML rows (15 and 61): frozen, but a re-run must not duplicate them;
a reconnected Cerbo: its cerbo_id is not read as an identity yet, so its rows fall back to the
name index, as today;
the 4 ambiguous rows, until J23 is applied.

For these rows the partial index is exactly today’s rule: the same columns, still across sources. A
record with a Kaiser id never touches it. So medications_collapsed and conditions_collapsed drop
to 0 for Kaiser records by construction, and any nonzero value is a defect to stop on.
It cannot fail on prod’s data. The partial index covers a subset of the rows the full index
already keeps unique, which is migration 112’s argument. The migration:

builds the new index before it drops the old one;
copies 112’s transaction-scoped advisory lock and catalog check. Cloud Run and the local backend
both run the chain at boot, and two chains creating one index name would fail a boot.

ModsMedication and ModsCondition declare the new indexes, and a test compares the declared shape
with the migrated one, as tests/test_migration_112.py does.

2.3 How the existing rows map to per-record rows
The 137 medication and 42 condition rows that carry a Kaiser id are already per-record rows. Each was
inserted from one record, the first to carry its name, and I-2’s backfill gave it that record’s id.
What is wrong with them is that they are stale, not that they stand for a name. So I-3 keeps them and
updates each one from its own record at the first sync. Every replaced value goes to
mods_ehr_record_change.
This differs from the I-2 hand-off outline, which had the old rows marked superseded. Superseding:

would need a marker column on both tables and a filter in every reader;
would collide with the identity index: a superseded row keeps its id, so the fresh row for the
same record would be refused;
would keep nothing that update in place loses. The history table holds every old value, and the
pre-sync backup (§6) holds every old row.

4. The derived views
4.1 Shape
Per record, then per consumer. The view classifies each record into a state, and each consumer
combines the states the way its error costs say:

A safety screen against her regimen must over-include. Missing a drug she takes is the
dangerous error.
The knowledge graph must under-assert. An edge saying she takes a drug is a fact the explorer
shows, and that a future export could train on.

A single “current” boolean cannot serve both, so the view never collapses to one.
One implementation, in Python. I recommend a module, for example backend/mods_ehr_derived.py,
with a pure classifier per record type and thin readers over them, rather than a SQL VIEW. The rules
are judgment calls that will change, and a SQL view would make every change a migration. The KG
builder, the Terminal and the Ledger are all Python, so a SQL view would also be a second
implementation that could disagree with the first. D-Q4-16 says “derived view”, meaning derived, not
necessarily a SQL VIEW. Each rules-table row below becomes one test case.
Stamped. Every result carries:

rules_version (starting at ehr-derived/1) and as_of. The KG writes both into edge metadata,
so a materialization built under older rules is visible by comparing the stored stamp with the
code’s.
last_sync_at: the last Kaiser sync that fetched the type without a failure. “Current” means
current as of that sync, and a sync needs Richard’s login: there is no refresh token. A consumer
shows it beside the list.

Scope. Kaiser FHIR records (epic_fhir). The March HTML rows enter only where a rule row says so.
Cerbo needs its own rows once it is reconnected (#512). Its prescriptions and supplements are exactly
what a safety screen needs, and nothing here covers them yet.
Readers.

classify_medication_order(row, as_of) and classify_condition(row), both pure;
classify_medication_orders(rows, as_of): every order’s state, with M20 decided per drug
(added 2026-10-08, §4.2). Every medication reader and the KG builder go through it;
medications(db, patient, as_of) → each order with its state and reason;
medications_to_screen(...), the safety list;
active_conditions(...), the active view.

They are served at GET /api/mods/clinic/medications/current and
GET /api/mods/clinic/conditions/active, mounted in mods_clinic_api.py, which touches no registry
hotspot. The Terminal serves them as ehr ls medications/current and ehr ls conditions/active.
Dates. as_of is a date, defaulting to today in Pacific time. Kaiser datetimes are stored as UTC
calendar days (audit §3), so a window can be one day off at its edge. No rule below is that sensitive.

5. What the patient KG emits after I-3
5.1 Medication edges
The builder classifies every Kaiser order and resolves each order’s drug as it does today: the name’s
first word, then the full name, through DRUG_ALIASES. Then it decides per resolved entity (M13):

current_medication if any order is current;
otherwise past_medication if any order, or any March HTML row, is evidence she took it;
otherwise nothing.

Treatment-episode drugs still win (M18). Compared with today, on the same rows:

an order that is cancelled, a draft, entered in error, of unknown status, or not an order stops
producing past_medication;
an active order outside its window moves from current_medication to past_medication;
a March HTML row reading active moves from current to past, unless a Kaiser order for the same drug
is current;
a drug with one current and one ended order gets one current edge, never both.

5.2 Condition edges
One biolink:has_phenotypic_feature edge per resolved disease entity, from every record that is not
void, refuted or unconfirmed, of any category and any status. That keeps today’s “has had”
meaning, the one the foundations trained on. Compared with today, on the same rows:

refuted, entered-in-error and unconfirmed records stop producing edges;
each edge’s metadata is aggregated, not copied from whichever row came first.

The disease resolver matches names exactly, so most Kaiser condition names resolve to nothing today.
docs/pdr_personalization_writeup.md counts 6 phenotype edges on her node. Expect the edge set to
move little; the proof below measures it.
5.3 Edge metadata
Today the first row added wins. Both edge tables insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
(mods_patient_kg_service 995 and 1018), and the builders read rows with no ORDER BY. With 509
orders for about 140 drug names, an edge’s status or start_date would then depend on row order:
the tie-break the house rules forbid.
The rule instead:

Scalar keys: each key the edge carries today holds the value when every contributing record
agrees. Otherwise it is NULL, and the distinct values are listed under <key>_values. The keys are
name, status or clinical_status, category, rxnorm_code, route, dose_text,
frequency, icd_code, snomed_code and abatement_date.
Dates: start_date and onset_date hold the earliest date.
Added: record_count, source_record_ids (sorted), state_counts, rules_version and
as_of.

A shuffled input must give identical edges and metadata; a test checks it.

Built on branch claude/ehr-i3-per-record after D-Q4-18 (#689), “A with all defaults”. Where

Interpretations, each open to change:

§5.3’s scalar rule counts an unstated value as a value: a key holds its value only when
every record states the same one, unstated included.
end_date (“valid until”) is on today’s medication edge but not in §5.3’s key list; it is
treated as a scalar. The edge also carries clinical_status_raw, per J19.
A “resolved entity” is a connected component: records that resolve to a common target on
either side decide together, so no target can receive both medication predicates.

rides on the profile’s edge under also_from.

without a start date not recent.
Medication and condition rows from a source other than Kaiser FHIR and the March HTML
import (Cerbo, once reconnected) are not classified and contribute nothing; none exist.

the previous sync’s UTC day; an undated row is counted apart, never guessed.
