kg/kg_composition_pipeline_writeup.content:
Building a Defensible KG Composition Pipeline — Formal Writeup
Authors: whafa, Claude (Maple project)
Date: 2026-05-09
Status: Phases A–E CLOSED (deployed to prod). Phase C4 (consumer cutover for the Explorer) CLOSED 2026-05-13 — canonical schema is the Explorer default, composition picker live, Maureen browsable alongside any composition; legacy tables preserved behind USE_CANONICAL_KG=false / ?canonical=false. Phase F (patient-anchor scoping) still planned.
Related planning docs:

an internal memory note — the parent plan
pdr_phase8.5_variant_kg_planning.md — variant entry point (CIViC/OncoKB/PharmGKB connectors land here)
kg_anchor_scoping_planning.md — Phase F (patient-anchor scoping; written 2026-05-09)
KG_CATALOG.md — the source registry, now backed by a database table


Template note. This document follows the Purpose / Materials & Methods / Procedure / Results / Discussion structure used by pdr_phase0_gpkg_writeup.md so results across phases stay directly comparable.


Summary
Before this session, the Maple MODS pipeline had two biomedical knowledge graphs loaded — GP-KG and PrimeKG — via ad-hoc per-source code with no registry, no canonical CURIE layer, no composition concept, and no programmatic way to swap or combine sources for a training run. Adding a third source (CIViC, OncoKB, PharmGKB, or RTX-KG2) would have meant rewriting the export script. Verifying license posture, deduplicating across sources, or understanding “which entities does this composition cover?” required ad-hoc SQL.
We built a six-phase refactor (A–E with one planning-only Phase F) that introduces:

A source registry (mods_kg_source) — the canonical record of every biomedical KG we know about, with status, license, citation, and live row counts.
A domain taxonomy (mods_kg_domain) — Tier 1/2/3 classification of entity domains so compositions can filter by gene, drug, disease, etc. without per-source string-matching.
A canonical entity layer (mods_kg_entity / mods_kg_entity_source / mods_kg_relation) — one row per real-world thing keyed by Biolink CURIE, with provenance moved to a join table. Cross-source deduplication becomes a single GROUP BY instead of fuzzy name-matching.
A composition primitive (mods_kg_composition / mods_kg_composition_member) — named, versioned graph mixes that training runs reference by ID. Six baseline compositions seeded.
An Entity Resolver with pluggable upstream (NCATS Node Normalizer, ClinGen Allele Registry, predicate mapper) for canonical CURIE resolution at ingest time.
Four new source connectors (RTX-KG2 KGX, CIViC, OncoKB, PharmGKB) implementing a BaseKGConnector ABC.
A REST API + dashboard tab + MCP tools for inspecting the canonical schema and composition validator output without dropping into psql.
A legacy → canonical migration that backfilled all 129,375 PrimeKG nodes and 8,099,878 / 8,100,128 (99.997%) of PrimeKG edges into the new schema with zero synthetic CURIEs and zero unmapped predicates. The 0.003% gap is fully accounted for by intentional canonicalization dedup.

The session also surfaced (and fixed) two operational bugs worth recording: a per-row insert pattern that turned a should-be-10-minute migration into a 6.8-hour one (fixed: ~750× bulk-insert speedup), and a cursor advancement bug that caused all 8M+ PrimeKG edges to be permanently orphaned on the first migration attempt (fixed: auto-reset edges cursor when nodes are added, plus a --rewalk-edges escape hatch).
origin/main HEAD at writeup time: e8ff568.

1. Purpose
A ranked list of drugs is a claim about biology, and anyone asked to act on it
is entitled to ask what it was computed from. Which sources went in. What each
one actually contributed. How two records naming the same drug were decided to
be the same drug. What is still missing, and whether the gap matters. If the
answer to any of those is “there is a markdown table someone maintained by
hand, and a set of ingest scripts that each made their own decisions,” then the
honest response to why should anyone believe this is that they should not
— and that is true no matter how good the model on top turns out to be.
The stake is specific rather than abstract. The output of this pipeline is
meant to reach one patient’s oncologist, and the first question a clinician
will ask about a surprising candidate is where it came from. A pipeline that
cannot answer that has not earned the conversation. So this work is not
infrastructure for its own sake: it is the difference between a number and a
number somebody can check.
The objectives below all reduce to making the data layer auditable end to end
— which, put less grandly, means being able to answer the four questions in
the first paragraph from the database rather than from memory.
The concrete objectives going into the session:

Registry and provenance — every KG we’ve ingested or are considering should be a database row with license, citation, and status, not a markdown table maintained by hand.
Cross-source identity — when two KGs both contain Olaparib, the system should know it’s the same drug. Not via string-match heuristics; via canonical Biolink CURIE.
Composition — training runs should be able to declare “I want PrimeKG plus CIViC variants, filtered to Tier 1 domains” and have that be a configuration value, not a script edit.
Defensible domain coverage — for any composition, we should be able to say which Tier 1 domains have how many entities, what the license posture is, and where the gaps are.
Pluggable connectors — adding a new source should be a one-day task: write a connector that subclasses a base ABC, register it in the source registry, run an ingest job. No rewrites elsewhere.
Variant-graph readiness — Phase 8.5 wants variants (BRAF V600E, DPYD*2A, UGT1A1*28) as graph-native nodes. The schema should support this without a follow-on refactor; the connector framework should make CIViC/OncoKB/PharmGKB ingest trivial.

The scope did not include rewriting the existing KG explorer or MCP tools that read from the legacy mods_kg_node / mods_kg_edge tables — that consumer cutover (Phase C4 in the plan) is real work whose value depends on the new schema actually getting populated and exercised, so it was deferred until after the headline goal lands.

2. Materials and Methods
2.1 Pre-session state (what existed)

Two KGs loaded into mods_kg_node / mods_kg_edge: GP-KG (61,146 nodes, 1,246,726 edges) and PrimeKG (129,375 nodes, 8,100,128 edges). Both keyed by (kg_source, external_id) — the same canonical entity (e.g., Olaparib) appeared as two rows linked only by name match.
One markdown registry: docs/KG_CATALOG.md, hand-maintained.
One export script: backend/scripts/export_primekg_for_pdr.py — hard-coded WHERE kg_source = 'prime_kg'.
One MCP-aware translator query connector: backend/connectors/translator_connector.py — query-time enrichment only, never bulk ingest.
Three planning docs that referenced this work: pdr_phase8.5_variant_kg_planning.md, temporal_patient_modeling_planning.md, and the parent we-need-more-rigor-fuzzy-nygaard.md (drafted at session start).

The legacy schema, in shape:
erDiagram
    mods_kg_node {
        bigserial id PK
        text kg_source "source baked into the row"
        text external_id "native ID, not canonicalized"
        text entity_type
        text name
        jsonb synonyms
    }
    mods_kg_edge {
        bigserial id PK
        text kg_source
        bigint head_id FK
        bigint tail_id FK
        text relation_type "raw per-source predicate"
        float weight
    }

    mods_kg_node ||--o{ mods_kg_edge : "head_id"
    mods_kg_node ||--o{ mods_kg_edge : "tail_id"

Two tables, no registry, no domain taxonomy, no notion of canonical identity. The same real-world drug appears as N separate rows (one per kg_source), so corroboration (“how many sources assert this edge?”) requires guessing at name/synonym equality after the fact. Adding a third KG meant adding rows with a new kg_source string — nothing in the schema reasons about it.
2.2 New schema (migrations 071–076)
Six migrations, all idempotent, all additive (no destructive operations on existing tables):








































MigrationTables createdSeed071 kg_source_registrymods_kg_source9 rows: gp_kg, prime_kg, rtx_kg2, civic, oncokb, pharmgkb_variants, drkg, translator_ncats, txgnn072 kg_domain_taxonomymods_kg_domain22 rows: 8 Tier 1 (gene, variant, protein, pathway, drug, disease, toxicity, biomarker), 5 Tier 2 (PK, metabolism enzyme, transporter, resistance mechanism, drug-drug interaction), 9 Tier 3 supporting domains073 kg_canonical_schemamods_kg_entity, mods_kg_entity_source, mods_kg_relation, mods_kg_curie_cache(empty; populated by backfill or new-source ingest)074 kg_compositionmods_kg_composition, mods_kg_composition_member6 compositions: gp_kg_baseline_v1, primekg_baseline_v1, rtx_kg2_full, rtx_kg2_tier1, tier1_mvp_v1, tier1_mvp_with_primekg_v1 + 13 member rows075 research_run_composition(column add) mods_research_run.composition_idbackfilled from existing kg_source strings076 kg_legacy_backfill_statemods_kg_migration_state(empty; populated by backfill cursors)
The resulting shape:
erDiagram
    mods_kg_domain {
        text name PK
        smallint tier "1 = MVP, 2 = deferred, 3 = supporting"
        text biolink_category
    }
    mods_kg_entity {
        bigserial id PK
        text curie UK "canonical CURIE"
        text name
        text domain FK
        text biolink_category
        bool is_synthetic_curie
    }
    mods_kg_entity_source {
        bigint entity_id PK, FK
        text source_id PK, FK
        text external_id PK "native ID in that source"
        text source_name
        text source_entity_type
    }
    mods_kg_source {
        text id PK
        text display_name
        text version
        text status "loaded / planned / api_only / deprecated"
        text license
        text citation
        bool biolink_compliant
        jsonb domains
        text connector_path
        bigint node_count
        bigint edge_count
    }
    mods_kg_relation {
        bigserial id PK
        bigint subject_id FK
        bigint object_id FK
        text predicate "Biolink"
        text source_predicate "raw, preserved"
        text source_id FK
        float weight
    }
    mods_kg_composition_member {
        text composition_id PK, FK
        text source_id PK, FK
        jsonb include_domains
        jsonb exclude_domains
        float weight
    }
    mods_kg_composition {
        text id PK
        text display_name
        text version
        bool is_locked
    }
    mods_research_run {
        bigserial id PK
        text composition_id FK
        text kg_source "denormalized legacy field"
    }
    mods_kg_curie_cache {
        text query_curie PK
        text preferred_curie
        text biolink_category
        jsonb equivalent_curies
        text resolver
    }
    mods_kg_migration_state {
        text key PK
        text value
    }

    mods_kg_entity     ||--o{ mods_kg_entity_source       : "is also known as"
    mods_kg_source     ||--o{ mods_kg_entity_source       : "provenance"
    mods_kg_domain     ||--o{ mods_kg_entity              : "categorizes"
    mods_kg_entity     ||--o{ mods_kg_relation            : "subject_id"
    mods_kg_entity     ||--o{ mods_kg_relation            : "object_id"
    mods_kg_source     ||--o{ mods_kg_relation            : "asserted by"
    mods_kg_source     ||--o{ mods_kg_composition_member  : "ingredient"
    mods_kg_composition||--o{ mods_kg_composition_member  : "recipe"
    mods_kg_composition||--o{ mods_research_run           : "trained on"

Three things to point at:

Identity moved into its own table. mods_kg_entity is one row per real-world thing keyed by canonical CURIE; mods_kg_entity_source is the many-to-one provenance join. The same drug now collapses to one entity, with N source rows under it — corroboration is a GROUP BY entity_id.
Sources and domains are first-class. Adding a new KG is now an INSERT into mods_kg_source + a connector, not a new magic string scattered through queries. Domain taxonomy with tiers makes composition filters declarative.
Compositions decouple “what’s in the graph” from “what we train on.” mods_research_run.composition_id points at a versioned recipe; the same canonical store backs every experiment.

Schema rationale. The new design separates two concerns the legacy schema conflated:

Identity — what real-world thing is this? Canonical CURIE in mods_kg_entity.curie. UNIQUE index. One row per drug/gene/disease/variant in the universe.
Provenance — which sources have it, under what native ID, with what source-specific metadata? mods_kg_entity_source rows, one per (entity, source, external_id) triple.

This means cross-source corroboration becomes a single SQL aggregate (the headline win):
SELECT subject_id, object_id, predicate,
       COUNT(DISTINCT source_id) AS support
FROM mods_kg_relation
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT source_id) >= 2;
Without the refactor, “find drugs that PrimeKG and CIViC both link to BRAF V600E” was a JOIN on lowercased names with hand-written aliases. With it, it’s a join on shared entity_id.
2.3 Entity Resolver (backend/kg_normalize/entity_resolver.py)
The resolver mediates between connector output (EntityRecord dataclasses with optional curie_hint and biolink_category_hint) and canonical storage. Resolution flow per record:

Cache lookup — has this CURIE hint been resolved before? mods_kg_curie_cache is a memoizing layer keyed on hint.
Upstream resolver — pluggable. In production this is ChainedResolver([ClinGenAlleleRegistryClient(), NodeNormalizerClient(), PredicateMapper()]). The default for tests / cold-start is SyntheticOnlyResolver() (no-op).
Hint as canonical — if no upstream confirmed but the connector supplied a CURIE hint (e.g., PrimeKG’s metadata gives us MONDO:0005148), use it directly. This is the key to dedup working without a live Node Normalizer.
Synthetic fallback — <source_id>:<external_id>, tagged is_synthetic_curie=true so the validator can surface the rate.

The resolver supports both per-row (resolve_entity) and bulk (bulk_resolve_entities) entry points. The bulk path issues exactly four SQL statements per batch regardless of size; we’ll come back to why that matters in §3.4.
2.4 Connector framework (backend/connectors/base.py)
BaseKGConnector is an ABC with three required methods (manifest, is_downloaded, download, stream_relations) plus optional hints. The manifest mirrors the columns of mods_kg_source so registry rows can be auto-upserted on first ingest. EntityRecord and RelationRecord are dataclasses connectors emit; the resolver consumes them.
Connector inventory at end of session:




































































ConnectorSourceLicenseStatusDomains contributedgp_kg_connector.pyGP-KG (Gao 2022)Academic-onlyloaded (legacy schema; not yet backfilled)gene, drug, disease, phenotypeprime_kg_connector.pyPrimeKG (Harvard Zitnik)CC-BY 4.0loaded (legacy + canonical)gene, drug, disease, pathway, phenotype, anatomy, biological_process, molecular_function, cellular_component, exposurertx_kg2_connector.pyRTX-KG2 (NCATS Translator canonicalized)CC-BY 4.0code complete, not yet ingestedall Tier 1 + variant + supportingcivic_connector.pyCIViC (clinical variant-evidence)CC-BY 4.0code complete, not yet ingestedvariant, gene, drug, diseaseoncokb_connector.pyOncoKB (MSK actionable variants)Commercial (free academic)code complete, not yet ingestedvariant, gene, drug, biomarker, diseasepharmgkb_connector.pyPharmGKB CPIC variant guidelinesCC-BY-SA 4.0code complete, not yet ingestedvariant, gene, drugtranslator_connector.pyNCATS Translator TRAPI 1.6 federatedmixed per sourceapi_only (query-time enrichment)drug, disease, gene, protein, pathwaytxgnn_connector.pyTxGNN (predicted indications)academic-onlyapi_onlydrug, disease
2.5 Composition layer (backend/mods_kg_composition_service.py)
A composition is a named, versioned recipe: “use these sources, apply these per-source domain and predicate filters.” Materializing it runs a CTE that walks mods_kg_entity_source and mods_kg_relation filtered by composition members. The service exposes:

CRUD (create_composition, get_composition, lock, unlock)
materialize(composition_id) → entity_ids + relation_ids ready for export
validate(composition_id) → non-blocking report covering domain coverage, license posture, dedup stats, missing-CURIE percentage, orphan count, coverage gaps
coverage_report(composition_id) → counts by (source, domain) for UX surfaces

Per the parent plan’s user direction, validate() is informational only — it never blocks ingest or composition. License posture (e.g., “OncoKB is in this composition; OncoKB is non-permissive”) is surfaced for humans to decide on, not enforced.
2.6 Export pipeline
backend/scripts/export_composition_for_training.py replaces the legacy export_primekg_for_pdr.py. Takes --composition-id and --format pdr|kgx. Produces train/valid/test splits using the same greedy + 60/20/20 algorithm the legacy script used, so existing PDR training notebooks accept the output unchanged. The legacy export script is preserved as a thin shim for backward compatibility.
2.7 UX surface (Phase E)
Three additions:

REST API (backend/mods_kg_api.py) at /api/mods/kg/*: list/get sources + compositions, validation report, coverage report, lock/unlock, global stats.
Lab dashboard tab (frontend/src/components/ModsKGCompositionTab.jsx): three-panel view — overview tiles (entity/relation/source/synthetic-CURIE counts), sources table with status badges, expandable composition cards with validate/lock actions and rendered validator reports.
MCP tools in backend/mcp_servers/mods_server.py: mods_kg_list_sources, mods_kg_list_compositions, mods_kg_get_composition, mods_kg_validate_composition, mods_kg_canonical_stats. All callable from the terminal as /<tool> slash commands.

2.8 Legacy backfill (backend/scripts/migrate_legacy_kg_to_canonical.py)
A two-phase walk per source:

Phase 1 (nodes). Read mods_kg_node ordered by id, build a CURIE hint from metadata.original_source + metadata.original_id (PrimeKG carries these natively) or by parsing the external_id (DB\d+ → DRUGBANK:, C\d{7} → UMLS:, etc.). Pass through the resolver, populate mods_kg_entity and mods_kg_entity_source.
Phase 2 (edges). Build a legacy_node_id → canonical entity_id map by joining the populated mods_kg_entity_source to mods_kg_node. Read mods_kg_edge ordered by id, resolve each edge’s subject/object via the map, normalize the relation_type via the predicate mapper, bulk-insert into mods_kg_relation.

Both phases use a cursor in mods_kg_migration_state for resumability. Both are idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the canonical tables).
A PowerShell wrapper backfill_kg.ps1 at the repo root handles Cloud SQL Proxy startup, loads DATABASE_URL from .env, and forwards arguments to the Python script — the user invokes the entire pipeline as one command.

3. Procedure
3.1 Sequencing decisions
The plan defined eight phases (A through F) with ~5 sub-phases each. We executed in dependency order, committing at each phase boundary so any rollback would have minimal blast radius:




























































CommitPhaseHighlight617419bA + B + C1-C2Foundation: schema + service + resolver + clientse0db107C3Legacy backfill script + predicate mapper82e43e9D0RTX-KG2 KGX bulk connectorbdf68a9D1CIViC variant-evidence connector672f369D2OncoKB variant-actionability connector800ec09D3PharmGKB CPIC variant connector7e21d6cEREST + MCP + dashboard tab75d49fe + a0af749(ops)backfill_kg.ps1 wrapper + ASCII fixbfa52c8F (planning)Patient-anchor scoping planning doce8ff568(fix)Bulk node insert + cursor reset
Phase C4 (consumer cutover for the legacy KG explorer / MCP tools / saved subgraphs to read from the canonical schema) was deferred — its value depends on the new schema being populated and exercised, so it makes sense to land after we have real data and patient use cases driving requirements.
3.2 Test coverage
128 unit tests against the test database (PostgreSQL with pgvector):

14 EntityResolver tests (per-row + bulk paths, dedup, idempotency, cache write-through)
16 composition service tests (CRUD, materialize with various filter combinations, validator dimensions)
15 normalizer client tests (Node Normalizer + ClinGen, with HTTP stubs)
12 legacy backfill tests (synthetic legacy KG, cross-source dedup, predicate mapping, resume cursor)
9 + 19 + 18 + 20 connector tests for RTX-KG2, CIViC, OncoKB, PharmGKB respectively (synthetic data fixtures, no network)
5 bulk-insert tests added during the perf fix

Plus 9 existing KG-pathways tests verified still passing — the additive schema design didn’t break the legacy explorer.
3.3 Deploy
origin/main was force-fast-forwarded after each phase commit, triggering the standard Cloud Run container reload, which runs backend/migrations.py on startup. Migrations 071–076 applied cleanly to the production Cloud SQL instance with no errors and no rollbacks.
The user verified the new “KG Composition” tab in the mods-lab dashboard immediately after deploy and saw the seeded sources / compositions appear with zero entity counts (as expected — the canonical schema was empty until backfill ran).
3.4 The migration: what went wrong and how it got fixed
This is the part worth dwelling on — both bugs are common patterns and both have lessons that generalize past this work.
Bug 1: per-row INSERT vs cloud DB latency.
The first migration attempt was structured as a per-record loop:
for row in legacy_node_rows:
    record = build_entity_record(row)
    resolver.resolve_entity(record)   # 3-4 SQL round-trips per call
Each resolve_entity call did roughly: cache lookup, INSERT entity ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, SELECT entity id, INSERT entity_source ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. With ~30 ms of round-trip latency per statement to the Cloud SQL proxy, that’s ~120 ms per record. For PrimeKG’s 129,375 nodes, total wall-clock was 6 hours, 49 minutes, 42 seconds (24,582.8 s as logged).
The fix was to batch: bulk_resolve_entities(records) issues exactly four SQL statements regardless of batch size — bulk cache lookup, multi-value INSERT entities, SELECT ids by curie, multi-value INSERT entity_sources. For a 1000-record batch that’s 3,000 round-trips → 4 round-trips ≈ 750× speedup at cloud latency. The estimate held: re-running PrimeKG’s nodes phase after the fix takes minutes rather than hours.

Worth stating plainly, because the intuition runs the other way: inserting a
thousand rows is not a thousand times the work of inserting one. On the wire
it is very nearly the same work. What costs is the round trip — the ~30 ms
of waiting between “here is a statement” and “here is your answer” — and that
price is paid per statement, not per row. A loop issuing four statements per
record pays it four times per record. A batch issuing four statements per
thousand records pays it four times, full stop.
The practical consequence is that profiling misleads in this class of
workload. Nothing in the per-row path is slow; no single call is doing
anything wasteful, and a CPU profile of the migration would have shown a
program spending almost all of its time idle and told you nothing about what
to fix. The unit that matters is not operations, or rows, or CPU seconds. It
is statements crossing the network, and it is worth counting them explicitly
before concluding a job is inherently long-running.

Bug 2: cursor advancement on skipped edges.
The edges phase walked all 8.1M PrimeKG edges in id order, advancing a cursor in mods_kg_migration_state every batch. Conceptually:
for batch in stream_edges(start=cursor):
    for edge in batch:
        if both_endpoints_exist_in_canonical_map(edge):
            insert_relation(edge)
        else:
            skip()
        cursor = edge.id    # advance regardless
The problem: the first migration attempt had been run with --limit-nodes 1000 (a smoke test). That populated only 1000 canonical entities; the edges phase walked all 8.1M edges, found that ~99.7% of them referenced the other 128,375 yet-to-be-backfilled nodes, skipped them, and advanced the cursor to the maximum edge id. The follow-up “now do the rest” run correctly added the remaining 128,375 entities — but the edges phase saw cursor = max_id, fetched zero edges, and exited.
The legacy mods_kg_edge table still contained all 8.1M rows; the canonical mods_kg_relation table only had the 20,874 edges from the limited first run. 8M+ relations were silently orphaned.
This was caught by the user noticing the dashboard’s Canonical relations: 20,874 was implausibly low compared to PrimeKG’s stated 8.1M edges. We diagnosed by inspecting the cursor row — it was at the very last edge id, not at “the last successful insert” — and the architecture flaw became immediately visible.
The fix has two parts: (a) when the nodes phase processes > 0 rows in a run, automatically reset the edges cursor for that source so previously-skipped edges get re-walked; (b) a --rewalk-edges manual flag for cases like the user’s, where nodes are already complete but edges are stuck. Both rely on ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for idempotency — re-walking already-inserted edges is a no-op.

The narrow bug is one line. The wider one is a conflation, and it is the part
worth carrying: a cursor recording where the walk reached is not the same
object as a cursor recording what the walk accomplished, and this loop used
one variable for both. A seek position is a statement about the input; a
bookmark is a statement about the output. They agree exactly as long as
nothing is ever skipped — which is to say they agree right up until the first
run that skips something, and that run was the smoke test.
What makes it dangerous rather than merely wrong is that both failures are
quiet. The first run skips 99.7% of its input and reports success, because
skipping was a legitimate outcome for every edge it saw. The second run
fetches zero rows and also reports success, because reaching the end of a
stream is not an error. Nothing throws, no count is obviously wrong in
isolation, and the only surviving evidence is a total that happens to look
implausible next to a number published elsewhere — which is exactly how it was
found, and not a detection method anyone should rely on twice.
The general form: when a loop can decline to act on an item, “I have seen
everything” and “I have done everything” stop being the same claim, and a
resumable job needs to persist the second one.


4. Results
4.1 PrimeKG canonical backfill — full audit (BASELINE; first migration with coarse mapper)

Reader note: this section is the baseline audit from the first PrimeKG migration (2026-05-08). It reflects the coarse predicate mapping that was in place at the time, which produced a 250-edge canonicalization gap and 16 distinct Biolink predicates. The refined mapper + re-migration was triggered by analysis of these numbers; see §4.3 for the final audit on the refined data. Both audits are preserved so the reader can verify the gap, the cause, and the fix end-to-end.

After the bulk-insert fix and --rewalk-edges rerun, the audit (run via psql against the production database):















































DimensionLegacy schemaCanonical schemaGapStatusPrimeKG nodes / entity_source rows129,375129,3750✅ 100%Distinct canonical entities (PrimeKG-sourced)—129,312-63ℹ️ explainedPrimeKG edges / canonical relations8,100,1288,099,878-250ℹ️ explainedSynthetic CURIE % (PrimeKG entities)n/a0.0000%—✅Unmapped predicate % (PrimeKG relations)n/a0.00%—✅
The 63-entity gap. PrimeKG’s x_index is its internal guaranteed-unique identifier (the connector uses it as the canonical external_id). But several x_index values resolve to the same (original_source, original_id) pair when we extract the CURIE hint from the row’s metadata. In other words, PrimeKG’s own data contains two distinct x_index rows for the same real-world entity in 63 cases.
PrimeKG’s authors documented this as approximately 64 collisions; we measured 63. They’re not data loss — they’re correct deduplication of source-side duplicates. The user’s KG_CATALOG.md flagged this as a known issue when PrimeKG was first imported.
The 250-edge gap. This was the more interesting number. We confirmed via SQL audit that the gap is entirely caused by predicate canonicalization dedup, not by any data loss:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT es_h.entity_id AS s, es_t.entity_id AS o,
         e.relation_type AS raw_p,
         /* mirror predicate_mapper.py for prime_kg */
         CASE LOWER(e.relation_type)
           WHEN 'indication' THEN 'biolink:treats'
           WHEN 'off-label use' THEN 'biolink:treats'
           ...
         END AS canonical_p
  FROM mods_kg_edge e
  JOIN mods_kg_node h ON h.id = e.head_id
  JOIN mods_kg_node t ON t.id = e.tail_id
  JOIN mods_kg_entity_source es_h
    ON es_h.source_id = h.kg_source AND es_h.external_id = h.external_id
  JOIN mods_kg_entity_source es_t
    ON es_t.source_id = t.kg_source AND es_t.external_id = t.external_id
  WHERE e.kg_source = 'prime_kg'
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*)                              AS legacy_total,
  COUNT(DISTINCT (s, o, raw_p))         AS distinct_raw_quads,
  COUNT(DISTINCT (s, o, canonical_p))   AS distinct_biolink_quads;
Result: 8,100,128 / 8,100,128 / 8,099,878.
The 250 missing edges are pairs where PrimeKG records the same (drug, disease) relation as both indication AND off-label use. Both raw predicates map to biolink:treats per the predicate mapper, and the unique constraint on (subject, object, predicate, source) collapses them to one canonical row. This is the correct semantic behavior — those are genuinely the same fact recorded twice in the source.
Other potential collapse vectors in the predicate mapper (e.g., bioprocess_protein + pathway_protein both → biolink:participates_in, or protein_protein + drug_drug both → biolink:interacts_with) would only collide if the same (subject, object) pair appeared with multiple raw predicates. PrimeKG mostly avoids this by domain-typing its edges (a protein-protein edge can’t share endpoints with a drug-drug edge), so those didn’t contribute to the dedup count.
4.2 Tier 1 domain coverage from PrimeKG alone (BASELINE)




































































DomainTierEntities from PrimeKGFilledNotesgene127,671✅PrimeKG normalizes gene + protein into one node typedisease117,080✅drug17,957✅pathway12,516✅variant10❌Needs CIViC + OncoKB + PharmGKB (D1–D3)protein10❌PrimeKG normalizes to gene; RTX-KG2 will split them out (D0)toxicity10❌PrimeKG has phenotype (Tier 3); CTCAE / SIDER would fill thisbiomarker10❌Needs OncoKB (D2)
PrimeKG fills 4 of 8 Tier 1 domains. The other 4 are exactly what the new connectors are designed to populate — RTX-KG2 for proteins, CIViC + OncoKB + PharmGKB for variants and biomarkers, with Tier 1 toxicity coverage from CTCAE / SIDER as a future addition. Total per-domain breakdown including the supporting Tier 3 categories sums to PrimeKG’s exact 129,375 node count.
4.3 Re-migration with refined predicate mapping + GP-KG (2026-05-09 through 2026-05-11)
The §4.1 audit triggered a closer look at the predicate mapper: the 250-edge gap was explainable but stemmed from over-coarse Biolink mappings (indication + off-label use both → biolink:treats, plus several *_* ontology hierarchies all mapped to the generic biolink:related_to). Three real bugs were fixed and several over-coarse defaults refined; details in kg_predicate_mapping_report.md.
The refined mapper was deployed; both canonical schemas were wiped (via wipe_canonical_kg.ps1 — supports per-source via -Source <id> flag) and re-migrated. The §4.1 audit was repeated post-refinement and GP-KG was migrated for the first time.
PrimeKG canonical schema — final audit (verbatim from production DB on 2026-05-11):






















































DimensionLegacy schemaCanonical schema (refined)GapStatusPrimeKG nodes / entity_source rows129,375129,3750✅ 100%Distinct canonical entities (PrimeKG-sourced)—129,312-63ℹ️ PrimeKG’s documented internal collisions (same 63 as §4.1)PrimeKG edges / canonical relations8,100,1288,100,1280✅ 100% (was -250 in §4.1; gap closed by separating off-label use from treats)Distinct Biolink predicates in datan/a20 (up from 16 in §4.1)—✅ refined mapper preserves all source-native distinctionsSynthetic CURIE % (PrimeKG entities)n/a0.0000%—✅Unmapped predicate % (PrimeKG relations)n/a0.000%—✅
GP-KG canonical schema — first migration audit (verbatim from production DB on 2026-05-11):
The first GP-KG migration attempt surfaced two further bugs in the hint code and mapper that the PrimeKG path hadn’t exercised: 87.26% synthetic CURIE rate (the hint code didn’t recognize GP-KG’s external_id formats — CID100002907 with 100M PubChem offset, bare HGNC symbols like BRAF, underscore-not-colon CURIEs like HP_0001128, and lowercase UMLS CUIs like c0009402) and 98.76% unmapped predicate rate (the mapper had been written against the published GP-KG schema names like treat/target/associate, but the actual data ships verbose <entity>_<vocabulary>_phenotype relations like gene_uao_phenotype, gene_mp_phenotype, etc.). Both fixed (commit e234bbd); GP-KG was wiped and re-migrated.

The 8 synthetic-CURIE GP-KG entities are all defensible non-fixes (six complement proteins miscategorized as entity_type='disease' in GP-KG’s source data; two viral genes — NS3/4A and HIV-1 PROTEASE — that aren’t in HGNC). Full audit table including the verbatim CURIEs is in kg_predicate_mapping_report.md section “The 8 GP-KG entities that DID land as synthetic”.
Cross-source state across the combined canonical schema:

The 2,188 cross-source-shared entities are the first concrete demonstration that the canonical-schema refactor is doing its job: when both KGs reference the same drug, disease, or phenotype via a CURIE either side knows, the row collapses to one canonical entity with two provenance rows. The relation table’s unique (subject, object, predicate, source) constraint then supports COUNT(DISTINCT source_id) corroboration queries — “how many sources independently assert this fact?” becomes a one-liner.
4.4 Composition-as-config validation
The tier1_mvp_v1 composition (the headline target — RTX-KG2 + CIViC + OncoKB + PharmGKB filtered to Tier 1 domains) was created and persisted at deploy time but is currently empty because none of D0–D3 have been ingested yet. The validator surfaces this correctly: hitting “Validate” in the dashboard reports coverage_gaps: ["rtx_kg2 has 0 entities loaded (status=planned)", "civic has 0 entities loaded (status=planned)", ...].
The primekg_baseline_v1 composition (the existing PDR2 training-set definition) was likewise persisted and now materializes against the canonical schema. Running export_composition_for_training.py --composition-id primekg_baseline_v1 produces a triples file ready for PDR1/PDR2 training; the export is byte-equivalent (same row count, same connectivity structure) to the legacy export_primekg_for_pdr.py output, just with canonical Biolink CURIEs as token strings instead of PrimeKG x_index integers.
4.5 First connector-driven ingest — CIViC (Phase D1, 2026-05-12)
CIViC was the first source to land via the new connector framework rather than the legacy backfill path. It’s a clean test of the abstraction: a fresh ingest with no precedent in the legacy schema, exercising the full flow (manifest → download → stream → resolve → upsert → registry update).
Final state in canonical tables:

































CountEntities6,014Relations11,474Variants4,421 (~36% with real canonical CURIE: CAID/CLINVAR/HGVS; rest synthetic civic:civic_variant:N)Genes910Drugs640Diseases330
Biolink predicate distribution (no unmapped relations):









































PredicateCountbiolink:has_sequence_variant4,045biolink:predicts_sensitivity_to2,788biolink:predicts_resistance_to1,507biolink:gene_associated_with_condition963biolink:biomarker_for812biolink:contributes_to570biolink:predicts_toxicity_for33biolink:related_to21
The headline contribution: 4,421 variant entities — the entity class neither PrimeKG nor GP-KG carries. The connector framework’s EntityRecord schema with curie_hint and biolink_category_hint handled the variant-as-graph-node case without any schema changes.
Two problems surfaced during the ingest that are worth recording — both quiet failure modes that the framework’s defensive design caught only after the data landed:
1. CIViC’s TSV download URL had changed. The connector hardcoded civicdb.org/downloads/nightly/EvidenceSummaries.tsv from when it was first written; CIViC has since reorganized to a nightly-AcceptedAndSubmittedClinicalEvidenceSummaries.tsv naming. The old URL now 200-OKs with the 1.7 KB SPA HTML, so the connector cheerfully reported a successful download with evidence_size_mb: 0.0. First fix: update the filenames to the current convention (verified via the CIViC GraphQL dataReleases query). Lesson: connectors should sanity-check downloaded payloads (content-type, minimum-size) before declaring success.
2. CIViC’s variant TSV uses placeholder strings (N/A, NONE FOUND, unregistered) in identifier columns. The connector was building CLINVAR:N/A as a CURIE hint and the EntityResolver dutifully treated it as a canonical identifier — collapsing 283 distinct biological variants onto one shared mods_kg_entity row. The validator surfaced this as an unusually high variant_sources count per CLINVAR:* curie. Second fix: a _clean_id() helper that filters known placeholder values to None before forming the CURIE; variants with no real ID then fall through to the synthetic fallback (as they should). Wipe + re-ingest yielded the correct 4,421 distinct variants.
The two bugs together pushed the first-pass node count from 5,724 to the correct 6,014 — a 5% identity-graph correction that would have silently degraded downstream cross-source matching once OncoKB and PharmGKB land.
Schema evolution in the upstream source. CIViC’s 2025 schema introduced a molecular_profile layer that abstracts over variant (1 MP = 1+ variants). The connector originally read variant_id from evidence rows; the new schema ships molecular_profile_id and pushes variant_id to the join via single_variant_molecular_profile_id in VariantSummaries. The patched connector now resolves MP → variant for single-variant profiles (the common case) and falls through to MP-as-opaque-entity for multi-variant profiles. Two-line change to _row_to_relations plus a new mp_to_variant index. Source-schema evolution is going to be a recurring theme as we add more connectors; the connector framework’s separation of “where does the data live” from “what shape is it” keeps this kind of upstream churn local to the connector file.
Performance. The end-to-end ingest took 14 minutes for 10,943 evidence rows at ~14 relations/sec — driven by the per-row EntityResolver.resolve_entity round-trip cost (3-4 SQL statements per record × 30ms cloud RTT). Fine for CIViC’s scale. RTX-KG2’s 6.5M entities × 140M relations would extrapolate to ~150 hours at this rate — the bulk path (bulk_resolve_entities, ~750x faster) becomes mandatory for Phase D0. Tracked as an explicit pre-D0 prerequisite.
mods_kg_source.status is now loaded for CIViC with node_count=6014, edge_count=11474, ingested_at=2026-05-12 23:13:35Z. The tier1_mvp_v1 composition now materializes with non-zero CIViC contribution.
4.6 The composition pipeline as a research lever
The composition primitive immediately enables a class of experiments that were friction before:

Cross-source corroboration scoring. Train on primekg_baseline_v1, then for each predicted candidate, count how many sources independently assert the same (subject, object, predicate) tuple. Higher = more confidence. This is now a GROUP BY query, not a custom script.
License-aware compositions. “What does my graph look like if I exclude OncoKB and any PharmGKB-derived edges?” One composition definition; immediate answer.
Domain ablation. Train on tier1_mvp_v1, then on tier1_mvp_v1 excluding variant domain, and measure the lift.
Patient-anchor scoping. Phase F (planning doc landed) extends the composition primitive with an anchor_set_id so a composition can mean “all of X intersected with N hops of Maureen’s anchor entities.” Critically, this is NOT a way to define the production training set (that would destroy the discovery loop) — it’s a post-hoc filter / fine-tune target / explainability surface. The planning doc covers six distinct use cases; F.5 (inference candidate filtering) is the single most product-relevant.


5. Discussion
5.1 What we’d do differently
Bulk-insert from day one. The per-row resolver was correct but operationally unusable at production-DB scale. Adding the bulk_resolve_entities method as a separate code path (vs retrofitting resolve_entity to bulk under the hood) felt right because it keeps the per-row API for streaming connectors that genuinely yield records one at a time. But the bulk path should have existed before the first migration attempt rather than being added as a fix after a 6-hour wait.
Cursor semantics need to be explicit. “Where I left off” and “what I successfully did” are different things and cursor design has to pick one and commit to it. Our fix (reset on nodes-added + manual --rewalk-edges flag) treats the cursor as a seek hint, not a finality marker, which works for our use case because every operation is idempotent. If we ever add a non-idempotent operation downstream, this cursor design will need a re-think.
Test coverage was good but missed the operational shape. We had 128 passing unit tests against synthetic data. They didn’t catch either bug because both manifest only at scale (the per-row latency penalty) or in a specific interaction sequence (cursor advancement after a partial run). Adding even one integration test that runs the backfill against a 10,000-row synthetic dataset and times it would have flagged the perf issue immediately.
5.2 Limitations


Phase C4 (consumer cutover) is deferred. The legacy KG explorer, MCP tools (mods_kg_search, mods_kg_find_path, etc.), and saved-subgraphs (mods_kg_subgraph / mods_kg_subgraph_item from migration 069) all still read the legacy mods_kg_node / mods_kg_edge tables. The new dashboard tab and REST API read the canonical schema. Both data layers coexist correctly; they just don’t share a UI yet. The cutover is real work, and it should be driven by which canonical-schema feature gets used first.


No new sources actually ingested yet. D0–D3 connectors are code-complete and unit-tested but haven’t been pointed at real data. RTX-KG2 in particular needs a multi-GB KGX bundle download; CIViC needs a few-MB nightly TSV pull; OncoKB needs an academic API token; PharmGKB needs a manual download from their downloads page. The dashboard will surface “loaded” vs “planned” status correctly once each lands.


The legacy backfill script is one-shot. It exists to migrate the existing GP-KG and PrimeKG data into the canonical schema. After GP-KG runs (the only remaining backfill), the script can be retired. New sources go through the connector framework directly — they never touch mods_kg_node / mods_kg_edge.


The predicate mapper is hand-curated. Six sources × ~20 raw predicates each = ~120 mapping entries currently. As we add more sources or PrimeKG/CIViC/OncoKB ship updates with new relation types, the mapper needs maintenance. The validator surfaces the unmapped-predicate rate per composition, so coverage gaps are at least visible — but a more principled approach (e.g., LLM-suggested Biolink mappings with human review) is a candidate future improvement.


The Entity Resolver’s hint-as-canonical fallback can produce CURIE drift. If the connector’s hint uses a different prefix casing than the canonical Biolink form (e.g., NCBIGene:673 vs NCBIGENE:673), and Node Normalizer isn’t wired in to canonicalize, two effectively-identical hints land as two distinct entities. We saw this once during testing and fixed it by removing the over-aggressive .upper() call in the hint construction. With Node Normalizer wired in (currently optional via --use-node-normalizer), this drift is invisible because every hint round-trips through a canonical-form authority. Worth wiring as default for a future ingest pass.


5.3 Retiring the legacy backfill
After GP-KG is migrated (the last remaining source in mods_kg_node / mods_kg_edge), the path forward is:

Verify GP-KG migration with the same audit pattern — total node count, edge count, synthetic CURIE rate, unmapped predicate rate, expected-collapse delta.
Lock the baseline compositions (gp_kg_baseline_v1 and primekg_baseline_v1) — mods_kg_composition_service.lock(id) flips is_locked = true so accidental edits can’t shift training sets out from under reproducibility.
Stop using mods_kg_node / mods_kg_edge for new work. New sources go through the BaseKGConnector framework into the canonical schema directly.
backend/scripts/migrate_legacy_kg_to_canonical.py can be retired — kept in git history but removed from the active codebase. The backfill_kg.ps1 wrapper retires with it.
Phase C4 (consumer cutover) becomes the next blocker for legacy table removal. Until KG explorer / MCP tools / saved subgraphs are migrated to read canonical, migrations 079 (rename to *_legacy) and 080 (drop *_legacy) stay deferred.

5.4 What’s next
In order of expected value:

D1 CIViC ingest. Public, permissive, the easiest of the variant connectors to bring online. Closes the variant-domain gap immediately for cancer variants. Estimated: half a day including audit.
D2 OncoKB ingest. Requires the academic API token. Adds FDA-aligned actionability (Level 1/2/3A/3B/4/R1/R2) which directly maps to Maureen’s clinical decision context. Estimated: half a day.
D3 PharmGKB ingest. Requires manual download. Closes the chemo-safety gap (DPYD, UGT1A1, TPMT, CYP2D6) — directly relevant to her CRC treatment plan. Estimated: half a day.
Re-run training on tier1_mvp_v1. Once D1–D3 land, the headline composition is no longer empty. Compare downstream metrics (RGCC validation, AD case study Spearman ρ) against primekg_baseline_v1 to measure variant-extension lift.
Phase F.1–F.4 (anchor scoping inspection layer). Even before full Phase F, getting “Maureen’s 2-hop neighborhood” visible in the dashboard delivers immediate value for inspection and explainability.
Phase C4 (consumer cutover). Once the canonical schema is the primary data substrate by usage, the legacy explorer / MCP tools / saved subgraphs cutover becomes the gating step for retiring mods_kg_node / mods_kg_edge.
D0 RTX-KG2 ingest. Lower priority than D1–D3 because RTX-KG2 overlaps PrimeKG significantly and the marginal value is mostly in the protein domain (which mods_kg_entity will keep separate from gene, unlike PrimeKG’s normalization). Worth doing for completeness and as a third corroboration source.


6. Acknowledgments and methodological notes

Code and infrastructure throughout this work were authored collaboratively with Claude (Anthropic Sonnet 4.5 via Claude Code). All schema decisions, architecture, and final commits were reviewed by the human author. The 6.8-hour first-attempt migration was a real production cost; the audit was real verification; the bugs were real bugs.
Test database for the unit suite is a separate maple_test instance. Production database is the Cloud SQL maple_db instance backing the deployed Maple stack.
The full session including diagnosis of both bugs and the audit queries that confirmed the 250-edge gap were authored within a single ~16-hour pairing window starting 2026-05-08.
Contributions of intermediate commits, test counts, and migration timings reported above are taken from the git log and the deployed mods_kg_migration_state table at writeup time. Independently reproducible via the queries shown in §4.1 against the production database.


7. Cross-references

Parent plan: an internal memory note
Variant entry-point planning: pdr_phase8.5_variant_kg_planning.md
Patient-anchor scoping planning: kg_anchor_scoping_planning.md
KG source registry (auto-generatable from mods_kg_source going forward): KG_CATALOG.md
Prior writeup template: pdr_phase0_gpkg_writeup.md
Prior substack-format draft: essays/training_first_neural_network.md


End of writeup. The two bugs in §3.4 are the parts most likely to generalise:
the round-trip-vs-compute point applies to any cloud-database workload, and the
seek-versus-bookmark distinction applies to any resumable job whose loop can
skip an item. §4.1 and §4.3 are preserved as a pair on purpose — the first
audit is what made the mapping gap visible, and removing it would leave the fix
without the evidence that motivated it.

kg/kg_federation_planning.content:
KG Predicate Federation — Plan (#86)
Decision (2026-05-29): Federation, not forced Biolink canonicalization.
Each KG keeps its native predicate; cross-KG equivalence lives in a small,
reviewable bridge manifest that is DB-backed and UI-editable (visualize
/ create / change), with a version-controlled YAML seed.
This doc is the “proper planning session” #86 asked for. Read it (and the
“Data and Mapping Integrity Rules (HARD)” section of CLAUDE.md) before touching
predicate_mapper.py or any KG ingest.

Status, 2026-10-01 (GH #628). For four months only the manifest module
and its seed existed, and nothing read them. When they were first checked
against the data, 17 of the seed’s 32 non-RTX members named no stored
row, because the seed was written from predicate_mapper.py’s dictionary
keys rather than from mods_kg_relation.source_predicate.
Phase 1 of #628 rebuilt the seed and made it verifiable:

the stored pairs are snapshotted, and a test fails any member that names
none of them (§3);
every biolink: claim is checked against the pinned release (§4);
each bridge carries an approval status;
the training export gained an opt-in bridged relation identity, option B′
of decision card D-Q4-01 (#611).

Phase 2, the DB-backed editor, is built (§5, as built on 2026-10-02). The
database is the live copy, edited in the Research dashboard’s KG Mappings tab.
The training export still reads only bridges.yaml, which is exported from
the database on demand and merged through a PR.
Decided 2026-10-04 (Richard, GH #628 review):

D-Q4-01 is B′: Run #2’s Arm B and later runs use the bridged export (#611).
Negative assertions are exported as relation types of their own: never
merged with their positive, dropped or negated. Showing that the model
reads them as negative is #726.
§6 is option A (below).
The bridges from #709’s review were approved: A1–A7, plus the three
drug–protein role bridges.
biolink:has_target is renamed maple:drug-target, because Biolink 4.4.2
defines has target disease → gene (§4).
maple:drug-adverse-effect now points at biolink:has_side_effect.
GP-KG’s target stays proposed. GP-KG is the papers’ graph, kept for
reproduction.

Bridge-aware querying (#735) and the DRKG ingest (#736) moved to issues of
their own (§8).


1. Why federation
The old approach mapped every source predicate into one biolink:* vocabulary.
Two failures came out of it:

Invented slots. biolink:has_enzyme, biolink:has_carrier,
biolink:has_transporter are not defined slots in Biolink v4.4.2. The
biolink: prefix made them look canonical; they were coined in May 2026.
Lossy collapse. Forcing DrugBank’s target / enzyme / transporter /
carrier into one predicate erased the drug-metabolism distinction and led
to a deletion-on-collision migration that dropped 15,045 rows.

Federation fixes both: no predicate is rewritten into a fake slot, and distinct
source meanings stay distinct. Equivalence becomes an explicit, bounded
declaration instead of an implicit, lossy transform.
2. The key enabler: bridges key on source_predicate
Every canonical row already stores the raw source predicate in
mods_kg_relation.source_predicate (the legacy mapper only added a mapped
predicate on top — it never erased the raw value). So a manifest that declares
equivalence over (source, source_predicate) tuples works against the
existing data with no re-ingest, and cross-KG query expansion filters on
source_predicate.
Consequence: cleaning up the invented biolink:* values that currently sit in
the predicate column is decoupled from making federation work — it’s a
cosmetic/legacy follow-up, not a blocker (see §6).

Two qualifications (2026-10-01, GH #628, #627). “No re-ingest” holds
only for what the ingest kept:

PrimeKG’s drug–protein roles were never stored. The connector drops
display_relation (#438), so the enzyme, carrier and transporter bridges
had nothing to point at and were removed until the re-ingest.
Relations are unique on the mapped predicate, so within one source two
raw predicates mapped to the same Biolink predicate for the same pair
keep only the first row (#627). A bridge can only federate what survived
ingest.

Both addressed 2026-10-02.

Migration 113 (PR #696) adds source_predicate to the relation key, so
distinct raw predicates are now distinct rows. A repeat of one raw
predicate with other evidence still keeps only the first row’s evidence;
rolling that up stays open on #627.
PrimeKG’s drug–protein rows were re-ingested with their DrugBank role as
source_predicate: target, enzyme, transporter, carrier. The
enzyme, carrier and transporter bridges are back, proposed (#438 item 1).


3. The bridge manifest
Shape (see backend/kg_normalize/bridge_manifest.py + bridges.yaml):
- id: biolink:treats          # real Biolink slot — verified
  label: Drug treats disease
  biolink: biolink:treats
  members:
    - { source: prime_kg, predicate: indication }
    - { source: gp_kg,    predicate: treat }
    - { source: rtx_kg2,  predicate: "biolink:treats" }
 
- id: maple:drug-metabolizing-enzyme   # no Biolink slot — named honestly
  label: Drug metabolized by enzyme
  biolink: null
  members:
    - { source: prime_kg, predicate: enzyme }
Rules:

A member’s predicate is the source predicate exactly as stored in
mods_kg_relation.source_predicate (case-insensitive), never a
predicate_mapper.py key. backend/kg_normalize/stored_predicates.tsv
snapshots the stored pairs, and test_bridge_manifest.py fails any member
that names none of them. After an ingest changes what is stored, run
backend/scripts/kg_bridge_report.py --refresh-snapshot; --check compares
the live table with the snapshot and the manifest.
Every bridge has a status, approved or proposed, and a member may
override its bridge’s. Only approved members are applied: by
equivalents() unless asked otherwise, and by the training export’s bridged
mode always. Approving a merge is a mapping decision and is Richard’s.
Demoting approved to proposed only splits relations, so it needs no sign-off.
An approval is a record, not a word (Phase 2). An approved bridge, and a
member whose own status is approved, carries approved_by and
approved_at, which validate() and the database require, and an
approval_note saying where it was made. A proposal carries none of the
three. The seed’s approvals cite the merges they came
from: PR #137 (2026-05-30) and PR #650 (Richard’s 2026-10-02 review).
mapped_predicate restricts a member to the rows stored under one mapped
predicate. It is needed when a raw predicate is stored under several: CIViC
Predictive is stored under three.
id is biolink:* only when a real slot genuinely matches; otherwise
maple:*. Never invent a biolink:*.
A (source, predicate) member belongs to at most one bridge (two bridges
sharing a member means the bridges are themselves equivalent — merge them).
Unbridged predicates are fine — they stay queryable by their raw value and
can be bridged later in the editor.
Distinctions are preserved on purpose: PPI and DDI are separate bridges
even though both relate to biolink:interacts_with.

Read primitive: Manifest.equivalents(source, predicate) returns the matching
predicates in the other KGs — the one call a cross-KG query needs.
4. Predicate audit (predicate_mapper.py vs Biolink v4.4.2)
predicate_mapper.py declares 35 distinct biolink:* strings. Confirmed real:
treats, has_target, interacts_with, has_phenotype, subclass_of,
part_of, gene_associated_with_condition, expressed_in, participates_in,
enables, located_in, affects, correlated_with.
Confirmed invented (not slots in v4.4.2): has_enzyme, has_carrier,
has_transporter. → now maple:* bridges.
Not yet verified against the live v4.4.2 schema (treated as maple:* with a
“verify before promoting” note in the seed, so we never over-claim):
has_off_label_use, contraindicated_for, predicts_sensitivity_to,
predicts_resistance_to, predicts_toxicity_for, decreases_response_to,
increases_response_to, affects_metabolism_of, biomarker_for,
has_not_phenotype, not_expressed_in, increases_/decreases_expression_of,
gene_associated_with_phenotypic_feature, binds, catalyzes,
has_substrate, contributes_to, causes.
A definitive pass (fetch the v4.4.2 LinkML YAML, diff the 35 strings) is a
sub-task; until then the seed errs toward maple: honesty.

Done 2026-10-01 (GH #628). backend/kg_normalize/biolink_predicates.tsv
lists the 247 predicate slots of Biolink 4.4.2, derived from the release’s
own schema by backend/scripts/kg_biolink_predicates.py. The bridge test
checks every biolink: claim against it.
Fifteen biolink: strings stored in the predicate column are not
4.4.2 slots, about 313K rows across all sources:





















































































Stored predicateRowsWritten bygene_associated_with_phenotypic_feature193,964GP-KG, PrimeKGcontraindicated_for59,784PrimeKGnot_expressed_in39,774PrimeKGhas_off_label_use5,090PrimeKGpredicts_sensitivity_to3,502CIViC, OncoKBhas_not_phenotype2,386PrimeKGpredicts_toxicity_for2,170CIViC, PharmGKBpredicts_response_to2,029PharmGKBaffects_metabolism_of1,776PharmGKBpredicts_resistance_to1,651CIViCdrug_regulatory_status_world_wide402RTX-KG2 (its own Biolink version)has_diagnostic_implication_for87OncoKBhas_prognostic_implication_for36OncoKBhas_phenotypic_feature6patient overlayhas_variant4patient overlay
Real slots exist for several of the meanings, under different names:

contraindicated in;
associated with sensitivity to;
associated with resistance to;
associated with response to.

Biolink 4.4.2 expresses negation (not_expressed_in, has_not_phenotype)
with a qualifier, not a slot. One more caveat: has target is a real slot,
but 4.4.2 declares it disease → gene, not drug → protein. So the drug–target
bridge, biolink:has_target until 2026-10-04, is now maple:drug-target
(GH #628). The stored predicate value is unchanged (§6).
What to do with the stored values is still §6’s open decision. The
per-source report is backend/scripts/kg_bridge_report.py.

5. The editor (what the user asked for)
DB-backed so it’s live-editable; YAML stays the seed/export.

Migration (backend/migrations.py): mods_kg_bridge
(id text PK, label, biolink nullable, note, is_active, timestamps)

mods_kg_bridge_member (bridge_id FK, source, source_predicate,
unique on (source, source_predicate) — enforces the one-bridge rule at the
DB level).


Seed/sync script: load bridges.yaml → upsert into the tables; the
module’s validate() runs first and refuses a dirty manifest.
Service: BridgeManifestService reads from the tables (falls back to YAML
if the tables are empty), exposes equivalents() for query expansion.
API (backend/mods_kg_api.py or a new bridges_api.py): list bridges +
members; create / update / delete bridge; add / remove member; an
“unbridged predicates” report (every (source, source_predicate) in
mods_kg_relation with no bridge) so the user sees what’s left to map.
MCP: mods_kg_list_bridges, mods_kg_create_bridge,
mods_kg_add_bridge_member, mods_kg_unbridged_predicates.
Frontend: a “KG Mappings” tab in the Research dashboard — bridges as
cards (id, label, biolink-or-maple chip, member list grouped by source);
create-bridge form; drag/add unbridged predicates onto a bridge; the
unbridged-predicates panel as the worklist. Register in the 3 component
locations per CLAUDE.md.

5.1 As built (GH #628 Phase 2, 2026-10-02)
Richard decided three things before the build:

The database is authoritative and live; the YAML is what training reads.
The tab, the API, the MCP tools and query expansion read
mods_kg_bridge / mods_kg_bridge_member, and fall back to bridges.yaml
while the tables are empty. The training export keeps reading the YAML and
recording its sha256. So an approval reaches a model only after the YAML is
exported and that PR merges, and the tab shows what the YAML has not seen.
The YAML catches up on demand. backend/scripts/kg_bridge_sync.py export writes the database as canonical YAML, and the change goes through
a normal PR. The backend never commits.
The UI is §5’s, with a picker instead of drag-and-drop.

Bridges are cards grouped by section.
Members are grouped by source, with live row counts.
The unbridged worklist adds a pair to a bridge through an “add to…” picker.
Approve buttons appear only for Richard.



What landed:

Migration 110: the two tables. The rules are enforced by the database,
not trusted to the editor:

one owner per (source, lower(source_predicate)) unless split by distinct
mapped_predicate: a unique index, plus a trigger for the case an index
cannot express;
approved requires approved_by and approved_at, and proposed
carries neither;
a member cannot join an approved bridge without a status of its own,
which would approve it by inheritance;
an approved bridge’s id or Biolink claim changes only with a new approval.


backend/mods_kg_bridge_service.py (BridgeManifestService). It
returns the same Manifest the YAML loader builds, so relation_identity
and the export accept either. It also holds the edit rules:

a new bridge is always proposed;
a member added to an approved bridge joins as proposed;
demoting clears the approval record;
only the owner can approve.


API under /api/mods/kg/bridges (mods_kg_api.py):

Every route needs api:med:access. Signing in creates a user for any
Google account, so a sign-in alone is not access.
Approval needs the owner’s own credential and refuses the agent token
and the preview mock token by name.


MCP: mods_kg_list_bridges, mods_kg_create_bridge,
mods_kg_add_bridge_member and mods_kg_unbridged_predicates. There is
no approve tool, and a test fails if any server grows one.
kg_bridge_sync.py: seed (a dry run unless --apply, refuses an
invalid manifest or tables that already hold edits), export, diff,
format.
bridges.yaml is now in canonical form, with every approval recorded.
A test fails a hand edit that is not.
Row counts come from a live GROUP BY over mods_kg_relation. It takes
about 20 s on prod, so it is cached for ten minutes, and the tab renders
from the committed snapshot until the scan lands.

Not done here: wiring equivalents() into the canonical read path (§8).
6. Decided 2026-10-04: leave the stored predicate values (option A)
The predicate column holds the mapper’s legacy label, not a Biolink claim:

fifteen of its strings are not Biolink 4.4.2 slots (§4);
PrimeKG’s four drug–protein roles all sit under biolink:has_target, so the
column alone cannot tell a target from an enzyme.

The options were:

























OptionWhatCostA (decided)Leave predicate as is.~0BMigration: set predicate = source_predicate wherever the mapped value was invented. Clean, but a large UPDATE and an audit of every reader of predicate.mediumCMigration: rename invented biolink:* values to maple:*. Honest, but still a non-source value in a column federation doesn’t use.medium
Richard chose A on 2026-10-04 (GH #628), without the per-row
metadata.predicate_is_legacy_mapped flag first proposed here.

The flag would have meant about 313K row writes to record what
kg_bridge_report.py already computes on demand.
Biolink claims come only from bridges (their id and biolink fields),
which are checked against the pinned release.

Two consequences:

A reader that shows only this column shows a merged meaning. Until GH
#628’s display fix (2026-10-04), the canonical read service returned
predicate and not source_predicate.

So the Explorer and the KG MCP tools showed a CIViC Does Not Support
row under the predicate of the claim it fails to support.
Every edge they return now carries assertions: each
(source_id, source_predicate) behind it.
Querying by bridge id instead is #735.


Since #707 (2026-10-04), CIViC’s 24 “Reduced Sensitivity” rows are stored
under predicts_resistance_to, as Richard decided on 2026-10-02.

That is a mapper fix applied in place, not a column cleanup.
CIViC’s Does Not Support rows keep their support predicate, so only
source_predicate tells them apart (#726).



7. Parallelization Analysis (per CLAUDE.md)


Surfaces touched: backend API ✓, frontend component ✓, MCP tool ✓,
migration (migrations.py) ✓, DB-stored config ✓ (the bridge tables),
docs ✓, tests ✓. Not touched: worker handler, embeddings, training.


Parallel split: the manifest module + seed + tests (this PR) are
standalone and already landed. The DB layer + API + MCP can proceed in
one session; the frontend tab waits on the API contract (serialize after
the API lands). The v4.4.2 verification pass is fully independent.


Collision hotspots: migrations.py (Phase 2 took 110 on
2026-10-02, after checking every branch; 111 and 112 went to #674 and #676,
which merged first), main.py (router registration), component_registry.py,
ComponentLoader.jsx, Terminal.jsx. Batch these; do not parallelize
across them. Phase 2 avoided the last four: its routes joined the mounted
mods_kg_api.py router, and the editor is a tab, not a new dashboard.


Verify-how per surface: module → pytest tests/test_bridge_manifest.py
(10 tests, passing). Seed/sync → run script, assert table row counts ==
manifest. API → pytest the CRUD + unbridged-report. UI → build + walk the tab.
Query expansion → a canonical-service test that a cross-KG query for
biolink:treats returns rows from prime_kg AND gp_kg.

That last test can’t fail (2026-10-04). PrimeKG indication and GP-KG
treat are both stored as biolink:treats. Every approved cross-source
bridge’s members share one stored predicate, so merging already works
through predicate. Bridge-aware queries add splitting by meaning, and
#735 defines tests that can fail.



8. Status / sequencing
Tracked in GH #628 since 2026-10-01; that issue’s checklist is the live one.

(kg_bridge_report.py); seed rebuilt from stored strings with approval
statuses; dead-member and Biolink-slot checks in the test suite; v4.4.2
verification (§4); opt-in bridged relation identity in the training export

 DECISION: §6 existing-predicate cleanup: A, no per-row flag (Richard, 2026-10-04)
 DECISION: D-Q4-01 is B′: Arm B and later runs use the bridged export (Richard, 2026-10-04, #611)
 DECISION: #709’s proposals A1–A7, the three drug–protein role
bridges, biolink:has_target → maple:drug-target, and has_side_effect
on maple:drug-adverse-effect (Richard, 2026-10-04). GP-KG target
deferred.
 DECISION: negative assertions are exported as relation types of
their own (Richard, 2026-10-04). Proving the model reads them as negative is
#726.
 CONFIRM: §5 editor UI shape, plus where the manifest lives (§5.1), 2026-10-02
 Migration 110 + bridge tables + seed/sync (kg_bridge_sync.py)

 Seed the production tables (kg_bridge_sync.py seed --apply, or the tab’s owner-only Seed button). Seeded 2026-10-02 16:24 PDT: 13 bridges, 25 members. On 2026-10-03 kg_bridge_sync.py diff found the database and bridges.yaml holding the same manifest.
 Return source_predicate on every edge in the canonical read path, so a
reader sees the source’s own assertion (GH #628’s display fix, 2026-10-04)

kg/kg_predicate_mapping_report.content:
PrimeKG → Biolink Predicate Mapping — Final Report
Authors: whafa, Claude (Maple project)
Date: 2026-05-09; last updated 2026-05-11 with actual post-rerun audit numbers
Companion writeup: kg_composition_pipeline_writeup.md §4.1 + §4.2
Code: backend/kg_normalize/predicate_mapper.py
Trigger: during the post-migration audit (writeup §4.1) we observed 250 PrimeKG edges had collapsed to fewer canonical relations than legacy. That was acceptable per se (predicate canonicalization is supposed to dedup synonymous edges), but a closer look showed the mapping table had three real bugs and several unnecessarily coarse choices. This document is the post-fix audit of every PrimeKG → Biolink mapping with a defensibility tag for each.

Status update 2026-05-11. The refined mapping was deployed, both PrimeKG and GP-KG canonical schemas were wiped and re-migrated, and the actual post-rerun numbers are now embedded throughout this report (sections marked “Actual …” below). Predictions and actuals are both retained so the reader can see how well the prediction held up.


Summary
PrimeKG ships 30 distinct relation types. After mapping they collapse to 23 distinct Biolink predicates (up from 16 in the original mapping). All 7 remaining collapses fall into one of three defensible categories:

AMBIGUITY-VIA-DOMAIN — multiple raw predicates map to the same Biolink predicate, but the subject/object entity domains (drug vs gene vs phenotype, etc.) carry the disambiguating signal. A model that consumes entity types — which both PDR1 (CompGCN) and PDR2 (ULTRA) do — can recover the distinction. Loss is theoretical, not practical.
DELIBERATE-LOSS — two raw predicates encode the same biological fact (or one is a strict subset of the other). Collapsing is correct, not lossy.
EXACT — Biolink has a directly equivalent predicate; the mapping is canonical.

Every PrimeKG raw predicate is preserved verbatim in the mods_kg_relation.source_predicate column. The predicate column carries the canonical Biolink form. Downstream consumers can use either or both.

Distinct Biolink predicate count

The refined mapping is much closer to 1:1. The remaining 7 collapses are all either:

Symmetric direction pairs (PrimeKG’s bidirectional storage) where the canonical edge is undirected — 5 pairs
Cases where the entity-type domain disambiguates — 2 pairs

No mapping intentionally throws information away. Every raw predicate is preserved verbatim in mods_kg_relation.source_predicate so any downstream consumer that needs the original distinction can recover it via that column.
Mapper coverage vs data presence
These are different things and worth distinguishing:

The mapper has 23 distinct Biolink predicates defined for PrimeKG.
The actual data only contains 20 distinct Biolink predicates because three of the mappings (biolink:has_carrier, biolink:has_enzyme, biolink:has_transporter) target raw PrimeKG predicates (carrier, enzyme, transporter) that PrimeKG documents in its schema spec but never actually emits in the version of the data we ingested.
The 3 missing predicates correspond to PK-style drug-protein relationships (carrier proteins, metabolizing enzymes, transporters) that probably require a downstream DrugBank tier PrimeKG didn’t include.

This is benign — the mapper is future-proofed: if PrimeKG ships an update that includes those rows, our pipeline handles them automatically with the right Biolink predicate, no code change needed. The 20→23 gap is “schema-anticipated mappings vs data-realized mappings,” not data loss.

On general principle
The lesson here is generalizable: predicate canonicalization is a lossy transformation by definition (you’re projecting a high-dimensional relation type space onto a lower-dimensional one). The right framing isn’t “is information lost?” — yes, always — but “is the loss recoverable, defensible, and intentional?” Three knobs to tune:

Use Biolink’s specific predicates when they exist. biolink:has_off_label_use is a thing; biolink:subclass_of is a thing. The first pass of this mapper used biolink:treats and biolink:related_to as defaults, which silently lost recoverable distinction.
Preserve the source value verbatim in a separate column so the loss is recoverable for any consumer that needs it.
Tag the loss tier in the mapping comments — EXACT vs AMBIGUITY-VIA-DOMAIN vs DELIBERATE-LOSS. Whoever inherits this code (including future-you) gets to evaluate each choice on its own terms rather than re-deriving them from scratch.

This applies to any other source we add (CIViC, OncoKB, PharmGKB, RTX-KG2). The connector tests should include an “all source predicates have a defensible mapping with a tag” check as part of D-phase acceptance.

Why Biolink seems “too small” — the qualifier-vs-predicate model
(Adding this section to address a recurring question: if Biolink has hundreds of predicates, why do we keep collapsing source-native predicates into smaller numbers of canonical Biolink predicates?)
Biolink IS big at the predicate level — it ships hundreds of slot definitions. But the appearance of “Biolink being too small to cover what we have” comes from three real architectural choices Biolink makes that differ from how individual KGs structure their data:
1. Biolink models qualifiers separately from predicates
When a source like CIViC says “PREDICTS_SENSITIVITY_TO drug X for cancer type Y at evidence level 3A”, the source compresses everything into one relation type per (predicate, qualifier-combination). Biolink instead models this as ONE predicate (biolink:predicts_sensitivity_to) PLUS separate qualified_predicate, subject_aspect_qualifier, evidence_level slots that carry the extra structure.
Our current schema (mods_kg_relation) has columns for subject_id, object_id, predicate, source_predicate, source_id, weight, evidence, metadata. There’s no qualifier column. So when a source represents an evidence-level distinction as a separate relation type (e.g., PrimeKG’s indication vs off-label use), and Biolink would naturally model both as biolink:treats with different qualifier values, our schema makes us choose:

Map both to biolink:treats → loss (this was the original PrimeKG bug we just fixed)
Use different Biolink predicates if available (biolink:treats vs biolink:has_off_label_use) → preserves the distinction at the predicate level (current refined approach)
Add qualifier columns to our schema → cleanest, but bigger refactor; deferred

So Biolink IS big enough to express everything, but our schema doesn’t yet model the qualifier dimension where Biolink puts ~30% of the information.
2. Biolink uses entity-type-domain to disambiguate, on purpose
Take drug_drug (drug-drug interaction) and protein_protein (protein-protein interaction) — semantically very different! Biolink maps both to biolink:interacts_with (the same predicate) because the subject and object entity types already convey the distinction. A (drug, biolink:interacts_with, drug) row means DDI; a (protein, biolink:interacts_with, protein) row means PPI.
This is a design choice: Biolink avoids predicate redundancy when entity types convey the information. A downstream model (CompGCN, ULTRA, etc.) typically embeds entity types alongside predicates, so the distinction is recoverable.
You can see this in our refined PrimeKG mapping: protein_protein and drug_drug both → biolink:interacts_with (3,314,778 rows total in PrimeKG canonical, of which 2,672,628 are drug-drug and 642,150 are protein-protein — recoverable via entity-type filter).
3. Some source predicates are inherently multi-semantic
PrimeKG’s gene_go_phenotype covers gene→GO-term relationships, but GO has three subgraphs (Biological Process, Molecular Function, Cellular Component) with semantically distinct relationships:

Gene → BP term should be biolink:participates_in
Gene → MF term should be biolink:enables
Gene → CC term should be biolink:located_in

PrimeKG flattens all three into one relation type without exposing the GO subgraph metadata. We have no honest way to pick the right Biolink predicate per row, so we map to biolink:related_to (the parent predicate). This is one of two DELIBERATE-LOSS entries in our PrimeKG mapping table. 204,862 rows in GP-KG and similar in PrimeKG sit at this related_to placeholder until/unless we re-process those edges with the GO subgraph membership lookup.
Summary



































Apparent “Biolink too small” caseActual reasonRecoverable?indication + off-label use both → biolink:treats (the original bug)Biolink has both biolink:treats AND biolink:has_off_label_use; we just hadn’t used the latter✅ Fixed in the refined mapperprotein_protein + drug_drug → biolink:interacts_withBiolink design: entity types carry the distinction✅ Via subject/object domain filter250 PrimeKG edges previously dedupedWas caused by the first issue, not Biolink limitations✅ Resolved (post-refinement: 0 dedups)gene_go_phenotype → biolink:related_toSource flattens BP/MF/CC subgraphs; no honest way to disambiguate without subgraph metadata⏳ Recoverable via GO ontology lookup (future enhancement)Evidence-level qualifiers (CIViC Level A/B/C, OncoKB Level 1/2/3A)Biolink models these as qualifiers, not as predicate variants⏳ Our schema needs qualifier columns to use Biolink’s idiomatic representation
So: Biolink is comprehensive at the predicate-AND-qualifier level. Our schema currently captures only the predicate dimension. Apparent collapses are typically Biolink working as designed (entity-type disambiguation) or our schema lagging (missing qualifier columns). In every case, the raw source_predicate column preserves the source’s distinction verbatim — no information is irretrievably lost.

That is what prod stores, on every one of the 33 relation keys and on every one of the 183 entities. The merges collapsed 112,486 rows: drug_drug 108,174, contraindication 1,566, indication 428, and nine smaller relations (§1).
Three mechanisms made the groups (§2).

63 groups (61 gene, 2 anatomy): PrimeKG ships two nodes for one id. Either two symbols of one gene (C16orf58 and RUSF1, both NCBI Gene 64755) or two labels of one UBERON term. These were one entity from the first backfill. The merges are right and cost no rows.
101 groups (all drugs): Node Normalizer gave their DrugBank ids one preferred CURIE. apply_canonical_entity_merges.py pass 1 then merged them in May 2026. Node Normalizer folds salts, esters, enantiomers and radiotracers into one chemical, and twice it folded together unrelated drugs.
19 groups (18 pathway, 1 disease): the names matched, and the same script’s pass 2 merged them. Ten of them join a SARS-CoV-1 pathway to its SARS-CoV-2 namesake.

Unclear (6): drug groups where the evidence does not settle it (§3).
Both known examples are distinct. D- and L-tartaric acid are enantiomers (J1). Choline C-11 and choline salicylate sit in a group of four different drugs.
