Fix: SAMPLE_META multi-cancer accounting in both services, tissue-labeled timepoints, caveat banners, corrected tooltips (commit e0d489d). This is almost certainly the recent one you were half-remembering.
Source: project_genomic_browser.md.

A2 — an assumed “second hit via LOH” ✅ — assumed ~Apr, corrected 2026-05-30

Assumed: An allele at ~52% VAF in tumor tissue “strongly suggests LOH / biallelic loss” (→ a drug-eligibility framing).
Actually: B-allele-frequency analysis showed the allele is retained in all 3 samples, with the arm balanced. No copy-number second hit.
Fix: Copy/LOH tab built on real BAF data (commit 6556341); corrected the clinical readout.
Source: project_mods_research_assumptions.md (the wrong version) → project_genomic_browser.md (the correction).

A3 — Variant classification by count/VAF heuristic ✅ — ~May

Assumed: Could rank Caris variants by a count/VAF heuristic.
Actually: The heuristic buried the real clonal drivers. Had to classify by Caris’s own CI field (Pathogenic / VUS / Benign).
Source: project_genomic_browser.md.

A4 — Built work that was already done (#115/#118/#119) ✅ — 2026-05-30

Assumed: The open “PDR2 training knobs” issues described the current code.
Actually: The OOM-truncation fix, num_negative knob, and ReduceLROnPlateau decay were already implemented. Only a regression guard was genuinely needed.
Cost: Nearly re-built three already-satisfied features.
Fix: Added a regression guard (febfb3d), closed the rest as already-done.
Source: feedback_verify_issue_freshness.md.
⚠ Correction, 2026-10-09 (#861): the ReduceLROnPlateau decay was not already done. train_foundation_model builds the scheduler but never steps it, so every foundation trained at a constant learning rate, and #118 (LR decay) was closed on a false premise. The check stopped at “the object exists”. Check that it is called, too.

A5 — KG federation misread as “decentralized storage” ✅ — late May

Assumed: The federation decision replaced the canonical schema with decentralized per-source storage.
Actually: It’s predicate federation — a bridge-manifest layer on top of the unchanged canonical entity schema.
Also (same incident): I’d over-asserted “the KG is canonical” from CLAUDE.md’s Phase-C4 note while missing the later docs/kg_federation_planning.md decision entirely.
Fix: Re-grounded on the doc; lesson = open the doc, don’t infer it from its title/commit msg.
Source: feedback_repo_docs_source_of_truth.md.

A6 — Causal misattribution of an edge-count jump ✅ — ~mid-May

Assumed: Maureen’s canonical edge count jumping 135→250 was “dedup unlocking richer cross-source resolution” (plausible — we’d just run dedup).
Actually: prime_kg + gp_kg had flipped planned→loaded overnight, expanding the resolver’s match pool. Unrelated event.
Cost: Lost trust until I went back and checked timestamps.
Source: feedback_verify_before_claiming.md.

A7 — Wrong codebase identity (kg-predict vs PDR1) ✅ — ~Apr

Assumed (by a prior explore pass): an early run used the kg-predict codebase, concluded from raw byte-count comparison.
Actually: It was PDR1/code — the byte diff was CRLF line endings, not a different file. Verify by code markers (-scalars flag, scalar-modulation block), not byte counts.
Source: project_pdr_training.md.

A8 — Default patient assumed single-row ✅ — broke 2026-05-22, found ~2026-05-30

Assumed: mods_patient has exactly one row; _get_default_patient_id returned an ID only when len==1.
Actually: A 2nd patient (PGP stand-in) was added → resolver returned None → GET /patient-profile 404’d, silently breaking the Patient Profile + PDR Input tabs for 8 days; a frontend effect then re-fired the failed fetch every render (404 request storm).
Fix: earliest-created default (= Maureen) + !profileError guard in ResearchDashboard.jsx. Robust picker tracked as #146.
Source: project_default_patient_resolution.md.


B. PDR2 / ML-pipeline hallucinations
(assumed-portable, assumed-defaults, or trusted-upstream that broke)
B1 — classify_entity assumed paper-naked identifiers ✅ — ~2026-05-18

Assumed: Upstream regexes (^C\d{7}$, ^DB\d{5}$, MP:/HP:) would classify our entities.
Actually: Our Biolink CURIEs (DrugBank:, NCBIGene:, MONDO:, HPO:) match none → everything bucketed as “gene”, drug_inv_vocab empty, the drug-only personalization mask zeroed everything → vacuous “Δ=0 everywhere” eval. Misleading, not crashing.
Fix: Override classify_entity for CURIE prefixes; verified 7,782 drugs after.
Source: feedback_pdr2_classify_entity_biolink.md.

B2 — Trusted upstream eval (saturated MRR ≈ 0.99) ✅ — 2026-05-02/03, code-fixed 2026-05-30

Assumed: Upstream validate()/evaluate_model() MRR/Hits@1 ≈ 0.99 were real.
Actually: A too-aggressive relation-aware filter + mishandled out-of-mask positives saturated the metric. The honest signal was AUPRC 0.0025 — the 0.0025-vs-0.99 gap was the canary.
Fix: Separate full-ranking eval (eval_maple.py); upstream out-of-mask ranking corrected in 4ecd621 (#116).
Source: project_pdr2_gpkg_first_run.md.

B3 — Assumed ULTRA-3g warm-start would help ✅ — 2026-05-03

Assumed: Warm-starting from ultra_3g.pth (general-domain pretrain) beats from-scratch.
Actually: Negative transfer on biomedical KGs — −46% MRR, ~100× worse Hits@1. The general-domain relation graph is actively misleading for biomedical relations.
Fix: Default to from-scratch on new biomedical KGs.
Source: project_pdr2_gpkg_first_run.md.

B4 — Checkpoint v1 assumed sufficient for resume ✅ — 2026-05-26

Assumed: Saving model weights was enough to warm-start/resume foundation training.
Actually: Cold-started Adam (m=v=0) → sign-SGD pathology for ~1000 steps kicked converged Run B out of its loss basin (bowl-shaped MRR collapse: 0.00121 → 7.7e-6 → 9.5e-5).
Fix: Checkpoint format v2 saves optimizer/scheduler/RNG/step (#29); --resume_with_lr_warmup for v1 sources. Adam buffers from pre-v2 runs are permanently lost.
Source: project_pdr2_checkpoint_v2_contract.md.

B5 — --seed assumed applied globally ✅ — fixed 2026-05-30

Assumed: run_maple.py --seed seeded the run.
Actually: It was parsed but only used for validate() subsampling — never applied to torch/numpy/random/cuda, so even bit-equivalent resume was impossible from RNG drift alone.
Fix: 074cf91 (#40) applies --seed globally at startup.
Source: project_pdr2_checkpoint_v2_contract.md.

B6 — ent2id assumed stable across sessions ✅ — ~Apr

Assumed: The entity→index map is reproducible, so a checkpoint can be loaded in a fresh session.
Actually: ent2id is built from train.txt traversal under Python set-hash randomization; a fresh-session load scrambles predictions (ρ 0.74→0.067) or crashes (CUDA index OOB / cuFFT INTERNAL_ERROR).
Fix: PYTHONHASHSEED=41504 in cell 1; run inference in the same session as training, or carry the ent2id sidecar.
Source: project_pdr_training.md.

B7 — test.py defaults assumed to match the checkpoint ✅ — fixed 2026-04-30

Assumed: Default gcn_layer=1 / opn=corr would load any checkpoint.
Actually: A 2L or opn=sub checkpoint either raises Unexpected key(s) in state_dict or — worse — silently builds the wrong model. Notebook templates Cell 20/22 shipped this bug.
Fix: Always pass full arch flags; patched all 5 templates.
Source: feedback_test_py_arch_flags.md.

B8 — Pickle assumed NumPy-version-portable ✅ — ~2026-05-18

Assumed: A patient-data pickle written locally would load in the container.
Actually: Local NumPy 2.x pickles np.ndarray with numpy._core refs; the container’s NumPy 1.x can’t unpickle (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy._core').
Fix: Serialize numeric vectors as Python lists, not ndarrays.
Source: feedback_pdr2_pickle_numpy_portability.md.

B9 — Drive append-mode assumed durable ✅ — 2026-04-30

Assumed: test.py’s per-batch open(save_result, 'a') to a Drive path is fine.
Actually: Colab’s Drive FUSE drops the inode under tight write loops — crashed CV-eval at step 12k/25k (47 min in), metrics.json never written.
Fix: Write to local /content, copy to Drive only after the process exits.
Source: feedback_drive_fuse_append_mode.md.

B10 — Vertex export omitted the maple_patient overlay ✅ — 2026-05-16, fixed 2026-05-24

Assumed: The worker’s composition export matched Colab’s.
Actually: It didn’t pass --include-source maple_patient → Maureen’s node + 203 triples missing on every Vertex run of a Maureen-containing composition. Vertex-vs-Colab comparisons were silently not apples-to-apples.
Fix: 79d3b36 plumbs the overlay through PDR2 handlers.
Source: project_pdr2_phase1_status.md.

B11 — Manifest gpu_type / val plumbing assumptions ✅ — 2026-05-15

Assumed: Manifest fields reflected the actual run.
Actually: A smoke test logged A100_40GB while running on T4; val_n_sample/validate_every weren’t plumbed to the container → best_mrr null on Vertex rows. (Also: T4’s OOM cascade ends at batch_size=4 vs A100’s 32 — not the same experiment.)
Source: project_pdr2_phase1_status.md.

B12 — Quota grant assumed = capacity / single-tier ✅ — 2026-05-14 & ~05-18

Assumed (a): Compute-Engine GPU quota was enough for Vertex. Actually: Vertex Custom Training has a separate quota tier on top; submit 429’d on custom_model_training_nvidia_l4_gpus.
Assumed (b): L4 quota granted = L4 available. Actually: us-central1 L4 capacity was thin — jobs sat PENDING 2h+ then failed “Resources insufficient.” Default to A100.
Source: feedback_vertex_quota_layers.md, feedback_vertex_l4_capacity_unreliable.md.


C. Backend / infra coding hallucinations
C1 — Swallowed SQL error without db.rollback() ✅ — 2026-05-26

Assumed: try: query … except Exception: return {} safely degrades.
Actually: _load_cost_so_far referenced non-existent columns; the swallowed error left the Postgres transaction aborted, so a later innocent query died with InFailedSqlTransaction — pointing at the wrong culprit.
Fix: rollback inside the except; don’t lean on broad-except as a contract.
Source: feedback_swallowed_sql_error_needs_rollback.md.

C2 — Long handler with no heartbeat → double-execution race ✅ — 2026-05-26

Assumed: A worker handler can run a long phase without heartbeating.
Actually: handle_cost_sync_gcp went silent >300s during a 28,775-row per-row UPDATE → orphan-recovery re-claimed it; two workers ran concurrently, both paid full cost, hit DEAD on the third stale-heartbeat.
Fix: wrap long handlers in _start_pdr_heartbeat_thread.
Source: feedback_long_handler_heartbeat_thread.md.

C3 — Drop-migration without gutting the creator ✅ — 2026-05-23

Assumed: Adding migration 088_drop_med_advocate_tables was enough.
Actually: On restart, the old creator (015) re-armed (tables now gone), tried to re-CREATE, and failed on enum drift → backend startup aborted (FATAL: migrations failed).
Fix: any DROP migration must also gut the older CREATE migration.
Source: feedback_deletion_migration_must_gut_creators.md.

C4 — ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE deadlock under parallel ingests ✅ — 2026-05-17

Assumed: The CURIE-cache upsert was safe to run from concurrent ingests.
Actually: Two INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on mods_kg_curie_cache deadlocked. (The cache is a deterministic memo — the UPDATE was redundant anyway.)
Fix: DO NOTHING (9d4f1ef). Fix the SQL, don’t serialize/retry-bandaid.
Source: feedback_fix_deadlocks.md.

C5 — OncoKB: bridge edges where a merge was right ✅ — 2026-05-18

Assumed: Task said “approach A (bridge) safer, recommend first” → I shipped 53 same_as bridge edges.
Actually: 53 rows, all unambiguous → an entity merge was correct from the start; bridges force the model to learn same_as=identity. User: “feels sloppy.”
Fix: a567a52 merged them. Lesson: for small/unambiguous dupes, go straight to the clean fix.
Source: feedback_prefer_merge_over_bridge.md.


D. Process / execution slips (incl. source control)
(not assumption-hallucinations, but mistakes during coding we had to undo — logged for completeness)

Root cause of the git ones (D1, D2, D10): this checkout has a shared index + working tree + HEAD across parallel sessions. The user routinely has uncommitted WIP staged in that shared index, and another session can move HEAD out from under a command mid-run. Standing guardrails: commit with an explicit pathspec only (never bare git commit / -a); never git checkout/restore a file that may hold the user’s unstaged work; prefer gh pr merge (origin-side) over local git merge; re-check git branch --show-current before any local merge/commit.

D1 — Bare git commit swept the user’s WIP ✅ — 2026-05-29

The #86 federation commit pulled in ~11 files of uncommitted #108 work from the shared index. Caught before push. Fix: always commit with an explicit pathspec.
Source: feedback_commit_with_pathspec_shared_index.md.

D2 — git checkout <file> destroyed unstaged work ✅ — ~2026-05-15

Reverting my own migration_081 with git checkout wiped the user’s unstaged migration_080 (~110 lines), unrecoverable; they had to recreate it.
Source: feedback_git_checkout_destroys_unstaged.md.

D3 — Re-ran “pending” tasks from a resumed session ✅ — ~Mar

Logged 9 duplicate TRT injections and double-deducted vial volume because the context summary listed them as pending though IDs 155–163 were already in the DB.
Source: feedback_check_before_reexecuting.md.

D4 — Chip task wired the wrong table ✅ — ~May

A chip about a “KG matching column” was about the PrimekgBadge in the (unpushed) Patient Profile tab; I wired the Inference tab’s Drug ID column instead — compiled, internally consistent, wrong target.
Source: feedback_chip_unpushed_wip.md.

D5 — Bypassed the worker queue with raw gcloud ✅ — 2026-05-21→24

Submitted Run A/B foundations via gcloud “to save time” → invisible in the cockpit for ~48h, hours of hand-written SQL backfill + manual ingest. The bypass cost more than it saved.
Source: feedback_never_bypass_worker_queue.md.

D6 — Notebook replace() patching + premature plateau calls ✅ — 2026-04-29

Cell-9 tee patch silently dropped the RESTORE_FLAG line → user’s RESUME=True did nothing for ~30 min; plus escape-juggling / orphan-apostrophe bugs from multi-line replace(). Separately, called training plateau 3× in one day on 1–3 flat points, wrong each time (noise dips recovered).
Fix: ast.parse validation + whole-cell line-lists; declare plateau only after 5 consecutive non-improving evals.
Source: feedback_notebook_patching_safety.md.

D7 — String-substitution chain re-mangle ✅ — 2026-05-15

Overlapping-prefix replacements produced PrimeKGCIViCPharmGKB**PharmGKB**Maureen; trainer crashed at dataset lookup. Fix: longest-prefix-first / word-boundary regex / AST.
Source: feedback_string_substitution_order.md.

D8 — Assumed “imports locally → imports on the worker” ✅ — 2026-05-20

Missing List in a from typing import … line passed on local Python 3.14 but NameError’d at module load on Docker workers, bouncing 3 Vertex submissions through claim→error→release.
Fix: 10cd1fe; pre-deploy get_type_hints() check.
Source: feedback_worker_typing_imports.md.

D9 — Assumed local files == running container ✅ — 2026-05-18 & 2026-05-20

Added a dataset class (locally only) → container AttributeError after ~60s. Added an entrypoint.sh MODE branch (locally only) → 3 jobs failed ERROR: unknown MODE=fine_tune, ~$5–10 A100 burned. Container snapshots lib/pdr2/* at build — needs a rebuild.
Source: feedback_pdr2_dataset_class_in_container.md, feedback_pdr2_entrypoint_in_container.md.

D10 — Local git merge landed on the wrong branch ✅ — 2026-05-30

Assumed: git merge would apply to the branch I thought I was on.
Actually: there’s one shared HEAD across sessions; another session’s checkout moved HEAD between my commands, so the merge landed on the live feat/gb-igv branch instead of the intended target. Also hit “Base branch was modified” repeatedly because main is pushed to directly by other sessions mid-task.
Fix: prefer gh pr merge (origin-side — never touches the shared HEAD); re-check git branch --show-current before local merges; git fetch + retry on “base modified.”
Source: feedback_commit_with_pathspec_shared_index.md.

D11 — My own commit clobbered earlier cleanup ✅ — 2026-05-15

Assumed: my 43c06dc (PDR2 Vertex eval pipeline + composition polish) was purely additive.
Actually: it clobbered the explorer Phase 1.5 cleanup and re-introduced an already-removed KG Health tab; had to restore the same day.
Fix: 83a2d16 “restore Phase 1.5 cleanup clobbered by 43c06dc + remove KG Health tab.”
Source: git log (43c06dc → 83a2d16).


To triage (from git log; not yet confirmed mine vs. pre-existing)
Move up into A–C once root cause is confirmed.

🔍 c7704a1 2026-05-27 — fix(api): close schema-extras silent-drop hole (#41) — API silently dropped schema extras.
🔍 c310709 2026-05-27 — fix(startup): only reset truly-stale tasks on backend boot (#33 Bug A) — boot reset not-truly-stale tasks.
🔍 970f751 2026-05-29 — fix(ehr): extract dropped fields in Epic/Kaiser FHIR parsers (#66-#71) — FHIR parsers dropped fields.
🔍 4ec7b2a 2026-05-29 — fix(migrations): drop migration 091 — DRKG predicate backfill is dead weight — shipped a migration that was dead weight.
🔍 804bd83 / cc5f172 2026-05-19 — cost BQ event_uid dropped rows (missing labels-hash / full fingerprint).
🔍 0acd62d 2026-05-18 — cache filenames >200 chars → ENAMETOOLONG; had to hash.
🔍 83a2d16 2026-05-15 — explorer Phase 1.5 cleanup clobbered by 43c06dc; had to restore.
🔍 169ab88 2026-05-30 — upsert_run_by_name was downgrading status/metrics; had to refuse downgrades (#117).
🔍 a3c76d1 2026-05-27 — pdr-eval read flat instead of nested raw/filtered/rel_filtered structure.


E. Added from the manual transcript sweep (2026-05-31)
(Recovered by ripgrep over raw session JSONL after the MCP transcript-search tool stayed gated. Bracketed tags map to categories A–D. Session ids in italics for traceability.)
E1 — Hallucinated a DB column drugbank_id [B/infra] ✅ — 2026-05-22

Wrote a query against g.drugbank_id — a column that doesn’t exist (the schema has drug_name + rxnorm_code only). Caught and replaced with a graceful empty-list fallback. (session 0ed1c039)

E2 — Misread the requirement “write results directly to the DB” [A/requirement] ✅ — 2026-05-20

You said you’d rather write all results directly to the DB rather than a script that backfills after the fact; I misread and built toward the pass-through approach. Corrected once you flagged it. The most on-point “requirement hallucination” of the set. (session bf8f8940)

E3 — Conflated live code with deleted Med Advocate, from a memory snippet [A/B] ✅ — 2026-05-20

Concluded some annotators were Med-Advocate-related based on a memory snippet without checking the actual call sites; you were right to push back. The inverse of the standing rule that repository documents are the source of truth — here a stale memory misled me and the code was the truth. (session 02cd6dc7)

E4 — “Conflated the layers” [A/arch] ✅ — 2026-05-22

Misdescribed the architecture layering; had to re-check and restate current status. (session 0ed1c039)

E5 — Wrongly concluded the local DB was unusable → fell back to files [C] ✅ — ~late May

Decided the DB wasn’t usable and fell back to file-based data; in fact mods_kg_canonical_stats returned 3.7M entities — the MODS server was talking to prod, I’d just misdiagnosed the connection. (session 4502bdc7)

E6 — Misread the prod flow during checkpoint work [B] ✅ — ~2026-05-26

Misread how the prod checkpoint flow worked; corrected after you pointed it out (same session that produced the v2 checkpoint contract, B4). (session cbef1cd7)

E7 — Run-data overwrite via duplicate experiment name [B/data-loss] ✅ — 2026-05-02

2026-05-02_pdr2_gpkg_warm_v1 and 2026-05-03_pdr2_gpkg_warm_v1 shared the experiment name → derived the same run id 529acfa7, so an orphan run overwrote the real run’s data. The concrete failure behind the “don’t derive run paths from date+experiment name” lesson in project_pdr2_gpkg_first_run.md. (session 63b50ec1)

E8 — Overwrote the wrong notebook cell [D6 instance] ✅ — 2026-05-02

“Made a mistake — overwrote the setup cell instead of the train cell”; restored it. Another instance of the replace()-blind notebook editing already captured in D6. (session 63b50ec1)

E9 — Per-epoch training logs lost in a reorg [data-loss, confirm-mine] 🔍 — surfaced 2026-04-29

GP-KG runs v1–v4 lost their per-epoch logs in the 2026-04-27 pre-reorg cleanup — gone from Drive too, unrecoverable without retraining. Unclear whether I ran that cleanup; flagged for confirmation. (session a79a912e)

E10 — Another shared-main divergence episode [D/source-control] ✅ — ~mid-May

Local main diverged from origin with a Terminal.jsx conflict; while reconciling, one option I surfaced was a destructive reset that would have discarded your commits 681f8f4 + e0c2cc7. Handled safely (checked the reflog, didn’t auto-destruct), but it’s the same shared-worktree churn as D1/D2/D10. (session fb3cc3ea)

E11 — Minor self-corrections (low severity) ✅

Wrong about “Opus 4.7 Max” capabilities, which changed a cost/calculus claim (ff858e40); jumped to “lower it” as a recommendation too fast (cdaf9cde); confused myself tracking which run was “Run B” in the results matrix (60fe0a92).


Method note for the next sweep: raw-JSONL grep is badly polluted by injected context (CLAUDE.md, the memory/*.md files — including this log itself — and the 7 auto-loaded paper texts). High-signal, low-noise patterns were assistant self-admissions (I conflated, I misread, I incorrectly assumed) and hallucinated-symbol callouts (doesn't exist, no such column). Generic terms (git checkout, you're right, reset) were ~all doc-echo. If the MCP search_session_transcripts tool is ever ungated, prefer it — it scopes to user/assistant messages and skips injected docs.

meta/memory_write_contract.title: Memory Write Contract
meta/memory_write_contract.content:
Memory write contract (epic #147, P5 / GH #155)
What belongs in the vector memory (save_memory / pdr_note_save) and what doesn’t. The store is
Claude Code’s research/operational recall — keep it durable and clean so auto-recall (the P3
hooks) surfaces signal, not noise. This is what prevents the “favorite color ×12” rot the audit found.
Save it when it’s DURABLE and would help a FUTURE session
Good test: would I want this resurfaced automatically, weeks from now, in a fresh session?

decision — a closed strategic call + its rationale (“Phase 0 uses PDR1’s trainer because …”).
insight — a non-obvious finding from analysis (“vanilla CompGCN over-smooths on dense KGs past ~3 layers”).
fact — a verified, stable fact (“the ex vivo drug-sensitivity panel was drawn twice, in February and September 2025”).
gotcha-style — a trap + how to avoid it (“never use split_KG.py for Phase 0 — ratios/seed differ”). Save these as insight or task_hint; a dedicated gotcha kind is a deliberate future enum migration (native Postgres memorykind type), not yet added.
task_hint — “next time do X” / “where is Y” navigation.
summary — a digest of a large artifact, run, or thread.
preference — a stable user/operator preference.

Do NOT save

Transient conversation state, current-turn plans, or thinking-out-loud.
Anything trivially derivable from code, git history, GitHub issues, or CLAUDE.md — don’t duplicate the repo.
Unverified guesses. A wrong memory silently misleads every future recall — if unsure, lower salience and say so in the content, or don’t save.
Secrets / credentials.
One-off trivia with no future value.

Discipline (this is what keeps it from rotting)

Search first. Run search_memory / pdr_note_search before saving. If a near-duplicate exists,
update_memory it instead of adding another row.
One fact per memory. Tight declarative title (3–8 words) + focused content. Don’t paste transcripts.
Pick the right kind (list above) — it drives filtering and recall.
pinned=true only for a handful of always-relevant anchors (current phase, hard constraints).
salience: default 0.5; raise for high-value durable facts, lower for ephemeral-ish ones.
Prefer pdr_note_save (with scope='run'/'task') for PDR-pipeline notes so they link to the run/task;
use save_memory for general research/clinical memory.

Everything lands in the canonical workspace user (MEMORY_WORKSPACE_USER). Curate via the Memory panel
(terminal alias memory); the nightly consolidation job (P6) merges accidental near-duplicates.

meta/mods_smoke_run_1_pm_charter.title: Smoke run #1 — PM charter
meta/mods_smoke_run_1_pm_charter.content:
Smoke run #1 — PM charter

Closed 2026-09-29. Smoke run #1 finished and the PM ran the §9 close-out. This is the charter as it stood while the run was live.

The PM is a long-lived Claude Code session, pinned in the desktop app. It runs a self-paced /loop and re-reads this file at every wake-up (a “tick”). The playbook, `mods_smoke_run_1_playbook.md`, says what to do. This file says how the PM operates and what it may do without asking. The ledger is #439.
1. Objective
Drive smoke run #1 until all ten machinery checks, M1–M10 (playbook §6), pass and §5.5 is closed. Work that is off the path (playbook §4, “deliberately not on this path”) is in scope only where it unblocks the path.
2. Authority (granted by Richard, 2026-09-28)

























GrantScopeDecisionsD1–D10 are accepted as written in playbook §3. The D7 mapping table still needs Richard’s approval before any code writes it. The two implementer choices (the CRC anchor and the candidate drug set) belong to the PM, and it records both in #439.MergeMerge critical-path PRs on green CI after reviewing the diff against the issue and the playbook.ComputeLaunch any runbook step (playbook §5) through the worker queue or the research API without asking. The **budget is 500 in total** for the run's cloud spend (Vertex and Cloud Build). The plan costs about 140, so the headroom is for one failed foundation, not for extra experiments. Use it wisely: before any job over $20, prove the path cheaply first: the M4 checks on a second export, and the container machinery tests. A short Vertex submit is not cheap in train mode, because it always runs the full post-training eval over the test set (hours). So watch the first epoch of the real job instead, and cancel on anomalies.PagingPush to Richard’s phone, batched. Nothing is pushed overnight; anything that arises waits for the morning batch.
3. Must ask
Stop only the affected lane. Keep the others moving, and add the question to the numbered “Waiting on Richard” list in the status comment.

Any decision that §2 does not settle. This includes any change to a D1–D10 choice, and the D7 mapping table.
Any ontology or vocabulary mapping that involves judgement (the CLAUDE.md hard rules).
A job outside the runbook, spend that would take the total past $500, and any second foundation attempt.
A failed acceptance check, or a number off its expected value. Examples: E3 doesn’t write 3,752 rows; the v0 funnel lands far from 594 / 109 (the approved D7 mapping); the new foundation’s MRR is not below 0.56. Investigate first, then report with the evidence. Never redefine a check to make it pass.
Anything destructive to ground truth (patient data, KG source rows, the RGCC tables), any force-push, a merge over red CI, any clinical claim, and any edit to docs/PDR_PIPELINE_PLAN.md.
Anything that needs a credential the PM does not already have. The PM already has the database credential, so it runs the stack itself; the charter first said the PM lacked it, which was wrong (corrected 2026-09-28). The PM never reads .env, never prints a secret, and never enters one anywhere.

4. The anti-idle rule
At the end of every tick, each lane (P, A, G, R) is in exactly one of three states, and the status comment says which:

advanced: something moved this tick;
waiting: on a named job, PR or agent, with an ETA and a watcher armed;
blocked: on a numbered item in “Waiting on Richard”.

A lane that is idle for any other reason is a defect, and the PM fixes it on the same tick. While a lane is blocked, the PM prepares its next step, so that a “yes” executes immediately.
5. Tick procedure

Orient. Read this file, #439 (the body and the status comment), and whatever is new since the last tick: issue comments, PR and CI changes, finished agents, watcher logs, and anything Richard said.
Reconcile against reality, not issue state. A closed issue is not a shipped fix. The sources:

gh issue list --label critical-path --state all and gh pr list. PR checks are read here, on the regular tick; the PM never runs a dedicated CI poller. The app sends a <ci-monitor-event> on failures for the PR bound to this session;
live task_queue rows (the maple-worker MCP) and in-flight mods_research_run rows;
python scripts/fixer_agent.py status, run from C:\Maple, and whether nightly runs are on;
what the workers are running: git -C C:/Maple log -1, and any reloader restarts in docker logs;
spend so far, estimated as job hours × rate and cross-checked with the maple-cost tools once synced.


Advance each lane in playbook order: dispatch, review, merge, launch, verify, tick boxes.
Write state. Edit the status comment (marker <!-- smoke-pm:status -->) in place. It holds each lane’s state, the in-flight ids and ETAs, the numbered “Waiting on Richard” list, spend against budget, the time of this tick and the next wake, all in PDT.
Page only when “Waiting on Richard” gains an item or something fails that needs him. Send one batched push, outside quiet hours.
Sleep with ScheduleWakeup, passing the same loop prompt. Size the delay to what is in flight: 5–15 min while dispatching or merging, 30–60 min while a multi-hour job runs. Background agents and Monitors wake the PM early anyway.

Watchdog. A local scheduled task watches the heartbeat in the status comment and notifies Richard if the loop stops waking. It cannot restart the loop. When the loop dies, usually through an app restart, recovery is Richard telling the pinned session to resume. On resuming, the PM compares the time now with the next wake in the status comment, runs a tick at once, and re-arms its loop and its Monitors.
6. Executors

The fixer takes fixer-eligible critical-path issues: python scripts/fixer_agent.py start --issue N, run from C:\Maple. It merges on green CI by design. After each merge, check the issue’s stateReason.
Background subagents take the larger issues. Launch them with the Agent tool, isolation: "worktree", in the background. Brief each one with the issue, the playbook section, the collision rules below, and its own test database. It opens its PR with Fixes #N only when the issue is fully done, and Refs #N otherwise. The PM reviews the diff, then merges on green CI.
One executor per test database. The fixer owns one test database, and each subagent gets its own throwaway test database on the same server, with every database setting pointed at it. The test harness refuses any database that is not a dedicated test database.
Collision hotspots run one at a time: worker/task_handlers.py (#433), and lib/pdr2/code/script/* (#435, then #436).
The PM does not write feature code itself. Small fixes to a PR it is reviewing are fine.

7. Guardrails for long jobs

C:\Maple cannot be frozen, and no longer needs to be. Other sessions fast-forward it several times a day. On the morning of 2026-09-28 they did so four times, and each time all ten workers restarted (GH #361). Since then WORKER_AUTO_RELOAD=0 is the compose default, so a pull no longer restarts them. With reload off, the workers keep running the code they started with. To pick up merged code, send restart with the MCP worker_send_command, which waits for the current task to finish, or use docker restart while task_queue is quiet.
Launch drivers by docker exec into a worker. Never edit a .py in C:\Maple to launch or tweak a run.
Watch a multi-hour job with a detached poller that writes a log, plus a Monitor on that log. The poller exits on every terminal state, not only success.
E3 runs with --no-resume (#360). Delete a pipeline_config throttle row as soon as its pass ends.
Every job goes through the worker queue or the research API, never raw gcloud (M10).
Before the steps they affect, read #445 (the MCP export ignores the schema), #446 (the fine-tune path drops LOSS_VARIANT; set adjustment_target_domain: drug explicitly) and #447 (one bad score aborts a D2 shard).

8. House rules that bite

Everything Richard reads gives times in PDT.
For partial work, write Refs #N. Never put fix, fixes, fixed, close or resolve directly before #N, even inside quoted text.
Merge with gh pr merge N --merge (a merge commit, not a squash). Once git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the commits are in, delete the remote head branch by hand.
Commit with a pathspec (git commit -- <paths>), because the index is shared across worktrees.
Record decisions and findings with pdr_note_save. Lifecycle state goes in GitHub, never in memory.
Executors run on Opus 5.5, which is the default.

9. Closing
When M1–M10 pass:

Close out playbook §5.5: put the M9 provenance list in #439, write up the run, and save a pdr_note_save decision.
Turn the fixer back on.
Leave WORKER_AUTO_RELOAD at 0, the compose default since 2026-09-28. Don’t restore 1.
Disable smoke-pm-watchdog.
Post a final status, and stop the loop.

meta/q4_2026_roadmap.content:
Q4 2026 roadmap: earn a signal, ship a list
Milestone: Q4 2026 · Ledger: the
“Q4 2026 ledger” issue in that milestone · Charter:
research_steward_charter.md · Approved by Richard: 2026-10-01
This is the Research Steward’s playbook. It says what Q4 is for, the order of work, and the
pre-registered gates that decide whether a result counts. Every number here was verified on
2026-10-01 against code, the production database (read-only) or GitHub. Re-verify before relying
on one.

1. Where Q4 starts
Smoke run #1 (#439) proved the pipeline runs end to end on her released PRS, traceably. Its science
result is an honest null, and nothing was planned after it.
















































































AreaState on 2026-10-01SourceMachineryAll ten checks pass, about $130 spent, every artifact traceable.#439, [[results/mods_smoke_run_1_writeupBase modelLoses to popularity. Held-out filtered MRR is 0.021, against 0.031 for per-relation tail frequency. Graded RGCC ρ is +0.03 and +0.05 per draw, against +0.37 for node degree alone. Score vs degree: Spearman 0.86. Suspected cause: the mirror edge stays in the training graph (remove_one_hop=False).#523PersonalizationThe released criterion stalls in epoch 1 and ignores λ. It can only demote, and 73% of its mass runs through contraindicated_for.writeup §4.3, #420Validation labelsRGCC is single-agent and blind to her combination regimen, and degree explains much of it. Her medication history is circular. No clean label with n ≫ 1 exists.#523, vector memoryPRS590 released over 109 disease anchors (smoke_v0); 3,752 computed. The model reads one slot per anchor.Gate F v0Expression84 genes, the union of two Caris MI Profile panels (10 of them from the 2024 specimen). Full WTS is ingested but unused: 59,960 genes, 17,604 in the foundation vocabulary.#212, #454KG exportOnly Biolink predicate is exported, never source_predicate. PrimeKG’s ~30 relations become ~20 labels. DDI and PPI share interacts_with (73% of test triples). Drug→protein roles are lost (display_relation is dropped at ingest).#592, #438CombinationsNone modeled; CIViC/OncoKB combinations are split into single-drug edges.#316, #594Metro MapHand-curated YAML (McLelland), uncited, not connected to KG reasoning or training.#595, #89, #90Treatments83 registry rows, mostly Translator auto-seeds. 0 suggestions, 1 candidate entry, no meetings/claims model, no trials connector.#565, #28CohortsDesigned, nothing built.#327, #316Public notebookLast deployed 2026-09-27 18:05 UTC, before #448’s corrections merged (2026-09-28 17:18 UTC). An editorial note-to-self is visible on live MapleLog pages.#589Her recordNothing has arrived since 2026-05-08 except one lab. The last Signatera report on file is 2026-03-03.#512, #131G1 (the list)Never shipped.[[MODS_MISSION_SPEC
Since then (2026-10-05): Arm A at 40 epochs became the checkpoint of record. It passed gates S3 and S4, then failed S5 and S6 on 2026-10-04: for her query it still ranks drugs mostly by popularity. Kaiser documents from after May began to arrive on 2026-10-02, when the backfill ran (#621). Decided cards are marked in §7, and the ledger (#599) holds the current state. The plan below is as approved on 2026-10-01.
2. The thesis
Two spines run in parallel. The Research Steward drives both, and Richard’s time goes only to
decisions.

Spine A: earn a signal. Make the base ranker beat popularity, then make personalization beat
the base ranker. Judge both on labels with n ≫ 1 (cell lines, organoids), with RGCC as a
secondary do-no-harm check.
Spine B: ship a list. An Options Ledger organized by decision horizon (Maintain / Prevent
while NED / Prepare for recurrence). It is fed by trials, cohorts, measured combination data and
the metabolic work, and by the model only once it has passed its gates. G1 never depends on
the model.

Spine A alone repeats the last nine months: machine first, list later. Spine B alone abandons the
project’s distinctive bet. B also gives A a destination, because every model candidate enters the
Ledger with its evidence.
The lesson that shapes the gates: the project polished inputs (PRS) before testing the model
that consumes them, and a ten-minute degree baseline would have exposed the model months earlier.
So in Q4, every model number ships beside the strongest non-learned baseline for its surface,
computed by committed code.

3. Spine A: earn a signal (Run #2)
3.1 Order of work

S0, no retrain. Test #523’s shortcut hypothesis on the existing foundation.
Evaluation rebuild (#593):

commit the baseline scorers;
write per-triple ranks and report per relation;
rank drugs given a disease (the G1 query);
partial ρ controlling for degree;
a validation curve;
zero-shot ULTRA as a baseline.


Arm A. Retrain with entity_model.remove_one_hop: yes and nothing else changed (same export,
same split fingerprint). About $115 and about 21 h.
Arm B or B′, chosen by how A comes out:

if A passes S3/S4, Arm B is the relation-fidelity export (#592);
if A closes the shortcut but fails S3, Arm B′ is one diagnostic: more negatives (128 instead
of 10), or an ULTRA-4g warm start.
A warm start from ultra_3g cost −46% MRR on GP-KG before the evaluation fixes
(agent_hallucination_log.md B3), so it is a diagnostic, not a
default.


Mechanism A in context (playbook §9.4). Score drug-grouped folds of her RGCC edges added to
the fact graph at query time. There is no retrain, because ULTRA has no per-relation
parameters. Judged against the drug-class-mean and degree baselines.
Proxy benchmark (#591). Run PRISM first, then GDSC2, with a frozen leave-one-subject-out
split and drug-mean as the baseline. Test simple conditioned models (kNN on expression, TabPFN)
before #420.
#420, the signed criterion. Only if a conditioned baseline beats drug-mean on the proxies.
Weights start at 0, early stopping uses the criterion’s own loss, and λ is applied at score
time.

Cap: two foundation retrains in Q4. Week-7 review (D19): if the best arm fails S4 and S6,
foundation work stops. The KG then supplies evidence paths only, and the budget moves to proxies.
3.2 The baseline rule (D11)
Every model number is reported beside the strongest non-learned baseline for that surface, computed
on exactly the same items by committed code. “Signal” means the paired-bootstrap 95% CI of
(model − baseline) excludes 0. A result that is above zero but not above its baseline is written up
as “no signal beyond popularity.”

























SurfaceBaselinesHeld-out link predictionper-relation tail frequency; degree; zero-shot ULTRADrugs ranked given a disease (G1 query)treats-subject count; degreeRGCC, per drawdegree (partial ρ given degree); drug-class meanProxies (across subjects)drug-mean (scores exactly 0 within-drug)
Per-relation reporting. Every held-out eval writes per-triple ranks. The stored table gives, per
predicate (and per source_predicate once the export carries it), the n, filtered MRR and Hits@10
for the model and every baseline. The headline macro-average excludes interacts_with. The G1 query
gets its own row.
3.3 Pre-registered gates
M4 (export hygiene), M9 (provenance) and M10 (venue) carry over from the smoke run unchanged.
Nothing is scored until D11–D20 are settled in the ledger, and no metric is looked at until its whole
grid is computed.




























































#CheckPasses whenS0Shortcut diagnosis (no retrain)On f1228371, 500 training triples: filtered MRR with the query edge and its mirror removed is ≤ 1/5 of the MRR with the query edge alone removed. If not, remove_one_hop isn’t the fix; go to B′ (D12).S1Clean A/BArm A’s split fingerprint = 4518539f…, and the resolved config differs only by entity_model.remove_one_hop: yes.S2Shortcut closedThe S0 probe on Arm A drops by at most 2×. A fixed 5K validation MRR is logged every 5 epochs. Training extends to 40 epochs only if the last two checkpoints are still rising.S3Held-out edges vs baselinesOn the same 50K sample, Δ MRR vs per-relation tail frequency has a CI above 0, both micro and macro (relations with n ≥ 1,000). Zero-shot ULTRA and degree are reported alongside.S4Indication recovery (G1 query)On held-out treats edges, drugs ranked given the disease among drug-domain candidates: Δ vs treats-subject count has a CI above 0.S5Not just popularitySpearman(score, degree) over the ~7,800 drug candidates for her CRC query is ≤ 0.6 (today 0.86). The top 10 come with paths (MODE=explain_paths), at least 3 of them mechanistic or personal.S6RGCC (secondary)Graded panel, per draw: partial ρ(score, RGCC given degree) has a CI above 0 on both draws. BRAF/MEK/EGFR agents are excluded, and test-retest is printed.S7Proxy benchmark is validThe frozen LOSO split is registered on #591 before any model runs. The drug-mean baseline is stored. The positive control (pan-cancer BRAF V600E → BRAF-inhibitor response, AUROC ≥ 0.75) is in the data and recovered. HT-29 is reported and never tuned on.S8Personalization (G3)LOSO on colorectal lines: mean within-drug, across-line Spearman has a CI above 0, and across-drug performance is no worse than drug-mean. For #420: on synthetic fits, s_resistant < 0 < s_sensitive, and at least 20% of adjusted drugs move up. On Maureen, Mission Spec §9’s Δρ ≥ 0.05 counts only with a CI above 0 and above degree.S9ProvenanceBaselines come from committed scripts and are stored as validation-result rows named by variant.
3.4 Decisions Richard makes before launch (D11–D20)
Recommendations are mine. Each one is a card in the ledger, and none is settled until Richard ticks
it.




























































#DecisionRecommendationD11Adopt the baseline rule (§3.2)Adopt.D12Retrain armsCap at two. Arm A is remove_one_hop only. Then B (relation fidelity) if A passes S3/S4, or B′ (one diagnostic) if A fails S3.D13Export relation identity (#592)Option B: Biolink predicate + source qualifier for every source predicate. That invents no new ontology mapping and drops no distinction. Drug-protein roles need a PrimeKG display_relation re-ingest; do it in Q4 if it is cheap, otherwise disclose. #438’s wrong merges: disclose now, fix with the re-ingest.D14Candidate set for her queryDrug-domain only. CIViC/OncoKB therapy and regimen entities are decomposed through the regimen tables or reported separately, never silently mixed in.D15RGCC’s role, and #324RGCC becomes secondary (S6). #324: declare the pre-smoke RGCC numbers void instead of restating them one by one.D16Proxy datasetsPRISM Repurposing first, GDSC2 as replication. CTRPv2, organoids and PDXE move to Q1 2027.D17Shared gene axis (#212)Drug-target genes present in both her WTS and the proxies’ expression, plus pathway-activity scores. One normalization for both.D18#420 parameterization (ii)Hierarchical, built per-type first: per-type effects in v0, with a per-entity residual added when the proxies support it. Weights start at 0.D19Week-7 reviewIf the best arm fails S4 and S6, stop foundation work; the KG supplies evidence paths only.D20Run #2 moneyInside the $500/month steward budget. Pre-registered jobs are pre-approved. Any single job above the steward’s approval threshold asks. Every job is estimated before launch and cancelled at 1.5× its estimate.

4. Spine B: ship a list
4.1 The Options Ledger (#565, #28)
Sequencing per #565. First consolidate docs/maureen_candidate_treatments.md to 5–10 real
entries, then derive the schema from their shape. The catalog consolidation is running now.
Draft schema, to be checked against the entries. It gets its own tables, and
ModsIntervention stays the patient-agnostic knowledge base:

































TablePurpose and key fieldsmods_optionHer candidate: kind {drug, combination, procedure, cell_therapy, vaccine, trial, supplement, lifestyle, monitoring_test}, target_condition, horizon {maintain, prevent_while_ned, prepare_for_recurrence}, status {researching, discussed_with_clinician, pursuing, started, declined, parked}, evidence_level, fit (facts, each with its source; a fact without a source doesn’t render), safety_vs_regimen {none_known, monitor, caution, avoid, unknown}, access_path, cost, readout (how benefit would ever be seen), next_step, decision_due, origin {human, model_run, llm_report, seed}mods_option_eventAppend-only history of status changes and decisionsmods_claimEvery claim a clinic, company or paper makes: type, source kind, verification {unverified, verified, contradicted, stale}, expires_at (30 days for trial status)mods_partyOrganizations and people. Never published.mods_meetingDate, parties, options discussed, summary, follow-upsmods_trialClinicalTrials.gov v2 cache: overall_status, why_stopped, eligibility, locations, fetched_at

Routes and UI. Routes mount in backend/mods_clinic_api.py, which main.py already includes,
so no registry hotspots are touched. A “Options” tab goes in the clinic view of
ModsLabDashboard.jsx: a board by horizon, a detail drawer with sourced facts, claims and their
verification badges, trials with their last-checked date, and a “Stale” filter. Desktop only.
Trials connector. Refreshed weekly; it alerts on status changes. A BATTMAN-style termination
must never again reach us through a press release.
Ranking. A transparent rubric: evidence × fit × safety × access × reversibility. It is a ranking
you can argue with, not a score.
The migration is a production schema change, because main.py applies migrations at startup.
Its merge waits for Richard’s schema card.

4.2 The G1 brief
The G1 brief is a rendering of the Ledger organized by horizon, with at most three options per
horizon in v0. G1 definition of done: Mission Spec §9’s fields (mechanism, evidence level, her
supporting data, interaction and contraindication flags, access path), plus “discussed with a
clinician.”
4.3 People like Maureen (#590, #591)

Guardrails.

Other patients never become KG nodes (Richard, 2026-06: population conditioning, not
patients-as-nodes).
Cohorts are validation and decision support, never a repurposing signal.
A single-patient table cannot learn personalization, so cohorts and proxies are what make G3
identifiable.


Cohort funnel (#590, running).

MSK-CHORD: public, 25,040 tumors, 24,028 treatment records, CC BY-NC-ND.
Other cBioPortal CRC studies.
Neighbors v0 is a two-week spike with one pre-registered question, proposed from the
funnel: how long BRAF/EGFR therapy holds in disease without liver metastases, and what patients
received next.


Her cell-line twin. HT-29 carries the exact APC c.4666dupA found in her tumour, plus BRAF V600E and MSS (verified
in Cellosaurus 2026-10-01). It also has TP53 R273H, SMAD4 and PIK3CA changes her tumour doesn’t carry,
so it is a sentinel, never a tuning target.

4.4 Combinations (#594)

Q4 adds a combination evidence column to the Ledger, filled from measured data: NCI ALMANAC
(the NCI-60 colon panel includes HT-29 and COLO 205) and Jaaks 2022.
Positive control: BRAF + EGFR synergy in BRAF-mutant colon lines. ALMANAC tests small
molecules, so its pair is likely a BRAF inhibitor plus an EGFR TKI; verify that the pair exists.
Q1 2027: regimen entities in the graph and learned combination scoring.

4.5 Metro (#595): a priority lane
Decided 2026-10-05 (D-Q4-04, #612): Metro is not reduced.

Why. The Metro Map is the only Maple feature Maureen has asked about or researched. A useful
Metro is the fastest way to get her using the system, and her use is the only user feedback the
project will get. So Metro and the metabolic hypotheses are among the most important parts of the
research. They sit beside PDR, not in place of it.
Scope. As much as current data and architecture allow. The therapy-adaptation layer, new
metabolic sources and a patient metabolic model are back in scope where they fit. None of them is
required this year.
Standing rule. Ask of any new work how it could feed Metro, and where Metro’s ideas could apply
elsewhere: the Options Ledger, the G1 brief, model candidate lists.
The wider bet. The repurposing engine need not stop at single prescription drugs. It can be
pointed at a combination of metabolic changes, brought on by diet, drugs or something else.

Order of work. The plan is on #595, as a starting point for Richard rather than a decision. In
outline:

Safe to read, and hers. Every station gets a badge against her current regimen, cited to the
drug labels. Today the map lists itraconazole, a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, and the Braftovi label
says to avoid those. A plain-language key goes with it. “Ask about this” and “Add to my options”
write to the Options Ledger; that is the feedback channel.
Ground it. Every station→line claim carries a KG path through a target edge, or a citation
checked against a primary source. An unsupported claim is shown as unsupported.
Light it from her WTS percentiles against the Caris colorectal reference, for both
colorectal specimens (the 2024 primary and the 2025 recurrence), with the caveats beside it.
Widen it. Her systemic metabolism (labs first, then measurement-trait PRS after D-Q4-11),
diet and supplement stations under the same safety screen, and combinations on the map with #594.
Research. Stations suggested by the graph (judged against degree, D11), therapy-adaptation
claims as cited claims, model scores once a foundation passes its gates, and a patient metabolic
model as a stretch spike.

On “fundamentally metabolic.” D-Q4-04 doesn’t turn on this question. Metro is a priority because
it is the surface she uses, and the testable form below is one of the things it should help test.
Claude’s view, recorded for the record: the evidence doesn’t support it for her tumor.

Her tumor has a canonical driver, and the one intervention with a measured, dramatic effect
targets that driver’s signaling loop. ctDNA went from 20.74 to 0.15 MTM/mL in about four weeks and
has been negative since 2025-12-05.
BRAF V600E does rewire metabolism in targetable ways (Yun 2015, Science: high-dose vitamin C and
GAPDH).
MAPK-blockade survivors are thought to shift toward oxidative metabolism. That is established in
melanoma and open in CRC.

So the testable form is: her driver creates metabolic dependencies, and her maintenance therapy
creates new ones. That lands on the NED question: what kills the cells her regimen doesn’t?

5. Background lanes













































LaneQ4 scopeIssueRecord freshness (week 1)Records since 2026-05-08, Signatera after 2026-03-03 (needs Richard’s portal access), the Signatera parser#512, #131Safety (week 1)Is she taking anything new? If so, screen it against encorafenib, binimetinib and cetuximab first.ledgerNotebook (week 1)Fix PR running; the redeploy is Richard’s call#589PRS v1Settle NR scale policy (+18 anchors on its own), #428 → #422 (palindromes, +8 alone, up to +71 together), parameterize the release tag; D2/D3 on the v1 candidate set only; defer ancestry PCs (#429) with the EUR basis documented#295, #422, #428Expression axis v3D17, shared with the proxies; becomes Spine A critical path once #591 lands#212SocialDraft → approve (Richard, 2026-10-01). 6. Calendar (Pacific time; PDT ends Nov 1)

9. Deferred to Q1 2027

Learned combination scoring, and regimen entities in the graph.
A patient-specific genome-scale metabolic model (Human-GEM constrained by her WTS), validated
against HT-29’s measured dependencies. Unfenced by D-Q4-04: in scope this year where it fits
(§4.5).
