D1 (mods_prs_panel_af) md5-checks every panel file against the panel’s own
checksums.txt, streams the .pvar.zst keeping the records at union positions (the index D2
scores through), then reads those records from the .pgen in position blocks and counts
alleles over the 3,330 unrelated samples, overall and per super-population. The product is
union_panel_af.tsv.gz: one line per union target, with af_effect, af_other and an per
group, read forward exactly as the union wrote the alleles. That is the panel half of the
palindrome comparison. Both alleles are given because at a split multiallelic site one is
not 1 − the other. D1 also measures the autosomal missing-call rate over the union’s own
sites (the #404 spike saw ~2.4 % on random panel variants), and it records its provenance,
including the archive checksum, on a gate_d1_panel_frequencies run row.
D2 (mods_prs_panel_score) resolves every scoring row once into an oriented weight on an
allele slot, then streams the panel records it touches in sorted blocks, adding one sparse
product per block into the n_scores × n_samples accumulator. Three properties are
enforced, not assumed:

Same policy. The policy is her stored Gate C dict, rebuilt with
ScoringPolicy.from_dict, which refuses a dict whose fingerprint it cannot reproduce. The
E2 rows are such dicts (they predate two policy fields), so a real D2 waits for E3. A
golden test also scores every fixture panel sample through score_variants and requires
agreement, under the default policy and every per-file variant.
Same missingness rule. A missing panel hardcall is dropped, as her no-calls are, and
never imputed. Every matrix row records the mean matched rows dropped per panel sample
beside her own count, so “the two deflations match” is a per-score measurement. Smoke
run #1 measured that they did not: over the 594 v0 scores her dropped share sat a median
2.3 points above the panel’s (GH #499).
Same locus set. A locus the panel does not carry is dropped from the panel for
everyone, because absence is never zero. Her Gate C sum still includes it, so she would be
compared on loci the panel never saw. At a REF-effect row that is a systematic +2w on
her side only, which is the REF-effect bug’s shape one level up. D2 therefore scores her in
the same pass from her Gate A callset, as one more column under the same rules.
run_gate_d.py places that panel-aligned score and names it in
percentile_v1.score_basis, beside her unchanged gate_c_raw_score. Since
gate_d2_panel_scorer_v2 (GH #499) the rule also runs from her side: a locus she has no
call at is dropped from every panel sample too. v1 dropped it from her column alone, which
moves her z by roughly gap × panel mean / sd, a predicted −5.5 SD on PGS005253. The header
says patient_missing_masked; run_gate_d.py refuses a patient column without it unless
--allow-unmasked-patient-missingness is passed, which percentile_v1 then records.

The site rules are as follows. Split biallelic SNV records at one position form a site,
whose REF count is ploidy − Σ ALT. An allele never observed at a called site counts 0,
since it is called absent. An SNV row with no SNV record at its position is
not_in_panel, and so is any indel without an exact record match, because indel
representation is not canonical. Males outside the chrX PARs, and on chrY, are dropped in D2
(Gate C refuses a non-diploid call) and counted once in D1.
Scoring rows are parsed once. The panel is re-read once per batch of scores that fits
--max-batch-rows, at ~12 B per matched row held and ~36 B per row peak while its CSR is
built, so batch size trades memory for panel passes. A pass is bound by the Windows bind
mount, which the #404 spike measured at ~16.6k records/s in order and ~1k/s scattered, so
the real run should stage the .pgen on container-local storage first. Shards split the
eligible list LPT on n_variants. --step merge refuses parts that disagree on panel,
policy, samples or patient column.

The open question was whether the 1,520 EAF-less scores could be oriented by some other
signal, and the lead was hm_source: if its ENSEMBL value meant “matched to a
strand-defined variant record”, ~45 % of deferred rows would need no frequency at all.
It does not. hm_source is the provenance of the coordinate, written by the
harmonizer’s HmPOS pass, which never reads or writes an allele; strand lives in a
separate HmVCF pass whose output the Catalog does not publish, and which labels
palindromes ambiguous rather than resolving them. Four lines of evidence, the blunt one
being that in PGS005393 hm_source = ENSEMBL labels 26,901 forward-strand rows and
26,801 reverse-complemented ones in the same file.
Two consequences carry forward. The EAF route is the only route, and it delivers
8.48 % of the fleet’s deferred palindromic rows once frequencies within 0.08 of 0.5
are excluded as undecidable — not the 9.5 % headline. And scoring files coded in Illumina’s
A/B convention are real and identifiable: their unambiguous SNVs are all A/C or A/G,
their strand is per-variant and unrecorded, and a blanket forward-strand assumption is
refuted by counterexample rather than merely unproven.
Full answer, the fleet-wide hm_source distribution and the recommended policy:
`prs_validation/palindrome_orientation_spike.md`.
But the EAF route is not the only one left, and the spike is what opened the other
(GH #404, 2026-09-27). Since harmonization
never touches alleles, a file’s non-palindromic rows are a direct readout of its author’s
strand convention — and 99.899 % of the 64.8M deferred palindromic rows sit in files that
match the reference forward at ≥ 99.9 %, against 8.48 % reachable by declared frequency.
Reading those palindromes forward is an inference about that file from thousands of
measured rows, not the blanket assumption §5.4 refutes. Its one failure mode — a pipeline
that orients unambiguous variants and leaves palindromes alone, which real sumstats
harmonisers do — is what the 167 EAF-carrying scores exist to measure. Decide it with D1,
before D2.
Measured the same day, without waiting for D1 — the licence holds per class of file, not
for the 99.899 %. The spike read the panel directly and tested the 167 EAF-carrying scores.

49 publications) and ≤ 0.12 % in genome-wide files. But the failure mode is real:
PGS000020 (7,502 rows, 0.175 % complement-only) has ~40 % of its palindromes reversed, so
the rate is necessary and not sufficient. The recommendation licenses the small class (527
scores, median 11.3 % of each score’s rows). It puts the genome-wide class (98.8 % of the

and refuses 1k–100k. The mechanism, ScoringPolicy.palindrome_forward_scores, ships empty

computed values across the full eligible set rather than on theoretical bounds. This is
the empirical case that raw sums cannot feed the PDR2 loss (§1.4) and therefore that Gate
D is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

No blend remains. All 2,321 E1 rows are superseded; zero quarantined rows carry the
old callset. The cheap invariant that proves it — and the one that would have caught the
hazard earlier — is the gate_a.n_records fingerprint on mods_polygenic_score.metadata:
select run_id, validity, metadata->'gate_a'->>'n_records', count(*)
from mods_polygenic_score group by 1,2,3;
Anything other than one n_records value across the live quarantined rows means a
mixed-callset fleet. That is a real hazard, not a hypothetical: the Gate C resume
predicate keys on SCORER_VERSION alone and is blind to the callset
(GH #360). SCORER_VERSION was unchanged
between E1 and E2 while the callset changed completely, so a default resume=True would
have skipped every score that already had an E1 row and silently produced exactly that
blend — both halves reconciling, both inside bounds, nothing downstream distinguishing
them. E2 was run with resume=False over an explicitly computed work list for this reason.
Operational notes worth carrying into Gate D:

The callset measured 8.45 GB resident, 498 B/record — not the 407 B/record E1
measured. Scaling the previous measured figure would have been 22 % low, so
B/record is a property of the particular union, not of DenseCallset (§5.3).
Budget concurrency against the Docker VM (30.7 GB), not the Windows host (62.8 GB
total / 35.5 GB free at the time). The host figure nearly authorised 4 shards where 2
was right.
Shard count and concurrency are separate knobs, and run_gate_e.py --shards conflates
them by design (it assumes N shards = N workers). E2 wanted 20 shards for restart
resilience — a killed shard restarts from zero, so small slices bound the loss — and 2-way
concurrency for memory. The lever that expresses both is a pipeline_config row
(stage_name='mods_prs_compute', enabled=1, max_concurrent=2), which the claim path
enforces race-free under pg_advisory_xact_lock. Delete the row afterwards or the
task type stays throttled forever. LPT balance over n_variants came out at 1.00×, and
all 20 shards completed first try with zero retries.

prs/smoke_v0_disease_mapping.content:
smoke_v0 disease mapping (D7): proposal for approval
Refs #430, #439 (decisions D6 and D7), #296, #244. Playbook: docs/mods_smoke_run_1_playbook.md §1.3, §3 (D6, D7) and §5.1 step 3.

Outcome (2026-09-29). This table was approved in PR #460 (2026-09-28), and backend/scripts/prs/build_smoke_v0_mapping_tsv.py now writes it. Gate F then released 590 of the 594 scores, over all 109 anchors, as smoke_v0 (release run c3be9df0). The four it held back were non-pick alternates that failed the post-D3 panel-coverage rule. Below is the proposal as it stood on 2026-09-28.


Nothing here is written to code or to the database. Choosing a disease anchor is an ontology mapping, so under the CLAUDE.md hard rule Richard approves the table before #430, #296 or #244 writes it. Every number below was measured on 2026-09-28 against the live quarantined E2 rows. They are re-measured on the E3 rows before release (§8). The document holds ids and counts only: no raw, z or percentile score values.

Summary

The #296 funnel reproduces exactly through R7 (3,752 → 1,861). R8, counted the way #296 counted it, gives 736 scores over 148 anchors, against #296’s 738 over 149. The whole gap is basal cell carcinoma (2 scores). It has no node in the composition under either spelling of its id (J10).
D7’s v0 exclusions then take the set to 594 scores over 109 diseases. They remove 24 multi-trait scores and 118 scores whose disease PrimeKG holds only inside a grouped node. The playbook’s “738 scores over 149 diseases” (D6, and the check in §5.1 step 3) is the count before D7. If this table is approved, that check should expect 594 / 109 on the E3 rows.
The CRC anchor is confirmed as MONDO:0005575 “Colorectal Cancer”. PrimeKG’s colorectal cancer node is merged into it under the padded CURIE, alongside CIViC and ClinVar. It has 7 drug neighbours: 5 through treats, 1 through contraindicated_for and 1 through has_off_label_use. The playbook’s “10 / 2 / 2” counts export lines, and every drug–disease pair is written in both directions. PrimeKG’s MONDO:24331 “colorectal carcinoma” has gene associations only (§5).
Of the 109 diseases, 94 are unambiguous and 15 are flagged, across nine judgement calls (J1–J9). J10 is an exclusion, so it has no row.
Two traps for whoever implements #430.

The scoring-file header maps all 9 v0 colorectal cancer scores to EFO_0005842. A mapping read from mods_prs_score_manifest.trait_efo would therefore lose the index disease.
The pickle reader settles ties in computed_at order. The chosen score for each disease therefore has to be written down explicitly (§8).



1. The funnel

R1–R7 match #296’s comment row for row.
R8 removes 1,125 scores:

1,123 carry no MONDO trait: EFO only 835, OBA only 239, HP only 35, EFO + OBA 10, and EFO + PATO 4. D7 excludes HP-only and EFO disease-like traits, and this is the step where they go.
2 carry a MONDO trait that no node in the composition carries: basal cell carcinoma (J10).

“Anchors” counts graph nodes. Several MONDO ids can share one grouped node, so the R8 and single-trait rows count fewer anchors than MONDO ids.
2. The rules applied
R1–R7, read from each row’s metadata:

R1: gate_c.weight_scale = 'additive'.
R2: gate_c.within_theoretical_bounds and gate_c.reconciles.
R3: gate_c.outcomes.scored ≥ 1.
R4: coverage_v1.structural_overlap, matched_rows / scoring_rows ≥ 0.90.
R5: gate_c.outcomes.ambiguous_palindromic = 0. These are the palindromic rows that reached orientation, the ones whose value depends on the pending palindrome decision.
R6: gate_c.n_complement_only_match / (scored + ref_allele_mismatch) ≤ 0.05, the same rate mods_prs_pipeline_service.strand_profile uses.
R7: coverage_v1.genotype_callability, callable_loci / matched_rows ≥ 0.90.

R8 and D7:

Trait source. The cached PGS REST metadata.json (trait_efo), cached 2026-07-09 to 2026-07-11. The REST value is the current mapping. The scoring-file header is what mods_prs_score_manifest.trait_efo holds, and it disagrees on 50 eligible scores. 36 of those are colorectal cancer, where the header still says EFO_0005842.
MONDO only. EFO, HP, OBA and PATO traits are not mapped.
Single trait. The REST trait list has exactly one entry. J9 covers how to read this rule.
Anchor. Take a node that carries the trait’s MONDO number under either spelling (MONDO:5148 or MONDO:0005148) and is in the composition:

if two such nodes exist, take the one that carries PrimeKG’s source (J1);
if there is no PrimeKG node, take the single CIViC/ClinVar/OncoKB node;
if only a MONDO_grouped: node carries the id, exclude it (D7);
if no node carries it, exclude it.


Vocabulary. maureen_focus_v1 as registered today: version v1, is_locked = false, last updated 2026-05-18 20:34 UTC. Its members are civic, clinvar, oncokb, pharmgkb_variants, and prime_kg minus the anatomy, cellular_component, molecular_function and exposure domains. The entity set is ModsKGCompositionService.build_filter’s SQL, verbatim. Relation counts follow materialize(): the relation comes from a member source, and both of its ends are in the set.

Cross-check: all 109 anchors appear in the de-facto foundation’s export on disk (916bdd2c, runs/2026-05-18_maureen_focus_v1/data/{train,valid,test}.txt).
The final check is against the new export’s vocabulary, after #432.


One score per disease. Take the most scored loci: snps_used, which equals Gate C’s outcomes.scored on every surviving row. This is today’s reader rule.

Tie-break: the lower PGS accession number.
J6–J8 propose overrides where the rule’s pick is wrong for her.



3. How many rows are clear

























Diseasesv0 scoresUnambiguous94492Flagged by J1–J915102Total109594
How each anchor was resolved:

exact (93): PrimeKG’s MONDO:<n>, the only node that carries the id.
exact, twin (5): PrimeKG’s MONDO:<n>, with a padded twin also in the vocabulary (J1).
padded, merged (8): only the padded CURIE is in the vocabulary, and PrimeKG’s node is merged into it.
padded, no PrimeKG (3): only the padded CURIE, carried by CIViC or ClinVar.

These are notes, not calls:


27 anchors (62 v0 scores) have no drug neighbour in the composition (no drugs). The personalization adjustment is one hop (evaluate_personalized_maple.py), so their PRS cannot move any drug. The edge-type breakdown in M7 will show this.


8 anchors are thin (thin): 5 or fewer in-composition relation ends. Check these first against the #432 export.


Umbrella classes have the most drug neighbours, and most of them are contraindications. Liver disorder has 644, every one through contraindicated_for. Hypertensive disorder has 403, and diabetes mellitus 381. The adjustment is edge-blind, so these push drugs the same way an indication would (#420). Worth knowing when reading M7.


Some diseases share the axis with their parent or child class. D7 keys by exact id and merges nothing, so a drug next to both nodes gets both adjustments. Examples:

urinary bladder cancer and urinary bladder carcinoma, which PrimeKG links to the same 12 drugs;
colorectal cancer and colorectal carcinoma (J3);
melanoma and cutaneous melanoma;
heart failure and congestive heart failure.

That is acceptable for a machinery test.


4. Judgement calls (the flagged rows)







































































#CallAffectsRecommendationJ1MONDO twins. Both spellings of the id are in the vocabulary. The padded twins are ClinVar or CIViC nodes, some of them merged with a GP-KG node that is named by a UMLS CUI. They have 1–16 in-composition relation ends and no drug neighbours. The PrimeKG nodes have 72–364.stroke disorder (17 scores); acquired polycythemia vera, lung carcinoma, seborrheic keratosis, urinary bladder cancer (1 each)Key to PrimeKG’s node, MONDO:<n>. The same rule, “take the node that carries PrimeKG’s source”, is what makes CRC’s anchor the padded MONDO:0005575. The twin defect itself is #438.J2Hypothyroidism. The only non-grouped node is ClinVar’s MONDO:0005420, with 1 relation end and no drugs. PrimeKG holds hypothyroidism only inside MONDO_grouped:5420_16412_15777 (3 conditions, 115 drug neighbours), which D7 excludes.hypothyroidism (10 scores)Keep it, keyed to MONDO:0005420. It is the exact class, and it is in the vocabulary. The position will be measured, and it will move no drug. If its one relation does not survive the #432 export, drop the disease. The alternative is to drop it now.J3Colorectal carcinoma. The Catalog maps 8 scores to MONDO_0024331, but all of them report “Colorectal cancer” (one says “Colorectal neoplasm”). PrimeKG’s MONDO:24331 has gene associations only.colorectal carcinoma → MONDO:24331 (8 scores)Keep it as its own position. Don’t fold it into the index anchor. Folding would be a carcinoma → cancer mapping. The index pick is the same either way: the best MONDO_0024331 score has 1,073,979 loci, against PGS003395’s 1,116,726.J4The index disease’s score. Most loci picks PGS003395, a PRS-CSx --meta score (Xin 2023). Its discovery GWAS was 65.6% EAS and 34.4% EUR, of 324,079 people. Two of its three evaluations were in EUR samples.colorectal cancer (9 scores)Keep PGS003395. The EUR-only alternative is PGS003431 (LDpred2-inf, Briggs 2022, 1,077,026 loci). Its GWAS is 67,878 EUR people. PGS003395’s EUR share alone is about 111,000.J5Tie. PGS003972 and PGS003973 both score 1,090,924 loci. They are PRSAAA and PRSAAA_woUKB: the same PRS-CS model, the second trained without UK Biobank.abdominal aortic aneurysm (4 scores)Accept the tie-break: PGS003972.J6Six-way tie. PGS005073–PGS005078 score 1,252,829 loci each. They are Gunn 2024 LDpred builds that differ only in their GWAS summary statistics and LD reference. REST records the same ancestry for all six, so only their names tell them apart. The tie-break would take PGS005073: AFR summary statistics, AFR LD.congestive heart failure (15 scores)Override to PGS005074 (EURss_eurld: EUR summary statistics, EUR LD).J7The same six-way tie, PGS005034–PGS005039. For CKD, most loci picks PGS005090, “CKD_PRS_AA” (Jones 2024). It was built for Black American populations, and its GWAS and evaluation were 100% AFR. It beats PGS003988 by 114 of 1,113,329 loci. PE: keep it, since there is no alternative. Picks whose GWAS includes Europeans stay as they are, including the multi-ancestry “MAE” picks: Graves, Hashimoto, thyroid carcinoma, preeclampsia, ulcerative colitis and nephrotic syndrome. So does CRC (J4). Glioblastoma’s only score reports no ancestry.J9What “multi-trait” means. This table reads it as “the REST trait list has more than one entry, in any ontology”, which removes 24 scores. The looser reading, “two or more MONDO traits”, would remove 16. It would keep 8 more: PGS001844 and PGS002056 (phlebitis + HP thrombophlebitis), PGS001861 and PGS002072 (cholelithiasis + HP cholecystitis), PGS002045 (eye disorder + EFO eye inflammation), PGS002768 (osteoporosis + EFO heel bone mineral density), and PGS005262 and PGS005263 (nodular goiter + EFO “benign”).cholelithiasis and osteoporosis (their picks would change); phlebitis, eye disorder and nodular goiter (would be added)The strict reading, as tabled. Each of the 8 is a combined or proxy phenotype. The loose reading would swap osteoporosis’s pick for a heel-BMD score (PGS002768), and cholelithiasis’s 12-locus pick for PGS002072 (cholecystitis + cholelithiasis).J10Basal cell carcinoma, MONDO_0020804 (PGS003416, PGS003417). No node in the composition carries this id, under either spelling. RTX-KG2 has one, but RTX-KG2 is not a member. The nearest node in the vocabulary is MONDO:0005341 “Basal Cell Carcinoma” (PrimeKG and CIViC). RTX-KG2 records it as a subclass of MONDO:0020804, and also, contradictorily, as an exact_match.not in the tableExclude it from v0. A parent → child mapping is not exact. This one exclusion is the whole gap between 738 / 149 and 736 / 148.

MONDO:0005575 “Colorectal Cancer” (entity 257724). Its sources:

civic (civic_disease:9256);

prime_kg (PrimeKG node 28849, merged under the padded CURIE);

There is no MONDO:5575 entity.


Every drug edge on it is PrimeKG’s, and each is stored in both directions:

treats: fluorouracil, trifluridine, tipiracil, carmofur and cetuximab;
has_off_label_use: oxaliplatin;

A.1 smoke_v0_d7_repro.py: the funnel, R8, D7, the picks and the table
"""smoke_v0 D7 disease mapping: the whole funnel in one read-only pass.
 
Run inside a worker container (it has DATABASE_URL and mounts the PGS cache):
    docker exec -i maple-worker-1 python - < smoke_v0_d7_repro.py > v0_repro.json
 
Read-only: SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY on the DB, and only reads of the cached PGS REST
metadata (/app/worker/data/pgs_catalog/PGS######/metadata.json). Selects ids and counts
only -- never raw_score, z_score or percentile.
"""
import json, os, sys, collections
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
 
PATIENT = 'PATIENT_UUID'
COMPOSITION = 'maureen_focus_v1'
CACHE = '/app/worker/data/pgs_catalog'
DRUG_PREDICATES = ('biolink:treats', 'biolink:contraindicated_for', 'biolink:has_off_label_use')
 
# ---- R1-R7 (#296), over the live quarantined rows ---------------------------------
RULES = """
WITH base AS (
  SELECT pgs_id, snps_used,
         metadata->'gate_c'      AS g,
         metadata->'coverage_v1' AS cov
  FROM mods_polygenic_score
  WHERE patient_id = :patient AND validity = 'quarantined'
), f AS (
  SELECT pgs_id, snps_used, g, cov,
    (g->>'weight_scale') = 'additive'                                             AS r1,
    coalesce((g->>'within_theoretical_bounds')::boolean, false)
      AND coalesce((g->>'reconciles')::boolean, false)                            AS r2,
    coalesce((g->'outcomes'->>'scored')::bigint, 0) >= 1                          AS r3,
    (cov->'structural_overlap'->>'matched_rows')::numeric
      / nullif((cov->'structural_overlap'->>'scoring_rows')::numeric, 0) >= 0.90  AS r4,
    coalesce((g->'outcomes'->>'ambiguous_palindromic')::bigint, 0) = 0            AS r5,
    coalesce((g->>'n_complement_only_match')::numeric
      / nullif(coalesce((g->'outcomes'->>'scored')::bigint,0)
             + coalesce((g->'outcomes'->>'ref_allele_mismatch')::bigint,0), 0), 0) <= 0.05 AS r6,
    (cov->'genotype_callability'->>'callable_loci')::numeric
      / nullif((cov->'genotype_callability'->>'matched_rows')::numeric, 0) >= 0.90 AS r7
  FROM base
)
"""
FUNNEL = RULES + """
SELECT count(*)                                                        AS quarantined,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r1)                                      AS r1,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r1 AND r2)                               AS r2,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r1 AND r2 AND r3)                        AS r3,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r1 AND r2 AND r3 AND r4)                 AS r4,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r1 AND r2 AND r3 AND r4 AND r5)          AS r5,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r1 AND r2 AND r3 AND r4 AND r5 AND r6)   AS r6,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r1 AND r2 AND r3 AND r4 AND r5 AND r6 AND coalesce(r7, false)) AS r7
FROM f
"""
SURVIVORS = RULES + """
SELECT f.pgs_id, f.snps_used, (f.g->'outcomes'->>'scored')::bigint AS scored,
       m.trait_efo AS header_trait            -- the scoring-file header, for the J-note only
FROM f LEFT JOIN mods_prs_score_manifest m ON m.pgs_id = f.pgs_id
WHERE r1 AND r2 AND r3 AND r4 AND r5 AND r6 AND coalesce(r7, false)
ORDER BY f.pgs_id
"""
# ---- every node that carries a MONDO number, and whether it is in the composition ---
ANCHORS = r"""
WITH nums AS (SELECT DISTINCT unnest(CAST(:nums AS int[])) AS n),
comp_ent AS (            -- ModsKGCompositionService.build_filter(), verbatim
  SELECT DISTINCT e.id
  FROM mods_kg_entity e
  JOIN mods_kg_entity_source es ON es.entity_id = e.id
  JOIN mods_kg_composition_member m
    ON m.source_id = es.source_id AND m.composition_id = :cid
  WHERE (m.include_domains IS NULL
         OR e.domain = ANY (SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(m.include_domains)))
    AND (m.exclude_domains IS NULL
         OR NOT (e.domain = ANY (SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(m.exclude_domains))))
),
cand AS (
  SELECT n.n, e.id, e.curie, e.name, e.domain,
         CASE WHEN e.curie = 'MONDO:' || n.n::text THEN 'unpadded' ELSE 'padded' END AS kind
  FROM nums n
  JOIN mods_kg_entity e
    ON e.curie IN ('MONDO:' || n.n::text, 'MONDO:' || lpad(n.n::text, 7, '0'))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT n.n, e.id, e.curie, e.name, e.domain, 'grouped' AS kind
  FROM nums n
  JOIN mods_kg_entity e
    ON e.curie LIKE 'MONDO\_grouped:%'
   AND n.n::text = ANY (string_to_array(split_part(e.curie, ':', 2), '_'))
),
ce AS (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM cand),
rel_side AS (            -- materialize() semantics: member source, both ends in the set
  SELECT ce.id AS eid, r.predicate, r.object_id AS other
  FROM ce JOIN mods_kg_relation r ON r.subject_id = ce.id
  JOIN mods_kg_composition_member m ON m.source_id = r.source_id AND m.composition_id = :cid
  WHERE r.object_id IN (SELECT id FROM comp_ent)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ce.id AS eid, r.predicate, r.subject_id AS other
  FROM ce JOIN mods_kg_relation r ON r.object_id = ce.id
  JOIN mods_kg_composition_member m ON m.source_id = r.source_id AND m.composition_id = :cid
  WHERE r.subject_id IN (SELECT id FROM comp_ent)
),
rel AS (
  SELECT rs.eid, count(*) AS n_rel_ends,
         count(DISTINCT rs.other) FILTER (WHERE o.domain = 'drug') AS n_drug_any,
         count(DISTINCT rs.other) FILTER (WHERE rs.predicate = ANY(:dp) AND o.domain = 'drug') AS n_drug_nbrs,
         count(DISTINCT rs.other) FILTER (WHERE rs.predicate = 'biolink:treats' AND o.domain = 'drug') AS t,
         count(DISTINCT rs.other) FILTER (WHERE rs.predicate = 'biolink:contraindicated_for' AND o.domain = 'drug') AS c,
         count(DISTINCT rs.other) FILTER (WHERE rs.predicate = 'biolink:has_off_label_use' AND o.domain = 'drug') AS o
  FROM rel_side rs JOIN mods_kg_entity o ON o.id = rs.other
  GROUP BY rs.eid
)
SELECT c.n, c.id, c.curie, c.name, c.domain, c.kind,
       (c.id IN (SELECT id FROM comp_ent)) AS in_comp,
       (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT es.source_id, ',' ORDER BY es.source_id)
          FROM mods_kg_entity_source es WHERE es.entity_id = c.id) AS sources,
       coalesce(rel.n_rel_ends, 0) AS n_rel_ends, coalesce(rel.n_drug_any, 0) AS n_drug_any,
       coalesce(rel.n_drug_nbrs, 0) AS n_drug_nbrs,
       coalesce(rel.t, 0) AS t, coalesce(rel.c, 0) AS c, coalesce(rel.o, 0) AS o
FROM cand c LEFT JOIN rel ON rel.eid = c.id
ORDER BY c.n, c.kind, c.curie
"""
 
 
def rest_traits(pgs_id):
    """The PGS REST trait list (the current mapping; the file header disagrees on 50 scores)."""
    with open(os.path.join(CACHE, pgs_id, 'metadata.json'), encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        return [(t['id'], t.get('label')) for t in (json.load(fh).get('trait_efo') or [])]
 
 
def main():
    eng = create_engine(os.environ['DATABASE_URL'])
    with eng.connect() as c:
        c.execute(text('SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY'))
        live = [list(map(str, r)) for r in c.execute(text("""
            SELECT run_id, metadata->'gate_a'->>'n_records', count(*) FROM mods_polygenic_score
            WHERE patient_id = :patient AND validity = 'quarantined' GROUP BY 1, 2"""), {'patient': PATIENT})]
        funnel = dict(c.execute(text(FUNNEL), {'patient': PATIENT}).mappings().one())
        surv = {r.pgs_id: r for r in c.execute(text(SURVIVORS), {'patient': PATIENT})}
        assert all(r.snps_used == r.scored for r in surv.values())
        traits = {p: rest_traits(p) for p in surv}
 
        def mondo(p):
            return [(int(i.split('_')[1]), l) for i, l in traits[p] if i.startswith('MONDO_')]
 
        nums = sorted({n for p in surv for n, _ in mondo(p)})
        by_n = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for a in c.execute(text(ANCHORS), {'nums': nums, 'cid': COMPOSITION,
                                           'dp': list(DRUG_PREDICATES)}).mappings():
            by_n[a['n']].append(dict(a))
 
    def resolve(n):
        """The v0 anchor rule for one MONDO number -> (route, node or None)."""
        inc = [a for a in by_n.get(n, []) if a['in_comp']]
        std = [a for a in inc if a['kind'] != 'grouped']
        if not inc:
            return 'none', None
        if not std:
            return 'grouped', None
        pk = [a for a in std if 'prime_kg' in (a['sources'] or '').split(',')]
        if len(pk) > 1:
            return 'ambiguous', None
        if pk:  # the node that carries PrimeKG's edges (J1: twins resolve here)
            node = pk[0]
            return ('exact' if node['kind'] == 'unpadded' else 'padded (PrimeKG node merged)'), node
        if len(std) > 1:
            return 'ambiguous', None
        return 'padded (no PrimeKG node)', std[0]
 
    def anchor_nodes(n):
        """Node ids a MONDO number anchors to: its resolved node, or its grouped node(s)."""
        route, node = resolve(n)
        if node is not None:
            return {node['id']}
        if route == 'grouped':
            return {a['id'] for a in by_n[n] if a['in_comp'] and a['kind'] == 'grouped'}
        return set()
 
    S = sorted(surv)
    # R8 as #296 counted it: a MONDO trait with any in-composition node, grouped included
    r8 = [p for p in S if any(anchor_nodes(n) for n, _ in mondo(p))]
    r8_nodes = set().union(*(anchor_nodes(n) for p in r8 for n, _ in mondo(p)))
    # D7: one trait only (any ontology), then no grouped anchor
    single = [p for p in r8 if len(traits[p]) == 1]
    single_nodes = set().union(*(anchor_nodes(n) for p in single for n, _ in mondo(p)))
    v0 = [p for p in single if resolve(mondo(p)[0][0])[1] is not None]
    by_anchor = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for p in v0:
        by_anchor[resolve(mondo(p)[0][0])[1]['curie']].append(p)
    rows = []
    for curie, ps in sorted(by_anchor.items()):
        n, label = mondo(ps[0])[0]
        route, node = resolve(n)
        ranked = sorted(ps, key=lambda p: (-surv[p].scored, int(p[3:])))   # most loci, then lowest accession
        others = [a for a in by_n[n] if a['in_comp'] and a['id'] != node['id']]
        rows.append({'label': label, 'mondo': 'MONDO_%07d' % n, 'anchor': curie, 'route': route,
                     'anchor_name': node['name'], 'sources': node['sources'],
                     'also_in_vocab': [(a['kind'], a['curie'][:40], a['name'], a['sources'],
                                        a['n_rel_ends'], a['n_drug_any']) for a in others],
                     'n_v0': len(ps), 'chosen': ranked[0], 'scored_loci': surv[ranked[0]].scored,
                     'runner_up': [ranked[1], surv[ranked[1]].scored] if len(ranked) > 1 else None,
                     'tied_at_top': [q for q in ranked if surv[q].scored == surv[ranked[0]].scored],
                     'rel_ends': node['n_rel_ends'], 'drug_any': node['n_drug_any'],
                     't': node['t'], 'c': node['c'], 'o': node['o'],
                     'n_header_not_rest': sum(1 for q in ps if (surv[q].header_trait or '')
                                              != ','.join(i for i, _ in traits[q])),
                     'v0_pgs_ids': sorted(ps)})
    no_mondo = collections.Counter('+'.join(sorted({i.split('_')[0] for i, _ in traits[p]}))
                                   for p in S if not mondo(p))
    grouped_out = []
    for p in single:
        n, label = mondo(p)[0]
        if resolve(n)[0] == 'grouped':
            g = [a for a in by_n[n] if a['in_comp'] and a['kind'] == 'grouped'][0]
            grouped_out.append([p, 'MONDO_%07d' % n, label, g['name'],
                                len(g['curie'].split(':', 1)[1].split('_')), g['n_drug_any']])
    out = {'live_rows': live,   # [run_id, gate_a.n_records, count] of the rows the funnel reads
           'funnel': funnel,
           'r8': [len(r8), len(r8_nodes)],
           'r8_removed_no_mondo': dict(no_mondo),
           'r8_removed_unanchored': [[p, ['MONDO_%07d' % n for n, _ in mondo(p)]]
                                     for p in S if mondo(p) and p not in r8],
           'd7_single_trait': [len(single), len(single_nodes)],
           'd7_multi_trait_removed': [[p, ['%s %s' % (i, l) for i, l in traits[p]]]
                                      for p in r8 if len(traits[p]) > 1],
           # J9: what the loose reading (drop only 2+ MONDO traits) would add back
           'd7_multi_loose_would_add': [[p, resolve(mondo(p)[0][0])[1]['curie'], surv[p].scored]
                                        for p in r8 if len(traits[p]) > 1 and len(mondo(p)) == 1
                                        and resolve(mondo(p)[0][0])[1] is not None],
           'd7_no_grouped': [len(v0), len(rows)],
           'd7_grouped_removed': grouped_out,
           'rows': rows}
    json.dump(out, sys.stdout)
 
 
main()

"""The CRC index anchor and the basal cell carcinoma gap, read-only.
 
    docker exec -i maple-worker-1 python - < smoke_v0_anchor_checks.py
"""
import os
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
 
eng = create_engine(os.environ['DATABASE_URL'])
Q = lambda c, sql, **kw: c.execute(text(sql), kw).fetchall()
with eng.connect() as c:
    c.execute(text('SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY'))
    print('composition:', Q(c, """SELECT id, version, is_locked, updated_at FROM mods_kg_composition
                                  WHERE id = 'maureen_focus_v1'"""))
    print('members:', Q(c, """SELECT source_id, exclude_domains FROM mods_kg_composition_member
                              WHERE composition_id = 'maureen_focus_v1' ORDER BY 1"""))
    for curie in ('MONDO:0005575', 'MONDO:5575', 'MONDO:24331', 'MONDO:0024331',
                  'MONDO:0020804', 'MONDO:20804', 'MONDO:0005341'):
        ent = Q(c, "SELECT id, name, domain FROM mods_kg_entity WHERE curie = :cu", cu=curie)
        if not ent:
            print(curie, '-> no entity')
            continue
        eid = ent[0][0]
        src = Q(c, """SELECT source_id, external_id FROM mods_kg_entity_source
                      WHERE entity_id = :i ORDER BY 1""", i=eid)
        drug = Q(c, """SELECT r.source_id, r.predicate,
                              CASE WHEN r.subject_id = :i THEN 'out' ELSE 'in' END, count(*)
                       FROM mods_kg_relation r
                       WHERE (r.subject_id = :i OR r.object_id = :i)
                         AND r.predicate IN ('biolink:treats', 'biolink:contraindicated_for',
                                             'biolink:has_off_label_use')
                       GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1, 2, 3""", i=eid)
        print(curie, tuple(ent[0]), '| sources:', src, '| drug relations:', drug)
    print('CRC drug partners:', Q(c, """
        SELECT DISTINCT r.predicate, d.curie, d.name
        FROM mods_kg_relation r
        JOIN mods_kg_entity e ON e.curie = 'MONDO:0005575'
        JOIN mods_kg_entity d ON d.id = CASE WHEN r.subject_id = e.id THEN r.object_id ELSE r.subject_id END
        WHERE (r.subject_id = e.id OR r.object_id = e.id)
          AND r.predicate IN ('biolink:treats', 'biolink:contraindicated_for', 'biolink:has_off_label_use')
        ORDER BY 1, 2"""))
    print('BCC 0005341 <-> 0020804:', Q(c, """
        SELECT s.curie, r.predicate, o.curie, r.source_id
        FROM mods_kg_relation r
        JOIN mods_kg_entity s ON s.id = r.subject_id JOIN mods_kg_entity o ON o.id = r.object_id
        WHERE s.curie IN ('MONDO:0005341', 'MONDO:0020804') AND o.curie IN ('MONDO:0005341', 'MONDO:0020804')"""))
    print('grouped nodes containing 20804:', Q(c, r"""
        SELECT id, curie FROM mods_kg_entity
        WHERE curie LIKE 'MONDO\_grouped:%'
          AND '20804' = ANY (string_to_array(split_part(curie, ':', 2), '_'))"""))
    drugsets = {}
    for cu in ('MONDO:1187', 'MONDO:4986'):   # urinary bladder cancer / carcinoma
        drugsets[cu] = {r[0] for r in Q(c, """
            SELECT DISTINCT d.curie FROM mods_kg_entity e
            JOIN mods_kg_relation r ON (r.subject_id = e.id OR r.object_id = e.id)
            JOIN mods_kg_entity d ON d.id = CASE WHEN r.subject_id = e.id THEN r.object_id ELSE r.subject_id END
            WHERE e.curie = :cu AND d.domain = 'drug' AND r.source_id = 'prime_kg'""", cu=cu)}
    print('bladder cancer vs carcinoma drug sets:', {k: len(s) for k, s in drugsets.items()},
          'identical:', drugsets['MONDO:1187'] == drugsets['MONDO:4986'])
    print("trap: prime_kg external_id '20804' is:", Q(c, """
        SELECT e.curie, e.name FROM mods_kg_entity_source es JOIN mods_kg_entity e ON e.id = es.entity_id
        WHERE es.source_id = 'prime_kg' AND es.external_id = '20804'"""))

"""Host-side checks on the reproduction's output (v0_repro.json), read-only.

   colorectal nodes carry there.
2. The REST records behind judgement calls J3-J8, and the REST cache dates.
 
    python smoke_v0_host_checks.py v0_repro.json
"""
import datetime, json, os, sys, collections
 
EXPORT = r'C:\Maple\runs\2026-05-18_maureen_focus_v1\data'
CACHE = r'C:\Maple\worker\data\pgs_catalog'
v0 = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))
rows = {r['anchor']: r for r in v0['rows']}
anchors = set(rows)
 
ends = collections.Counter()
preds = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
for split in ('train.txt', 'valid.txt', 'test.txt'):
    with open(os.path.join(EXPORT, split), encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        for line in fh:
            h, r, t = line.rstrip('\r\n').split('\t')
            for x in (h, t):

                        preds[x][r] += 1

      sorted(a for a in anchors if not ends[a]))
for x in ('MONDO:0005575', 'MONDO:24331'):
    print(x, 'appears', ends[x], 'times:', dict(preds[x]))
 
 
def meta(p):
    with open(os.path.join(CACHE, p, 'metadata.json'), encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        d = json.load(fh)
    pub = d.get('publication') or {}
    return {'name': d.get('name'), 'trait_reported': d.get('trait_reported'),
            'method': d.get('method_name'), 'params': d.get('method_params'),
            'pub': f"{pub.get('firstauthor')} {pub.get('date_publication')}: {pub.get('title')}",
            'ancestry': d.get('ancestry_distribution')}
 
 
for anchor in ('MONDO:0005575', 'MONDO:5350', 'MONDO:5009', 'MONDO:5068', 'MONDO:5300', 'MONDO:5279'):
    r = rows[anchor]
    print(f"\n== {r['label']} ({anchor}), {r['n_v0']} v0 scores; chosen {r['chosen']}; tied at top: {r['tied_at_top']}")
    extra = [r['runner_up'][0]] if r['runner_up'] and r['runner_up'][0] not in r['tied_at_top'] else []
    for p in r['tied_at_top'] + extra:
        print('  ', p, json.dumps(meta(p)))
 
print('\n== colorectal carcinoma (MONDO:24331): trait_reported of its v0 scores')
print(collections.Counter(meta(p)['trait_reported'] for p in rows['MONDO:24331']['v0_pgs_ids']))
 
print('\n== chosen scores whose REST GWAS ancestry is under 50% EUR, or not recorded as EUR at all')
for r in v0['rows']:
    g = ((meta(r['chosen'])['ancestry'] or {}).get('gwas') or {}).get('dist') or {}
    if g and float(g.get('EUR', 0)) < 50:
        print('  ', r['label'], r['chosen'], g, 'n_v0 =', r['n_v0'])
 
stamps = [os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(CACHE, p, 'metadata.json'))
          for r in v0['rows'] for p in r['v0_pgs_ids']]
day = lambda t: datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(t).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
print('\nREST metadata.json cached', day(min(stamps)), 'to', day(max(stamps)), 'for', len(stamps), 'v0 scores')

KGIA fine-tuning input file (GET /api/mods/research/patient-profile). One row
per section. Check the [ ] once we’ve QC’d that section’s data and confirmed
the records, the query shape, and any cleanup are good.
The “final file” = whatever the API returns when you toggle on the sections you
want. Toggling a section off in the UI also drops its entities from PrimeKG
coverage, so this is the same gate KGIA will see.

How sections were chosen for v1
Three filters, in order:

MEMORY notes about Maureen’s record. The “Genomic report parsing COMPLETE (2026-03-18)” memory enumerates the tables MODS parsers populated (alterations, gene expression, therapy associations, resistance factors, CTC profiles, drug sensitivities). Picked exactly those, plus their dependencies.
Existing snapshot service coverage. ModsSnapshotService already builds patient + cancer + biomarkers + treatments + RGCC. Kept those, added the post-snapshot tables.
KGIA’s input shape. --use_ploss consumes a PRS scalar + biomarker scalars + a patient-local KG. Anything that gives us biomarker scalars or KG-mappable entities (genes, drugs, diseases) earns a section.

What can contribute to the final file
Strictly: anything we choose to feed in. The KGIA loss is λ₁·PRS + λ₂·biomarker, so the floor is just PRS + biomarker scalars. Everything else expands the patient-local PrimeKG subgraph that surrounds the fine-tuning. The toggles let us experiment with which substrate gives the best ranking for Maureen.
Workflow

Pick a section. Read its current row count + notes above.
Inspect the data: hit the API with ?include=<key> and look at the JSON, or open the Patient Profile tab and toggle just that one on.
Note any cleanup needed under “QC notes” (add bullets).
When the data is good, check the section box at the top.
When all sections are checked, the v1 substrate is QC’d and we can move to PRS computation + biomarker vector serialization (next iteration).


GH #108 status (2026-05-29) — fixed feature schema landed
The open QC items about which gene / biomarker subset feeds KGIA and stable
PRS + biomarker vectors are answered by the committed, versioned cross-patient
feature schema (backend/mods_kgia_schema_service.py, table pdr2_feature_schema,
descriptor backend/pdr2_schemas/kgia_schema_v1.json):

expr_values is fed by mods_gene_expression (Caris WTS / RGCC gene
expression), not the noisy biomarker_series section — so the vital-sign /
imaging noise flagged for biomarker_series does not reach the model input.
Gene axis = union of assay-observed genes ∩ canonical KG, ordered by symbol.
prs_values = supported PRS traits (default_disease_pgs_set()) ∩ KG,
fixed across patients, ordered by CUI.
Every patient projects onto the SAME axis; a schema_hash +
validate_against_schema guard train==infer.
New endpoint GET /api/mods/research/patient-profile/kgia-tensors returns the
serialized vectors + hash + measured mask.

Still open (tracked, not blocking): biomarker categorization (#107) for the
biomarker_series display section; cross-assay unit normalization (Olink NPX
↔ Caris percentile) once a non-Caris patient lands.

GH #114 — QC’ing the personalized ranking
Once a --use_ploss fine-tune exists (POST .../runs/{id}/submit_finetune),
POST .../kgia/finetune/{run_id}/rank scores every candidate drug as a tail of
(patient, MAPLE:sensitive_to_drug, ?) under that checkpoint. The ranked top-K
lands on the run as a kgia_personalized_ranking validation row, read at
GET .../kgia/finetune/{run_id}/ranking and rendered in the Research dashboard’s
KGIA Ranking tab. Code: backend/mods_kgia_finetune_service.py.
[ ] QC the ranking, not just the profile

 Which track was it? With no released PRS the fine-tune ran Track A
(prs_values all zeros, so the disease weights got no gradient). Never
describe a Track A ranking as PRS-personalized.
 Anchor recovery. The payload’s anchors block gives the rank of drugs
from her own record — her mods_treatment_episode drugs and her
high_sensitivity RGCC agents. Deliberately not a clinical expectation
list: an anchor has to trace to a row in her record, not to what is typical for
her cancer type. A ranking that buries all of them is a finding about the
ranking.
 Read the held-out ranking. A candidate she already has a
MAPLE:sensitive_to_drug edge to was in the foundation’s training data, so its
rank is recall, not prediction (GH #214). Rows carry seen_in_training and a
held_out_rank; the UI defaults to held-out-only.
 Check counts.skipped — candidates the scorer could not resolve into
the dataset vocab, usually drugs this composition excluded. A large fraction
means the candidate set and the trained graph have drifted.
 Sanity-check the spread. All candidates share one (head, relation)
pair and one forward pass, so a near-constant score column means the model is
not discriminating — not that every drug is promising.

Per MODS_MISSION_SPEC §1.4 a high score means the graph’s geometry is consistent
with the drug being relevant; it is not evidence the drug works or is safe
alongside her regimen.
Still open for #114: a one-click launch (stage the patient bundle to GCS and
submit the fine-tune in one call) — today the pickle is built with
scripts/build_pdr2_input_pickle.py and uploaded by hand.

results/mods_smoke_run_1_playbook.title: Smoke run #1 — playbook
results/mods_smoke_run_1_playbook.content:
Smoke run #1 — real PRS → clean foundation → personalized drug ranking
Tracking issue: #439. Label: critical-path (every issue that blocks this run carries it, together with p0). Written: 2026-09-27 with Claude Opus 5.5, from a code, DB and artifact audit of work built mostly on Opus 5. Every number below was measured that day; re-verify any of them before you rely on it.

Outcome (2026-09-29). The run finished on 2026-09-29. All ten machinery checks (§6) were measured and pass; two of them, M6 and M9, were borderline, and Richard accepted both. Gate F released 590 scores over 109 diseases as smoke_v0. With her RGCC drugs held out of training, the base ranker shows no RGCC signal (graded-only ρ +0.03 and +0.05 per draw, intervals spanning zero), and the released criterion does not help. The rest of this page is the plan as written on 2026-09-27, with dated updates. Results: the run’s writeup and The smoke run lands.


The one-line version. We have never pushed Maureen’s real data through the whole machine. We have also never done it without her validation labels leaking into the training graph. This run does it once, deliberately, and checks every joint. Proving that personalization helps is not the goal. Proving that the machinery does what we think it does is.


0. What this run is, and what it is not
It is a machinery test on real inputs. The chain is:

PRS released and normalized onto a disease axis, plus her expression values.
A PDR2 patient pickle built from them.
A criterion fine-tune on a foundation trained without her drug-response labels.
Raw and personalized drug scores, stored side by side.
Per-draw RGCC metrics.

It passes when every check in §6 passes.
It is not a test of whether personalization works. The released PDR2 criterion is degenerate, its sign is fixed, and it is blind to edge types (§1.4). A null or negative lift is the expected result. Report it; it is not a failure of this run. The science run is run #2 (§9).
It is pre-registered. Record the decisions in §3 as ticked boxes in #439 before any drug is scored. Look at no metric until the whole grid in §5.4 is computed.

1.1 The foundation memorized the validation labels

Four of the five Tier-2 positives were memorized.

Oxaliplatin, cisplatin and mitomycin carried sensitive_to_drug in train.
Pemetrexed’s CHEBI edge was in test, but its PharmGKB twin, pharmgkb_variants:pharmgkb_drug:pemetrexed, was in train.
Carboplatin was the only held-out positive. That is why it sat at rank 260, the “outlier” MODS_MISSION_SPEC §5.3 blamed for suppressing Tier-1.

The PDR2 v2 RGCC signal was memorization. On the clean subset, graded-only, ρ is +0.22 / +0.28 (n=26), which is not significant.
Other drug-related leaks:

Medication history is circular for the response-episode surface. All 14 labelled response episodes are for drugs she has a tried_drug edge to, and 7 of those 8 drugs have a patient→drug edge in train.
The same drug can appear under two CURIEs. 22 held-out RGCC edges had the same agent in train under a sibling CURIE (oxaliplatin as CHEBI and as PharmGKB). A holdout must group by drug identity, not by CURIE.
The overlay erases the draw inversion. RGCC edges carry no draw date, and writes use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. All 12 drugs that moved 25 points or more between draws land in partially_sensitive.

1.2 The graph has a symmetry leak
PrimeKG stores most edges in both directions under one predicate, and the export splits per directed triple. 539,594 of the 890,384 test triples (60.6%) have their exact reverse in train (Appendix A.3). Training does not remove the mirror (remove_one_hop defaults to False), so the foundation learns a lookup, and every PrimeKG foundation MRR (0.56–0.59) is inflated by it. This is the FB15k / WN18 inverse-leakage pattern. The split is also not reproducible. Set order depends on an unset PYTHONHASHSEED, and the audit found two same-seed runs sharing only ~21% of their test sets. On top of that, every downstream handler re-exports and re-splits, and re-adds the full patient overlay while doing it (#433).
1.3 Real PRS cannot reach the model yet
resolve_prs_vector keeps only score rows with a disease_cui. Every row has none, so a released, normalized fleet still exports an empty PRS vector and the run silently becomes Track A (#430). The raw material for a disease axis is better than expected:

1,620 of the 3,753 eligible scores carry a MONDO trait, covering 245 diseases, and all 245 anchor in the maureen_focus_v1 slice. (Corrected 2026-09-28: not all. Basal cell carcinoma, MONDO_0020804, has no node in the composition under either spelling; smoke_v0 disease mapping, J10.)
173 of those diseases have more than one eligible score.
PrimeKG writes MONDO unpadded (MONDO:5148) while CIViC, ClinVar, OncoKB and RTX-KG2 write it padded. 14,504 unpadded disease entities have a padded twin.
In today’s export, the colorectal node that carries drug edges is MONDO:0005575 “Colorectal Cancer”: 10 treats, 2 contraindicated_for, 2 has_off_label_use (export lines, with each drug–disease pair written in both directions: 5 / 1 / 1 distinct drugs; smoke_v0 disease mapping §5, 2026-09-28). PrimeKG’s MONDO:24331 carries only gene associations.

1.4 The criterion, as released
The released loss (losses.py, paper_code) is base + λ₁·tanh(ŵ·prs) + λ₂·tanh(v̂·expr), where ŵ and v̂ are L2-normalized. Neither term sees the batch, and the forward pass runs under no_grad, so:

The weights are closed-form. The optimum is ŵ = −PRS/‖PRS‖ and v̂ = −expr/‖expr‖. The fine-tune reads the input vector back out; it learns nothing from the graph.
The sign is fixed. Every disease term w_d·p_d ≤ 0 and grows with p_d². Drugs adjacent to her most extreme-risk diseases, high or low, get pushed down.
Expression never trained. It arrives as Caris TPM percentiles (4–100), unscaled, so tanh saturates from step 0. All 5 past fine-tunes ended with protein weights at their random-init scale. The “top protein weights” in earlier writeups are initialization.
Eval and training disagree about scale. Eval multiplies raw weights where training normalizes them, and it counts each adjacency 2–4 times depending on mirror and inverse structure.
The adjustment is edge-blind. An indication edge and a contraindication edge push the same way. That is Phase 12 (#420).

This run fixes the inputs and the eval/train mismatch (#435). It deliberately keeps the released loss, and measures the degeneracy (check M6 in §6). Phase 12 is the science fix.
1.5 Silent-failure modes still in the code

A failed checkpoint load continues on a random model (lib/pdr2/code/script/model.py, #434). A smoke run could “pass” on a random foundation. Fixed 2026-09-27 (#434): a failed load now raises.
Bare debug_log calls in the PDR handlers raise NameError. One of them sits between the Vertex submit and saving the job id, so a retry can double-submit an A100 job (#398). Fixed 2026-09-27 (#398).
Rebuilding the schema without --version overwrites v1 in place. Fixed 2026-09-28 (#497): --version is required, and an existing version is refused without --overwrite.
Releasing is one-way today. store_score_result never supersedes a released row, so a later re-score leaves old released values being served (#296’s writer needs a demotion path). Fixed 2026-09-28 (#296): the v0 release writer can demote a release (release_gate_f.py --demote).
The worker reloader used to hard-kill in-flight tasks on any .py change under C:\Maple, a git pull included (#361). It now drains instead: on a change to a module the worker imported (tests are ignored) it finishes the current task, then restarts. A task still running after WORKER_RELOAD_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 6 h; 0 = no deadline) is still killed. It has been off by default since 2026-09-28 (WORKER_AUTO_RELOAD=0). Don’t turn it back on during a pass.

1.6 What is in good shape

Gate A, B and C are sound and verified: every E2 score reconciles, and none sits outside its theoretical bounds.
D1, D2 and D3 exist with fixture tests.
The HGDP+1kGP panel is staged and md5-verified.
The export reads normalized PRS and refuses raw sums (#297).
The worker → Vertex path exists for every mode.
The foundation retrain costs ~21 A100-hours, roughly $120.

Reasoning paths for the top 10 (added 2026-09-29, Richard). For each of the ten, record the graph paths that drove its raw score. This is the evidence a reviewer would have to accept before taking the drug seriously. It is also the direct test of whether the ranking does more than recall known CRC drugs.


Method.

Use BaseNBFNet.visualize() in our fork (lib/pdr2/code/ultra/base_nbfnet.py). It takes the gradient of the score with respect to every edge, then beam-searches the highest-weighted paths (NBFNet’s interpretation method; defaults num_beam=10, path_topk=10).
Nothing calls it today. EntityNBFNet only gets its query and each layer’s relation inside Ultra.forward, so a thin wrapper must set both from the relation model first, exactly as forward does.
Running it needs a container mode, e.g. MODE=explain_paths. That is one more change to batch into the Lane R rebuild (§10). Submit it through the worker queue (M10).



Explain the exact score.

Use the same checkpoint, the same fact graph and the same query as score_edges.
visualize() skips negative_sample_to_tail, so pass the triple already turned: (CRC anchor, inverse of biolink:treats, drug).
Positive control: the score computed inside visualize() must equal the drug’s raw_score to float tolerance. If it doesn’t, the paths explain some other number: stop and fix the query.



Record per drug the top 5 paths with their weights, each hop as name, CURIE and predicate. Classify each drug’s strongest path:

direct: the drug’s own edge to CRC (expected for a known indication);
mechanistic: drug → target → gene or pathway → CRC;
analogy: drug → shared target or class → another drug → CRC;
personal: through her own node, via her expression, variant or phenotype edges (legitimate, since D2 keeps them);
hub: through a generic, very high-degree node.

Report the count in each class. If every drug’s support is direct or analogy, the ranking is recalling known CRC drugs. Mechanistic paths are what repurposing needs.


Limits.

The paths explain the raw score only. The personalization adjustment is added after message passing and has no path; the “diseases whose PRS moved it” note covers it.
The foundation is frozen, so the paths are the same at every λ. Compute them once.
Gradient paths show what drove the score, not whether the biology holds.
No path may use one of the six predicates D2 excludes. One that does means M4 missed a leak.

wrong drug merges; MONDO twins; PharmGKB synthetic drugsThe canonical graphKnown limitation (D3); #438 before run #2

8. What we will be able to say afterwards, and what we won’t
If M1–M10 pass, we can say:

The machinery runs end to end on real inputs with no drug-response leakage, and every artifact is traceable.
Her PRS reached the model at the right positions.
The honest base-ranker Tier-1 and Tier-2 numbers per draw. These are the first clean RGCC numbers the project has had.
How much the released criterion moves the ranking, in which direction, and through which edge types.
For each of the top 10, which graph evidence drove its raw score, and how much of the list rests on recall (direct or analogy paths) rather than mechanistic evidence.

We will not be able to say:

That personalization helps. The criterion is degenerate and edge-blind; that question belongs to run #2.
Anything clinical. Single patient; RGCC is in vitro, fixed-concentration CTC data; five Tier-2 positives.
That a path’s biology is true. The paths show what drove a score, so they are hypotheses to review, not findings.
Anything about patient-node queries (Mechanism A). This run does not use them.


9. After the smoke run (run #2 and the rest)

Phase 12 (#420): a signed per-relation adjustment, plus a fine-tune whose signal depends on outcomes. Its parameterization, decision (ii), is Richard’s.
Final PRS policy:

#422: the palindrome forward set, strand-flip set and EAF gate, with the knob plumbing its comment describes; land #428 first;
#429: ancestry PCs;
the pgsc_calc witness;
then a release v1 that retires smoke_v0 through the demotion path. This is what “release most of the scores” needs.


Graph (#438): decide on the drug–protein roles, the bad drug merges, the MONDO twins and the PharmGKB drugs. Then re-export and retrain.
Mechanism A: drug-grouped K-fold in context. Fold k is scored with the other folds’ RGCC edges, one draw at a time, added to the fact graph. No retrain per fold is needed, since ULTRA has no per-relation parameters. This needs the overlay to carry draw dates.
Restate the old numbers (#324), for memorization as well as pooling.
The larger inputs: the WTS gene axis (#212) and population supervision (#327).


10. Parallelization analysis

Surfaces touched.

Backend: yes (#430, #431, #437, #296 writer, #244).
Frontend: no.
Worker handlers: yes (#433, #398).
Migrations: none expected; release_v0 and the axis live in existing columns and JSONB, so confirm before adding any.
MCP tools: no. The mods_pdr_export tool ignores the schema, so don’t use it for this run.
DB-stored config: yes, the pdr2_feature_schema v2 row.
Docs: yes (this file, the results writeup).
Tests: yes, in every code issue.
Container: yes, one rebuild after #434, #435 and #436, including the path-explanation mode for §5.4 step 4.


Parallel split.

Lane P code (#431) and runs (#339 → E3 ‖ D1 → D2 → D3) run independently of Lane G code (#432, #433, #434) and Lane R code (#435, #436, #437).
#430 and #244 need the mapping decision first.
Sequential joins: #296’s release waits on D3 and #430; the pickle waits on the release and axis v2; the fine-tunes wait on the pickle, the foundation and the rebuilt image.


Collision hotspots.

worker/task_handlers.py is shared by #398, #433 and #422’s plumbing: sequence them.
lib/pdr2/code/script/* is shared by #434, #435, #436 and the path-explanation mode: batch them into one rebuild.
requirements.txt (#339) is already done.
No migrations.py, component_registry.py, Terminal.jsx or main.py changes are expected.


Verify-how per surface.

Backend and PRS: pytest via scripts/run_backend_tests.ps1. The :5434 DB is broken (#421), so use CI or the agent DB.
Worker: a dry-run submission with a mismatched manifest refuses.
Container: a synthetic-pickle machinery test (M6, M7).
DB: the lifecycle counts (M1).
End to end: M1–M10.




Appendix A — Audit queries (reproduce §1)
A.1 Patient edges by split in the foundation’s training files.
cd /c/Maple/runs/2026-05-18_maureen_focus_v1/data
for f in train valid test; do echo "== $f"; grep "MAPLE_PATIENT:maureen" $f.txt | cut -f2 | sort | uniq -c; done
A.2 Per-draw Tier-1 of the v2 scores, split by whether the drug’s label was ever in train. Inputs: runs/2026-05-20_rgcc_tier1_v2/metrics.matched.csv (the sensitive_to_drug rows), edges.csv (agent → CURIEs), train.txt, and the labels:
SELECT coalesce(p.collected_date, p.reported_date) AS draw, a.agent_name, a.score_raw
FROM mods_functional_test_agent_result a

WHERE p.patient_id = 'PATIENT_UUID'
  AND p.test_name ILIKE '%onconomics%' AND a.score_raw IS NOT NULL;
A drug is “clean” when none of its CURIEs is the object of a MAPLE_PATIENT:maureen… MAPLE:*_to_drug line in train.txt. Spearman is computed per draw, never pooled.
A.3 Mirror leak.

A.5 MONDO padding twins.

results/mods_smoke_run_1_writeup.title: Smoke run #1 — machinery validation
results/mods_smoke_run_1_writeup.content:
Smoke run #1 — Formal Writeup
Authors: whafa, Claude (Maple project)
Dates: 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-29
Tracking: #439: status, provenance log, decisions
Playbook: mods_smoke_run_1_playbook.md · PM charter: mods_smoke_run_1_pm_charter.md

Machinery validation, not a recommendation. Nothing here is clinical advice. The run tests
whether the pipeline’s parts connect and measure what they claim to. It was never meant to show
that personalization helps.


Summary

The pipeline runs end to end for the first time with her real, released PRS. Here is the chain, with each stage’s first real output:

PRS: E3 → D1 → D2 → D3 → Gate F v0, releasing 590 scores over 109 diseases.
Patient inputs: KGIA axis v2, then the Track B and Track A pickles.
Model: a leak-free foundation, five fine-tunes, and a personalized CRC-anchor ranking.
Evaluation: the per-draw RGCC grid.


All ten machinery checks were measured, and all ten pass.

Eight pass outright.
Two were borderline, and Richard accepted both on 2026-09-29. M6: disease sign agreement 0.881 against a 0.90 bar. M9: scores reproduce to float precision, not bit for bit.


The clean holdout shows no RGCC signal. With her RGCC drugs removed from training, every drug is unseen. The base ranker’s graded-only Spearman ρ is +0.03 and +0.05 per draw, with CIs spanning 0, and its AUROC is about 0.61 on 5 positives. That agrees with the 2026-09-27 audit’s reading that the old PDR2 v2 “signal” was memorization.
The released personalization does not help. It is null at λ 0.01. At λ 0.1 it is slightly and borderline-measurably harmful (all-panel Δρ −0.057, CI [−0.121, −0.004]), and at λ 1.0 it trends harmful with CIs spanning 0. The expression-only control is null.
The criterion’s degeneracy is now measured on her data:

its weights stall within the first epoch;
λ has no effect on the learned weights;
the adjustment can only push a drug down;
73 % of it flows through contraindicated_for edges.


The foundation generalizes weakly. Its filtered MRR is 0.021 on held-out triples, well below published ULTRA-class numbers, even though it fits its training edges almost perfectly. (2026-10-05: it also loses to a non-learned baseline, found on 2026-10-01 (#523). Ranking by how often a node ends an edge of each relation in training scores 0.031, and a drug’s edge count alone reaches a graded RGCC ρ of +0.37 against the model’s +0.03; the model’s scores correlate 0.86 with that count. Suspected cause: the mirror of each query edge stays in the training graph.)

1. Purpose
Decided 2026-09-27: catalogue and retire the issues blocking a first end-to-end MODS run with real PRS. The run is a machinery smoke test. Its acceptance criteria (M1–M10, playbook §6) ask whether each stage produces what it claims, not whether the output is clinically useful. Against the mission’s goals:

G4 (traceability): tested directly, through M9 and the #439 provenance log.
G2 (the ranking recovers her measured sensitivities on a clean holdout): measured for the first time, on a leak-free foundation.
G3 (personalization improves on the raw ranking): measured with the released PDR2 criterion, which the project already suspected to be degenerate (#47, #420).

2. Materials and Methods
2.1 Patient inputs

























InputWhat was usedPRSGate F v0 release smoke_v0 (rules gate_f_v0_rules_v1, release run c3be9df0): 590 released scores over 109 MONDO anchors, one axis pick each. Placed as EUR z-scores (667 unrelated EUR panel samples, panel-aligned). D2 ran under the #499 fix (gate_d2_panel_scorer_v2), so her no-called loci are dropped from the panel too.Expression84 genes (v1’s gene axis, decision D8) from her most recent colorectal Caris WTS specimen, as probit z-scores of TPM percentiles (#435).AxisKGIA v2: 109 diseases × 84 genes, hash b95dcaff004ccf89, registered inactive (v1 untouched). The CRC anchor MONDO:0005575 is at position 8.PicklesTrack B: 109/109 PRS positions measured, sha 2761f70d…. Track A: PRS all zero with the same expression, sha b6fa381c….
2.2 Graph and foundation

Graph: composition maureen_focus_v1 plus the maple_patient overlay. The six MAPLE:* drug predicates are excluded (the three RGCC sensitivity predicates and the three medication predicates, decision D2).
Split: mirror-grouped (#432): 4,549,173 triples, split 2,796,395 / 876,339 / 876,406. Split fingerprint 4518539f… was reproduced by a second export (M4). The mirror leak is 0.000, against 0.606 for the old foundation.
Model: ULTRA / NBFNet, 6 layers, hidden size 64, from scratch, seed 41504.
Training: 20 epochs of about 3,700 s each on one A100-80GB, image ccad24d-smoke1 (5597a993…).
Early stop: the post-training full-test eval was cancelled at 09:40 on 2026-09-29, because it could not finish inside the job timeout (#515). The run row therefore reads failed, as the timeout would have left it.

2.3 Fine-tunes (decision D9)

Configurations: Track B at λ ∈ {0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0} (λ1 = λ2), plus Track A at λ 0.01.
Loss and image: the released paper_code loss, on image 9accf69-smoke1-ft (8261b505…).
Settings: batch 128 (FINE_TUNE_MAX_BATCH, #501); every child reused the foundation’s split (#433).
Early stopping: every run stopped after 12 epochs and restored epoch 6. The early stop keys on the epoch’s training loss, which the frozen foundation’s prediction term dominates.

2.4 Scoring (decisions D1, #436)

Query: the disease query (drug, biolink:treats, MONDO:0005575), over all 9,099 candidate drugs; 7,793 of them are in the drug target domain.
Adjustment: the edge-blind adjustment adds λ·ŵ·PRS over the drug’s disease anchors and λ·v̂·expr over its gene anchors. The anchors are its neighbours in the training graph, with direction and relation ignored.

2.5 Metrics

M5: full-ranking filtered MRR on 50,000 sampled test triples (#472).
M8: the per-draw RGCC grid (#437), for draws 2025-02-15 and 2025-09-19. The two draws are never pooled.

Panels: all-panel (n = 109 matched) and graded-only (n = 59).
Variants: raw and personalized; all drugs and drugs unseen in training.
Tier 1 is Spearman ρ against % cell death. Tier 2 is AUROC with RGCC’s 5 high_sensitivity agents per draw as positives against < 35 %.
Every cell carries its n and a bootstrap 95 % CI.



3. Procedure
The PM session ran the playbook between 2026-09-28 10:00 and 2026-09-29 11:40. The detours, each filed and fixed or recorded:


















































WhenWhat happenedIssue09-28 18:34D2’s first pass showed her no-calls deflating her score but not the panel’s. That biased her z by up to −5.5 SD on high mean/sd scores. Fixed, approved and re-run.#499 (PR #505)09-28 19:30Three freshly restarted workers broke on their first claim: a lazily imported model module raced debug_service’s writer thread.#507 (PR #509)09-28 18:45No worker handler set FINE_TUNE_MAX_BATCH, so every fine-tune would have run out of memory at batch 256.#501 (PR #503)09-28 21:55GitHub Actions used the private repo’s free monthly minutes. Richard set a budget; the CI trim is #516.#51609-29 08:28The local backend had stopped reloading at 11:58 the previous day, so it served 20-hour-old code.#51709-29 09:42The cancelled foundation had no kg_dataset_class, so all six children failed and were resubmitted. A cancel is also overwritten by a retry.#51509-29 10:22The rank endpoint parses the fine-tune’s patient_id label as a UUID and returns a 500.#51809-29 11:02The M5 eval sat 78 minutes queued on A100-40GB and was moved to A100-80GB.—
Every job went through the worker queue or the research API (M10). The only direct Vertex calls were two cancels, made through the app’s own provider.
4. Results
4.1 Machinery checks

















































CheckResultM1 PRS released✓ 590 released rows, all with z_score, a disease anchor and the smoke_v0 tag. The count equals the v0 funnel; 0 are outside their bounds. The four non-pick alternates were held back by the post-D3 panel-coverage rule.M2 Axis✓ v2 registered (hash b95dcaff004ccf89), v1 untouched, the CRC anchor on the axis.M3 Pickles✓ Track B measures 109 of 109 PRS positions; every value is finite; expression is probit z; the sidecars are present.M4 Export✓ 0 excluded-predicate lines; mirror leak 0.000; the manifest md5s reproduce.M5 Foundation✓ Loss 0.0573 → 0.00058 over 20 epochs. Every load logs its checkpoint sha. Filtered MRR 0.0209 (Hits@10 0.035), below the old leaky 0.56.M6 Fine-tune✓ disease cos(ŵ, −PRS) +0.649. ✗ disease sign agreement 0.881 < 0.90. ✓ protein cos +0.652, sign agreement 0.952. ✓ ŵ identical across λ > 0. ✓ Track A’s disease weights are bit-identical to the λ 0 control’s (weight decay only). ✓ split reuse on all five runs. Accepted by Richard, 2026-09-29.M7 Personalized scores✓ At λ 0, pers == raw on all 9,099 rows. ✓ The sampled adj matches an independent recomputation to 1.2e-7. ✓ Kendall τ 0.952 at λ 1.0. ✓ The relation breakdown is reported (§4.3).M8 Metrics✓ 20 rgcc_per_draw rows, n in every cell; every RGCC drug flagged unseen; test-retest printed on every run.M9 Provenance✓ The #439 provenance log links run ids, image digests, manifest md5s, the release tag, the schema hash and pickle shas. A re-run of one scoring job reproduces raw scores and ranks exactly, and adj to ≤ 1.9e-9 (float32 rounding). It is not bit-identical. Accepted by Richard as reproduced, 2026-09-29.M10 Venue✓ Every job went through the worker queue or the research API.
4.2 The foundation
The training loss fell to 0.00058, but the held-out filtered MRR is 0.0209: mean rank about 3,000 of about 103K entities, and Hits@1 is essentially zero. The model separates its training edges from sampled negatives almost perfectly, but ranks held-out edges only moderately. The old foundation’s 0.56 came from the mirror shortcut, which #432 removed. (2026-10-05: #432 removed the split-level shortcut. A training-time one, where each query edge’s mirror stays in the message-passing graph, is the suspected cause of #523.) Published ULTRA-class numbers on dense biomedical graphs are 0.13–0.4, so this foundation is weak for link prediction as well as for RGCC.
4.3 The released criterion’s behaviour


The weights stall almost immediately. Sign agreement is already 0.881 after the first epoch (100 steps), and between epochs 0 and 6 each weight moves by about 1e-4.

The tanh term saturates within about 50 steps, and AdamW’s second-moment memory then shrinks every step to almost nothing.
Against the λ 0 run, which shows the seed-42 starting point, every weight moved toward −sign(input): 109 of 109 disease weights and 84 of 84 gene weights. 38 disease signs flipped from wrong to right and none the other way.
The 13 still wrong are leftovers from the random start, spread across the |PRS| range.



λ does nothing at fine-tune time. The λ 0.01, 0.1 and 1.0 runs learned identical weights (cos 1.000000, max difference 2e-6), because Adam cancels the gradient’s λ scale. λ acts only as a scale on the adjustment at scoring, so the D9 fine-tune sweep was redundant.


The adjustment can only lower a score. With ŵ ≈ −PRS/‖PRS‖, each anchor term is about −z²/‖z‖, negative whatever the sign of her z. At λ 0.01, 1,254 of the 1,314 adjusted drugs go down.


It is edge-blind. Share of the adjustment’s absolute mass, by relation:

























relationsharedisease contraindicated_for72.7 %disease treats14.5 %disease has_off_label_use3.3 %gene has_target9.5 %
A drug contraindicated for one of her diseases is pushed the same way as a drug that treats it.


4.4 RGCC (M8)
Tier 1 is Spearman ρ; Tier 2 is AUROC on 5 positives. Each cell gives the 2025-02-15 draw, then the 2025-09-19 draw, as point [95 % CI].









































variantgraded ρall-panel ρall-panel AUROCraw+0.029 [−0.24, +0.32] / +0.046 [−0.23, +0.32]−0.193 [−0.37, −0.02] / −0.187 [−0.37, −0.00]0.525 / 0.521pers λ 0.01Δ −0.002 / −0.003Δ −0.010 / −0.009Δ −0.006 / −0.007pers λ 0.1Δ −0.063 / −0.056Δ −0.057 [−0.121, −0.004] / −0.054 [−0.117, +0.001]Δ −0.054 / −0.058pers λ 1.0Δ −0.110 [−0.41, +0.16] / −0.15Δ −0.034 / −0.047Δ −0.082 / −0.083Track A λ 0.01Δ +0.001Δ +0.000Δ +0.002
The all-panel ρ below zero is driven by the 53 MoAb/SMW agents that RGCC grades only as sensitive or not, all tied at 0. The graded-only panel is the one to read. The test-retest ceiling is ρ 0.9616 all-panel and 0.7635 graded.
4.5 The top 30
The annotated top 30, raw and at λ 1.0, is on #114.

Ranks 1–2 are the only two drugs whose treats-CRC edge is in the training split: tipiracil and trifluridine, at raw scores near +7.8.
Most of ranks 3–25 are CIViC / OncoKB therapy and regimen entities outside the drug domain. They include her own cetuximab/encorafenib regimen, FOLFOX, an anti-EGFR antibody and RAF inhibitors. The model recovers her actual treatment lines through evidence edges, but the personalization cannot reach them.
Cetuximab’s treats-CRC edge is held out, and it ranks 26 of 9,099.
At λ 1.0, personalization only removes drugs from the top 30: erlotinib and crizotinib.

5. Discussion
What the run shows. The machinery works and is traceable: every stage produced its artifact, and every artifact carries its provenance. The science is an honest null.

The base ranker has no signal on her RGCC sensitivities once the leak is closed.
The released criterion cannot help, for four reasons:

it stalls near its start;
it ignores λ;
it can only demote;
it cannot tell treats from contraindicated_for.



These are the defects #420 (a signed per-relation criterion) was designed around. This run quantifies them on her own data.
Limitations:

8 of the RGCC agents have no in-domain node, so the adjustment cannot reach them (#470).
One axis pick (PGS005253) carries a predicted +0.67 SD residual from the panel’s own missing calls (#513).
The fine-tune’s early stop keys on a training loss the criterion weights cannot move.
Tier 2 rests on 5 positives per draw.
The v0 release waived the pgsc_calc witness and the NR-scale policy.
The foundation’s held-out MRR is low.

What to do next, in the order the evidence suggests:

#420, the signed per-relation criterion, so the adjustment can promote as well as demote and can tell treats from contraindication.
Start the criterion weights at zero, and early-stop on the criterion’s own loss, not the training loss.
Use λ as a score-time knob, running one fine-tune rather than one per λ.
Revisit the foundation’s generalization (MRR 0.021) before relying on its ranking: depth, and more epochs past the stall, or a composition change.
The larger levers already on the roadmap: population supervision and variant-aware edges.

(2026-10-05: the Q4 2026 plan, written 2026-10-01, reorders this list. A no-retrain test of the #523 shortcut, an evaluation rebuilt around non-learned baselines, and a retrain that drops each query edge’s mirror come first. That retrain, Arm A, became the checkpoint of record and failed gates S5 and S6 on 2026-10-04. #420 runs only if a conditioned baseline beats drug-mean on a cell-line proxy benchmark.)
Operational lessons are in §3’s table. The durable ones:

a fix to data doesn’t repair data already derived (#499);
a reloader that watches 177 GB can silently stop (#517);
cancels and stops need first-class paths (#515);
timed wakeups can silently not fire, so waits hang on completion signals.

Provenance
Every run id, image digest, manifest md5, release tag, schema hash and pickle sha is in the #439 provenance comment. The large local artifacts (panel matrices, pickles, fine-tune weights, train.txt) are under backend/data/pdr2_pickles/2026-09-28_smoke1/ and backend/data/prs_panel/, host-only and gitignored.

results/pdr2_rgcc_tier1_v2_writeup.title: PDR2 v2 Foundation — Tier-1 / Tier-2 Validation
results/pdr2_rgcc_tier1_v2_writeup.content:
PDR2 v2 Foundation — RGCC Tier-1 / Tier-2 Validation
Authors: whafa, Claude (Maple project)
Date: 2026-05-20
Status: CLOSED. End-to-end pipeline built, container rebuilt (gcr.io/PROJECT/maple-pdr2-training:3fe1dc8-score-edges, Cloud Build 5ac4f1e2), Vertex job 1913996564225851392 ran on A100 in 4 min (after ~5 min PENDING). Tier-1 ρ = +0.181 (n=107, p=0.062 — marginal); Tier-2 AUROC = 0.835 (PASS). ⚠#324 — both computed on pooled RGCC draws; unrestated. ⚠ 2026-09-27: and on memorized labels. See the second correction below. Tier-2 beats every PDR1 Run-B/A1/v1 baseline; Tier-1 is about half of PDR1 Run B’s +0.351 — see §4.
Companion documents:

docs/pdr_phase7_5_rgcc_writeup.md — PDR1 Phase 7.5 (the validation framework + baseline numbers we’re comparing against).
docs/pdr2_track_a_v2_repro_writeup.md — the foundation run that produced the checkpoint being validated. §6 (open questions) explicitly tracked this Tier-1 validation as the missing piece.
Memory: the patient-specific validation writeup.



⚠ Correction, 2026-09-24 (GH #317). Every
Tier-1 / Tier-2 number below was computed on RGCC labels averaged across Maureen’s two
draws (2025-02-15, 2025-09-19). The draws are not replicates: 12 drugs move ≥25 points and
they move as two coherent classes — four taxanes down, eight anthracycline / topoisomerase-II
agents up — a shift RGCC states in its own page-1 summaries. Averaging sends both classes to
mid-range. Test-retest is ρ = +0.9616 over all 112 drugs, ρ = +0.7635 over the 59 graded ones.
compute_metrics_crc.py now evaluates per timepoint and refuses to pool; these results
need restating against it. The 112-drug / 109-matched panel figures below are correct and
unchanged.


⚠ Correction, 2026-09-27 (GH #214,
#439). These numbers measure memorization, not
generalization. The split flags in §4 were computed per exact triple. So a drug counted as
held out whenever its sensitive_to_drug edge was absent, even when the same drug had a
partially_sensitive_to_drug or resistant_to_drug edge in train, or was trained under a
sibling identifier (oxaliplatin exists both as CHEBI:31941 and as a PharmGKB duplicate).
